title.raw: 卷114 釋老志十 Volume 114: Treatise 10 - Buddhism and Daoism

sentences.zh: 大人有作，司牧生民，結繩以往，書契所絕，故靡得而知焉。

translations.literal: When great men arose and governed the people, from the age of knotted cords onward through what written contracts ended, thus none could know.
translations.idiomatic: When the great sages took office to shepherd the people, from the age of knotted cords through the period ended by written records, nothing can be known with certainty.

sentences.zh: 自羲軒已還，至於三代，其神言秘策，蘊圖緯之文，範世率民，垂墳典之迹。

translations.literal: From Fu Xi and the Yellow Emperor down to the Three Dynasties, their divine words and secret policies contained chart-and-weft texts, modeled the age and led the people, and left traces in the canonical tomes.
translations.idiomatic: From Fuxi and the Yellow Emperor down through the Three Dynasties, sacred utterances and hidden policies preserved the lore of charts and apocrypha, set norms for the world and guided the people, and bequeathed the record of the canonical classics.

sentences.zh: 秦肆其毒，滅於灰燼；

translations.literal: Qin displayed its cruelty and was extinguished in ashes;
translations.idiomatic: Qin unleashed its cruelty and perished in ashes;

sentences.zh: 漢採遺籍，復若丘山。

translations.literal: Han gathered the surviving records, restoring them like mountains.
translations.idiomatic: Han collected the surviving books and restored them in heaps as vast as hills.

sentences.zh: 司馬遷區別異同，有陰陽、儒、墨、名、法、道德六家之義。

translations.literal: Sima Qian distinguished similarities and differences, treating the doctrines of the six schools—Yin-Yang, Confucian, Mohist, Logician, Legalist, and Daoist.
translations.idiomatic: Sima Qian distinguished the various schools and recorded the doctrines of the six traditions: Yin-Yang, Confucian, Mohist, Logician, Legalist, and Daoist.

sentences.zh: 劉歆著七略，班固志藝文，釋氏之學，所未曾紀。

translations.literal: Liu Xin compiled the Seven Summaries, and Ban Gu recorded the arts and literature, but the learning of the Shakya clan was never chronicled.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Xin wrote the Seven Summaries and Ban Gu catalogued literature in the Treatise on Arts and Letters, yet neither recorded the teachings of Buddhism.

sentences.zh: 案漢武元狩中，遣霍去病討匈奴，至臯蘭，過居延，斬首大獲。

translations.literal: It is recorded that in the Yuanshuo era of Emperor Wu of Han, Huo Qubing was sent to campaign against the Xiongnu, reaching Gaolan and passing Juyan, where he took many heads in a great victory.
translations.idiomatic: According to the records, during the Yuanshuo reign of Emperor Wu of Han, Huo Qubing was dispatched against the Xiongnu, advanced to Gaolan, passed through Juyan, and won a great victory with many enemy heads taken.

sentences.zh: 昆邪王殺休屠王，將其眾五萬來降。

translations.literal: The King of Hunye killed the King of Xiutu and brought his fifty thousand followers to surrender.
translations.idiomatic: The King of Hunye killed the King of Xiutu and came to surrender with a following of fifty thousand.

sentences.zh: 獲其金人，帝以為大神，列於甘泉宮。

translations.literal: They captured his golden image; the emperor took it for a great deity and installed it in Ganquan Palace.
translations.idiomatic: They seized a golden statue, which the emperor regarded as a great god and set up in Ganquan Palace.

sentences.zh: 金人率長丈餘，不祭祀，但燒香禮拜而已。

translations.literal: The golden image was generally more than a zhang in height; no sacrificial offerings were made—only incense was burned and obeisance performed.
translations.idiomatic: The golden statue stood over a zhang tall; no animal sacrifices were offered—only incense was burned and worship performed.

sentences.zh: 此則佛道流通之漸也。

translations.literal: This was the beginning of the gradual spread of the Buddhist Way.
translations.idiomatic: This marks the earliest stage in the spread of Buddhism.

sentences.zh: 浮屠正號曰佛陀，佛陀與浮圖聲相近，皆西方言，其來轉為二音。

translations.literal: The proper name of Futuo is Foto; Foto and Futu sound alike—both are Western words that in transmission became two pronunciations.
translations.idiomatic: The correct term for Futuo is Buddha; Buddha and Futu sound similar—both are Western words that came to be rendered in two forms.

sentences.zh: 華言譯之則謂淨覺，言滅穢成明，道為聖悟。

translations.literal: Rendered in Chinese it means Pure Awakening, signifying the extinction of defilement and attainment of clarity, the Way as sacred enlightenment.
translations.idiomatic: In Chinese it is rendered as Pure Awakening, meaning the elimination of impurity and attainment of illumination—the Way as supreme enlightenment.

sentences.zh: 凡其經旨，大抵言生生之類，皆因行業而起。

translations.literal: In general its sutra teachings say that all classes of living beings arise because of karma.
translations.idiomatic: The gist of its scriptures is that all living beings arise from their deeds and accumulated karma.

sentences.zh: 有過去、當今、未來，歷三世，識神常不滅。

translations.literal: There are past, present, and future, passing through three ages; the conscious spirit is never extinguished.
translations.idiomatic: There are past, present, and future—the three ages—and the conscious spirit is never destroyed.

sentences.zh: 凡為善惡，必有報應。

translations.literal: Whatever good or evil one does, there must be retribution.
translations.idiomatic: Every good or evil act inevitably receives its due recompense.

sentences.zh: 漸積勝業，陶冶粗鄙，經無數形，澡練神明，[3]乃致無生而得佛道。

translations.literal: By gradually accumulating superior karma, refining the coarse and vulgar, passing through countless forms, cleansing and tempering the spirit, one finally reaches non-birth and attains the Buddha Way.
translations.idiomatic: By gradually accumulating meritorious deeds, refining what is crude, passing through countless rebirths, and purifying the spirit, one ultimately reaches the state of non-birth and attains Buddhahood.

sentences.zh: 其間階次心行，等級非一，皆緣淺以至深，藉微而為著。

translations.literal: The stages of mind and conduct in between are not of one rank; all proceed from shallow to deep, from slight to manifest.
translations.idiomatic: The stages of spiritual cultivation are many and varied, all advancing from the shallow to the profound and from the subtle to the manifest.

sentences.zh: 率在於積仁順，蠲嗜慾，習虛靜而成通照也。

translations.literal: In general it lies in accumulating benevolence and compliance, dispelling cravings and desires, and practicing emptiness and stillness to achieve penetrating illumination.
translations.idiomatic: In essence it consists in accumulating benevolence and compliance, relinquishing cravings and desires, and cultivating emptiness and stillness until one achieves penetrating illumination.

sentences.zh: 故其始修心則依佛、法、僧，謂之三歸，若君子之三畏也。

translations.literal: Therefore at the beginning of cultivating the mind one relies on Buddha, Dharma, and Sangha—called the Three Refuges—like the three things a gentleman holds in awe.
translations.idiomatic: At the outset of spiritual cultivation one takes refuge in the Buddha, the Dharma, and the Sangha—the Three Refuges—analogous to the three things a gentleman holds in awe.

sentences.zh: 又有五戒，去殺、盜、淫、妄言、飲酒，大意與仁、義、禮、智、信同，名為異耳。

translations.literal: There are also the Five Precepts: abstaining from killing, stealing, sexual misconduct, false speech, and drinking alcohol—their general meaning is the same as benevolence, righteousness, propriety, wisdom, and trustworthiness, differing only in name.
translations.idiomatic: There are also the Five Precepts—against killing, stealing, sexual misconduct, lying, and drinking alcohol—which correspond in spirit to benevolence, righteousness, propriety, wisdom, and trustworthiness, differing only in terminology.

sentences.zh: 云奉持之，則生天人勝處，虧犯則墜鬼畜諸苦。

translations.literal: It is said that if one upholds them, one is reborn in the superior realms of devas and humans; if one violates them, one falls into the sufferings of ghosts and beasts.
translations.idiomatic: Those who uphold them are reborn in the superior realms of gods and humans; those who violate them fall into the sufferings of ghosts and animals.

sentences.zh: 又善惡生處，凡有六道焉。

translations.literal: Moreover, the places of birth according to good and evil comprise six paths in all.
translations.idiomatic: The realms into which one is born according to one's deeds comprise six paths in all.

sentences.zh: 諸服其道者，則剃落鬚髮，釋累辭家，結師資，遵律度，相與和居，治心修淨，行乞以自給。

translations.literal: Those who follow its Way shave off their hair and beard, cast off burdens and leave home, form master-disciple bonds, observe the rules, dwell together in harmony, cultivate purity of mind, and support themselves by begging.
translations.idiomatic: Those who follow the Way shave their heads, leave home and family, take teachers, observe the precepts, live together in harmony, cultivate purity of mind, and support themselves by begging for alms.

sentences.zh: 謂之沙門，或曰桑門，亦聲相近，總謂之僧，皆胡言也。

translations.literal: They are called shamen, or sangmen—the sounds are also close—and collectively they are called seng; all are barbarian words.
translations.idiomatic: They are called shramanas, or sangmen—the sounds are similar—and collectively they are called monks; all these terms are foreign words.

sentences.zh: 僧，譯為和命眾，桑門為息心，比丘為行乞。

translations.literal: Seng is rendered as the harmonious assembly; sangmen means stilling the mind; biqiu means going forth to beg.
translations.idiomatic: Seng is rendered as the harmonious assembly; shramana means stilling the mind; bhikshu means mendicant.

sentences.zh: 俗人之信憑道法者，男曰優婆塞，女曰優婆夷。

translations.literal: Lay people who believe in and rely on the Dharma are called upasaka for men and upasika for women.
translations.idiomatic: Lay followers of the teaching are called upasaka for men and upasika for women.

sentences.zh: 其為沙門者，初修十誡，曰沙彌，而終於二百五十，則具足成大僧。

translations.literal: Those who become shramanas first observe the ten precepts and are called shamini; when they complete the two hundred fifty, they are fully ordained as great monks.
translations.idiomatic: Those who enter the monastic life first observe the ten precepts as novices; when they complete the two hundred fifty precepts, they are fully ordained as senior monks.

sentences.zh: 婦入道者曰比丘尼。

translations.literal: Women who enter the Way are called bhikshunis.
translations.idiomatic: Women who take monastic vows are called bhikshunis.

sentences.zh: [4]其誡至于五百，皆以□為本，[5]隨事增數，在於防心、攝身、正口。

translations.literal: Their precepts reach five hundred, all taking [the root precept] as foundation; numbers are added according to circumstances, aimed at guarding the mind, restraining the body, and rectifying speech.
translations.idiomatic: Their precepts number as many as five hundred, all founded on the root precept; additional rules are added as circumstances require, aimed at guarding the mind, restraining the body, and rectifying speech.

sentences.zh: 心去貪、忿、癡，身除殺、淫、盜，口斷妄、雜、諸非正言，總謂之十善道。

translations.literal: The mind abandons greed, anger, and delusion; the body removes killing, sexual misconduct, and stealing; the mouth cuts off falsehood, idle talk, and all improper speech—collectively called the Ten Good Paths.
translations.idiomatic: The mind abandons greed, hatred, and delusion; the body refrains from killing, sexual misconduct, and stealing; the mouth ceases lying, frivolous talk, and all improper speech—together called the Ten Good Paths.

sentences.zh: 能具此，謂之三業清淨。

translations.literal: One who can fully possess these is said to have the three karmas purified.
translations.idiomatic: Those who fully observe these are said to have purified the three modes of conduct.

sentences.zh: 凡人修行粗為極。

translations.literal: For ordinary people, practicing these is roughly the ultimate.
translations.idiomatic: For ordinary people, this practice represents the highest attainable standard.

sentences.zh: [6]云可以達惡善報，漸階聖迹。

translations.literal: It is said that through these one can comprehend retribution for evil and good and gradually ascend the traces of sainthood.
translations.idiomatic: Through these one can understand the recompense of good and evil and gradually ascend toward sainthood.

sentences.zh: 初階聖者，有三種人，其根業各差，[7]謂之三乘，聲聞乘、緣覺乘、大乘。

translations.literal: Those who first enter the ranks of sainthood comprise three kinds of people, their root-karma each differing—called the Three Vehicles: the Shravaka Vehicle, the Pratyekabuddha Vehicle, and the Mahayana.
translations.idiomatic: Those who first attain sainthood fall into three categories, each with different spiritual capacities—the Three Vehicles: the Shravaka Vehicle, the Pratyekabuddha Vehicle, and the Great Vehicle.

sentences.zh: 取其可乘運以至道為名。

translations.literal: They take as their name that which can be ridden to convey one to the Way.
translations.idiomatic: They are so named because each serves as a vehicle by which one may reach the Way.

sentences.zh: 此三人惡迹已盡，但修心盪累，濟物進德。

translations.literal: These three kinds of people have exhausted evil traces; they only cultivate the mind to sweep away burdens, aid beings, and advance in virtue.
translations.idiomatic: These three have exhausted the traces of evil; they cultivate the mind to shed defilements, aid living beings, and advance in virtue.

sentences.zh: 初根人為小乘，行四諦法；

translations.literal: Those of inferior capacity belong to the Small Vehicle and practice the Four Noble Truths;
translations.idiomatic: Those of inferior spiritual capacity follow the Small Vehicle and practice the Four Noble Truths;

sentences.zh: 中根人為中乘，受十二因緣；

translations.literal: those of middling capacity belong to the Middle Vehicle and receive the Twelve Links of Dependent Origination;
translations.idiomatic: those of middling capacity follow the Middle Vehicle and accept the Twelve Links of Dependent Origination;

sentences.zh: 上根人為大乘，則修六度。

translations.literal: those of superior capacity belong to the Great Vehicle and cultivate the Six Perfections.
translations.idiomatic: those of superior capacity follow the Great Vehicle and cultivate the Six Perfections.

sentences.zh: 雖階三乘，而要由修進萬行，拯度億流，彌歷長遠，[8]乃可登佛境矣。

translations.literal: Although there are three vehicles, one must still cultivate and advance through myriad practices, save and ferry hundreds of millions of beings, pass through vast ages, and only then can one ascend to the Buddha realm.
translations.idiomatic: Although there are three vehicles, one must still cultivate countless practices, save innumerable beings, and pass through vast ages before one can reach the Buddha realm.

sentences.zh: 所謂佛者，本號釋迦文者，譯言能仁，謂德充道備，堪濟萬物也。

translations.literal: What is called Buddha originally bore the name Shijiamo; rendered in Chinese it means Able to Be Benevolent, signifying virtue fulfilled and the Way complete, fit to save the myriad things.
translations.idiomatic: The Buddha was originally called Shakyamuni, rendered in Chinese as Able to Be Benevolent—meaning his virtue was complete and his Way perfected, fit to save all beings.

sentences.zh: 釋迦前有六佛，釋迦繼六佛而成道，處今賢劫。

translations.literal: Before Shakyamuni there were six Buddhas; Shakyamuni succeeded the six Buddhas in attaining enlightenment, dwelling in the present Fortunate Kalpa.
translations.idiomatic: Six Buddhas preceded Shakyamuni; Shakyamuni attained enlightenment after them, in the present Fortunate Kalpa.

sentences.zh: 文言將來有彌勒佛，[9]方繼釋迦而降世。

translations.literal: The texts say that in the future there will be the Buddha Maitreya, who will succeed Shakyamuni in descending to the world.
translations.idiomatic: The scriptures say that in the future the Buddha Maitreya will succeed Shakyamuni in descending to the world.

sentences.zh: 釋迦即天竺迦維衞國王之子。

translations.literal: Shakyamuni was the son of the king of Kapilavastu in India.
translations.idiomatic: Shakyamuni was the son of the king of Kapilavastu in India.

sentences.zh: 天竺其總稱，迦維別名也。

translations.literal: India is the general name; Kapila is a particular designation.
translations.idiomatic: India is the general term; Kapilavastu is a specific place name.

sentences.zh: 初，釋迦於四月八日夜，從母右脅而生。

translations.literal: At first, on the night of the eighth day of the fourth month, Shakyamuni was born from his mother's right side.
translations.idiomatic: Shakyamuni was born on the night of the eighth day of the fourth month, emerging from his mother's right side.

sentences.zh: 既生，姿相超異者三十二種。

translations.literal: Once born, his bodily marks of surpassing distinction numbered thirty-two kinds.
translations.idiomatic: At birth he displayed thirty-two extraordinary physical marks.

sentences.zh: 天降嘉瑞以應之，亦三十二。

translations.literal: Heaven sent auspicious omens in response, also numbering thirty-two.
translations.idiomatic: Heaven sent thirty-two auspicious omens in response.

sentences.zh: 其本起經說之備矣。

translations.literal: The Sutra of His Original Vows records these in full.
translations.idiomatic: The Sutra of His Original Vows records all of this in full.

sentences.zh: 釋迦生時，當周莊王九年。

translations.literal: When Shakyamuni was born, it was the ninth year of King Zhuang of Zhou.
translations.idiomatic: Shakyamuni was born in the ninth year of King Zhuang of Zhou.

sentences.zh: 春秋魯莊公七年夏四月，恒星不見，夜明，是也。

translations.literal: In the Spring and Autumn Annals, in the seventh year of Duke Zhuang of Lu, summer, fourth month, the fixed stars were not seen and the night was bright—this was that event.
translations.idiomatic: The Spring and Autumn Annals records that in the seventh year of Duke Zhuang of Lu, in the fourth month of summer, the fixed stars were not visible and the night was bright—this was that event.

sentences.zh: 至魏武定八年，凡一千二百三十七年云。

translations.literal: Down to the eighth year of Wuding of Wei, it is altogether one thousand two hundred thirty-seven years, it is said.
translations.idiomatic: By the eighth year of Wuding of Wei, one thousand two hundred thirty-seven years had elapsed, it is said.

sentences.zh: 釋迦年三十成佛，導化羣生，四十九載，乃於拘尸那城娑羅雙樹間，以二月十五日而入般湼槃。

translations.literal: At thirty Shakyamuni attained Buddhahood and guided and transformed all beings; after forty-nine years, on the fifteenth day of the second month, between the twin sala trees at Kusinagara, he entered parinirvana.
translations.idiomatic: At the age of thirty Shakyamuni attained Buddhahood and taught all beings; after forty-nine years, on the fifteenth day of the second month, between the twin sala trees at Kusinagara, he entered parinirvana.

sentences.zh: 湼槃譯云滅度，或言常樂我淨，明無遷謝及諸苦累也。

translations.literal: Nirvana is rendered as extinction and passing; alternatively it is called permanence, bliss, self, and purity, clarifying that there is no transmigration or accumulation of suffering.
translations.idiomatic: Nirvana is rendered as extinction and passing; it is also called permanence, bliss, self, and purity, signifying freedom from transmigration and all suffering.

sentences.zh: 諸佛法身有二種義，一者真實，二者權應。

translations.literal: The dharma-bodies of all Buddhas have two meanings: one true and real, the other expedient and responsive.
translations.idiomatic: The dharma-bodies of all Buddhas have two aspects: the true body and the responsive body.

sentences.zh: 真實身，謂至極之體，妙絕拘累，不得以方處期，不可以形量限，有感斯應，體常湛然。

translations.literal: The true body is the ultimate substance, wondrously transcending all bonds; it cannot be awaited in place or time, nor limited by form or measure; where there is sensation it responds, its substance ever serene.
translations.idiomatic: The true body is the ultimate substance, transcending all bonds; it cannot be located in space or time or measured by form; it responds wherever there is need, its essence ever serene.

sentences.zh: 權應身者，謂和光六道，同塵萬類，生滅隨時，修短應物，形由感生，體非實有。

translations.literal: The responsive body blends its light with the six paths, shares dust with the myriad kinds, birth and death following the seasons, length of life responding to things; form arises from sensation, the substance is not truly existent.
translations.idiomatic: The responsive body mingles its radiance with the six paths, shares the dust of the world with all beings, is born and dies according to the times, and lives long or short as circumstances require; its form arises from the needs of beings and is not ultimately real.

sentences.zh: 權形雖謝，真體不遷，但時無妙感，故莫得常見耳。

translations.literal: Although the expedient form may pass away, the true substance does not shift; only when the times lack wondrous sensation can one not constantly see it.
translations.idiomatic: Although the responsive form may pass away, the true body does not change; it is only because the times lack the proper receptivity that one cannot see it constantly.

sentences.zh: 明佛生非實生，滅非實滅也。

translations.literal: This clarifies that the Buddha's birth is not true birth and his extinction is not true extinction.
translations.idiomatic: This shows that the Buddha's birth is not a real birth and his passing is not a real passing.

sentences.zh: 佛既謝世，香木焚尸。

translations.literal: After the Buddha had passed from the world, fragrant wood was used to cremate the body.
translations.idiomatic: After the Buddha passed from the world, his body was cremated with fragrant wood.

sentences.zh: 靈骨分碎，大小如粒，擊之不壞，焚亦不燋，或有光明神驗，胡言謂之「舍利」。

translations.literal: The sacred bones broke into fragments the size of grains; struck they did not break, burned they did not char; some had luminous divine manifestations—in barbarian speech they are called relics.
translations.idiomatic: The sacred bones broke into fragments the size of grains; they could not be broken by striking nor consumed by fire; some displayed luminous signs—in foreign speech they are called relics.

sentences.zh: 弟子收奉，置之寶瓶，竭香花，致敬慕，建宮宇，謂為「塔」。

translations.literal: Disciples collected and enshrined them, placing them in jeweled vessels, offering incense and flowers in reverence and admiration, and building palaces called stupas.
translations.idiomatic: Disciples collected and enshrined them in jeweled vessels, offered incense and flowers in reverence, and built shrines called stupas.

sentences.zh: 塔亦胡言，猶宗廟也，故世稱塔廟。

translations.literal: Stupa is also a barbarian word, like an ancestral temple; hence the world calls them stupa-temples.
translations.idiomatic: Stupa is also a foreign word, equivalent to an ancestral temple; hence they are called stupa-temples.

sentences.zh: 於後百年，有王阿育，以神力分佛舍利，役諸鬼神，[10]造八萬四千塔，布於世界，皆同日而就。

translations.literal: A hundred years later there was King Ashoka, who by divine power divided the Buddha's relics, employed spirits and demons, and built eighty-four thousand stupas spread across the world, all completed on the same day.
translations.idiomatic: A century later King Ashoka used his supernatural powers to divide the Buddha's relics, employed spirits to build eighty-four thousand stupas throughout the world, all completed on the same day.

sentences.zh: 今洛陽、彭城、姑臧、臨淄皆有阿育王寺，[11]蓋承其遺迹焉。

translations.literal: Today Luoyang, Pengcheng, Guzang, and Linzi all have Ashoka temples, presumably inheriting traces of this.
translations.idiomatic: Today Luoyang, Pengcheng, Guzang, and Linzi all have Ashoka temples, presumably preserving traces of this tradition.

sentences.zh: 釋迦雖般湼槃，而留影迹爪齒於天竺，於今猶在。

translations.literal: Although Shakyamuni entered parinirvana, he left traces of his shadow, footprints, fingernails, and teeth in India, which remain to this day.
translations.idiomatic: Although Shakyamuni entered parinirvana, he left traces of his shadow, footprints, fingernails, and teeth in India, which remain to this day.

sentences.zh: 中土來往，並稱見之。

translations.literal: Those who traveled to and from the Central Lands all claimed to have seen them.
translations.idiomatic: Travelers to and from China all claimed to have seen them.

sentences.zh: 初，釋迦所說教法，既湼槃後，有聲聞弟子大迦葉、阿難等五百人，撰集著錄。

translations.literal: At first, the teaching that Shakyamuni preached—after his parinirvana, five hundred shravaka disciples including Mahakashyapa and Ananda compiled and recorded it.
translations.idiomatic: After Shakyamuni's parinirvana, five hundred shravaka disciples including Mahakashyapa and Ananda compiled and recorded the teachings he had preached.

sentences.zh: 阿難親承囑授，多聞總持，蓋能綜覈深致，無所漏失。

translations.literal: Ananda personally received the entrusted transmission; broadly learned and holding all in memory, he was able to synthesize profound meanings without omission.
translations.idiomatic: Ananda had personally received the Buddha's transmission; learned in all teachings and holding them in memory, he was able to synthesize their profound meaning without omission.

sentences.zh: 乃綴文字，撰載三藏十二部經，如九流之異統，其大歸終以三乘為本。

translations.literal: He then joined characters together and compiled the scriptures of the Three Baskets in twelve divisions, like the separate traditions of the nine schools; their general import ultimately takes the Three Vehicles as foundation.
translations.idiomatic: He then set down the scriptures of the Three Baskets in twelve divisions, like the separate traditions of the nine philosophical schools; their ultimate purpose rests on the Three Vehicles.

sentences.zh: 後數百年，有羅漢、菩薩相繼著論，贊明經義，以破外道，摩訶衍，大、小阿毗曇，中論，十二門論，百法論，成實論等是也。

translations.literal: Several centuries later, arhats and bodhisattvas successively wrote treatises praising and clarifying the sutra meanings to refute non-Buddhist paths—the Mahayana, the Great and Small Abhidharma, the Middle Treatise, the Twelve Gates Treatise, the Hundred Dharmas Treatise, the Establishment of Truth Treatise, and others.
translations.idiomatic: Centuries later, arhats and bodhisattvas wrote treatises in succession to elucidate the scriptures and refute non-Buddhist doctrines—the Mahayana, the Great and Small Abhidharma, the Middle Treatise, the Twelve Gates Treatise, the Hundred Dharmas Treatise, the Establishment of Truth Treatise, and others.

sentences.zh: 皆傍諸藏部大義，假立外問，而以內法釋之。

translations.literal: All rely on the great meanings of the various basket divisions, fictively posing external questions and explaining them with the inner Dharma.
translations.idiomatic: All draw on the major doctrines of the scriptural collections, pose hypothetical objections, and answer them with Buddhist teaching.

sentences.zh: 漢章帝時，楚王英喜為浮屠齋戒，遣郎中令奉黃縑白紈三十匹，詣國相以贖愆。

translations.literal: In the time of Emperor Zhang of Han, Prince Ying of Chu delighted in Buddhist fasting and precepts, sending his Director of Gentlemen to present thirty bolts of yellow silk and white gauze to the Chancellor of State to redeem his fault.
translations.idiomatic: During the reign of Emperor Zhang of Han, Prince Ying of Chu observed Buddhist fasting and precepts and sent his chamberlain with thirty bolts of yellow silk and white gauze to the chancellor to atone for his offense.

sentences.zh: 詔報曰：「楚王尚浮屠之仁祠，潔齋三月，與神為誓，何嫌何疑，當有悔吝。

translations.literal: An edict in reply said: "The King of Chu esteems the benevolent rites of the Buddha, keeping pure fast for three months and making vows with the spirits—what suspicion or doubt could there be? There should be no regret.
translations.idiomatic: The imperial reply read: "The King of Chu honors the benevolent rites of Buddhism, has kept a pure fast for three months, and made vows before the spirits—what suspicion or doubt could there be? You should feel no regret.

sentences.zh: 其還贖，以助伊蒲塞、桑門之盛饌。」

translations.literal: Return the redemption and use it to assist the lavish meals of upasakas and shramanas."
translations.idiomatic: Return the offering and use it to provide lavish meals for lay followers and monks."

sentences.zh: 因以班示諸國。

translations.literal: Thereupon it was promulgated to all the states.
translations.idiomatic: The edict was then promulgated to all the kingdoms.

sentences.zh: 桓帝時，襄楷言佛陀、黃老道以諫，欲令好生惡殺，少嗜慾，去奢泰，尚無為。

translations.literal: In the time of Emperor Huan, Xiang Kai spoke of the Buddha and the Way of Huang-Lao in remonstrance, wishing to make people cherish life and abhor killing, reduce cravings and desires, abandon extravagance, and esteem non-action.
translations.idiomatic: During the reign of Emperor Huan, Xiang Kai cited the Buddha and the Way of Huang-Lao in a memorial, urging people to cherish life and abhor killing, reduce desires, abandon extravagance, and esteem non-action.

sentences.zh: 魏明帝曾欲壞宮西佛圖。

translations.literal: Emperor Ming of Wei once wished to destroy the Buddhist pagoda west of the palace.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Ming of Wei once wished to destroy the Buddhist pagoda west of the palace.

sentences.zh: 外國沙門乃金盤盛水，置於殿前，以佛舍利投之於水，乃有五色光起，於是帝歎曰：「自非靈異，安得爾乎？」

translations.literal: A foreign monk then placed water in a golden basin before the hall and cast Buddha relics into the water; five-colored light arose, whereupon the emperor sighed and said: "If this were not supernatural, how could it be so?"
translations.idiomatic: A foreign monk placed water in a golden basin before the hall and cast Buddha relics into it; five-colored light arose. The emperor exclaimed: "If this were not supernatural, how could it be so?"

sentences.zh: 遂徙於道東，[12]為作周閣百間。

translations.literal: He then moved it east of the road and built a hundred chambers in a surrounding gallery.
translations.idiomatic: He then moved it east of the road and built a hundred chambers in a surrounding gallery.

sentences.zh: 佛圖故處，鑿為濛氾池，種芙蓉於中。

translations.literal: The former site of the pagoda was excavated to make the Mengfan Pool, and lotuses were planted in it.
translations.idiomatic: The former site of the pagoda was excavated to create the Mengfan Pool, in which lotuses were planted.

sentences.zh: 後有天竺沙門曇柯迦羅入洛，宣譯誡律，中國誡律之始也。

translations.literal: Later the Indian monk Dharmakala entered Luoyang and proclaimed and translated the precepts and vinaya—the beginning of precepts and vinaya in China.
translations.idiomatic: Later the Indian monk Dharmakala came to Luoyang and translated the precepts and monastic rules—the beginning of vinaya in China.

sentences.zh: 自洛中構白馬寺，盛飾佛圖，畫迹甚妙，為四方式。

translations.literal: From the construction of White Horse Temple in Luoyang, Buddhist pagodas were richly adorned; painted traces were exceedingly fine and served as models for all four directions.
translations.idiomatic: From the construction of White Horse Temple in Luoyang, pagodas were richly adorned with paintings of exquisite quality that served as models throughout the land.

sentences.zh: 凡宮塔制度，猶依天竺舊狀而重構之，從一級至三、五、七、九。

translations.literal: In general the regulations for palace pagodas still followed the old forms of India in reconstruction, from one story to three, five, seven, or nine.
translations.idiomatic: Palace pagodas generally followed Indian models in their reconstruction, ranging from one story to three, five, seven, or nine.

sentences.zh: 世人相承，謂之「浮圖」，或云「佛圖」。

translations.literal: People handed down the name, calling them futu, or saying fotu.
translations.idiomatic: People handed down the name, calling them futu, or fotu.

sentences.zh: 晉世，洛中佛圖有四十二所矣。

translations.literal: In the Jin age, there were forty-two Buddhist pagodas in Luoyang.
translations.idiomatic: During the Jin dynasty, Luoyang had forty-two Buddhist pagodas.

sentences.zh: 漢世沙門，皆衣赤布，後乃易以雜色。

translations.literal: In Han times shramanas all wore red cloth; later they changed to variegated colors.
translations.idiomatic: In Han times monks all wore red cloth; later they adopted variegated colors.

sentences.zh: 晉元康中，有胡沙門支恭明譯佛經維摩、法華、三本起等。

translations.literal: In the Yuankang era of Jin, the barbarian monk Zhi Gongming translated Buddhist scriptures including the Vimalakirti, Lotus, and Three Baskets of Origins.
translations.idiomatic: During the Yuankang era of Jin, the foreign monk Zhi Gongming translated scriptures including the Vimalakirti Sutra, the Lotus Sutra, and the Sutra of the Buddha's Original Vows.

sentences.zh: 微言隱義，未之能究。

translations.literal: Subtle words and hidden meanings could not yet be thoroughly investigated.
translations.idiomatic: Their subtle words and hidden meanings could not yet be fully understood.

sentences.zh: 後有沙門常山衞道安性聰敏，日誦經萬餘言，研求幽旨。

translations.literal: Later there was the monk Shi Dao'an of Changshan, intelligent by nature, reciting more than ten thousand characters of scripture daily and investigating abstruse meanings.
translations.idiomatic: Later the monk Shi Dao'an of Changshan, a man of keen intelligence, recited more than ten thousand characters of scripture daily and probed their profound meaning.

sentences.zh: 慨無師匠，獨坐靜室十二年，覃思構精，神悟妙賾，以前所出經，多有舛駁，乃正其乖謬。

translations.literal: Lamenting that he had no teacher, he sat alone in a quiet chamber for twelve years, pondering deeply and constructing refinements, attaining spiritual comprehension of wondrous profundities; the scriptures previously produced had many errors, and he corrected their discrepancies.
translations.idiomatic: Lamenting that he had no teacher, he sat alone in meditation for twelve years until he attained spiritual insight; finding many errors in earlier translations, he corrected them.

sentences.zh: 石勒時，有天竺沙門浮圖澄，少於烏萇國就羅漢入道，劉曜時到襄國。

translations.literal: In the time of Shi Le there was the Indian monk Fotucheng, who in youth in the state of Wuchang followed an arhat in entering the Way; in the time of Liu Yao he arrived at Xiangguo.
translations.idiomatic: During the reign of Shi Le, the Indian monk Fotucheng, who in his youth in Wuchang had studied under an arhat, came to Xiangguo during the reign of Liu Yao.

sentences.zh: 後為石勒所宗信，號為大和尚，軍國規謨頗訪之，所言多驗。

translations.literal: Later he was honored and trusted by Shi Le, styled Great Monk; military and state plans were often referred to him, and what he said mostly proved true.
translations.idiomatic: Later Shi Le honored and trusted him, calling him the Great Monk; he was frequently consulted on military and state affairs, and his words usually proved true.

sentences.zh: 道安曾至鄴候澄，澄見而異之。

translations.literal: Dao'an once went to Ye to visit Fotucheng; Fotucheng saw him and regarded him as extraordinary.
translations.idiomatic: Dao'an once went to Ye to visit Fotucheng, who regarded him as extraordinary.

sentences.zh: 澄卒後，中國紛亂，道安乃率門徒，南遊新野。

translations.literal: After Fotucheng died, the Central Lands were in turmoil; Dao'an then led his disciples south to Xinye.
translations.idiomatic: After Fotucheng's death, with China in turmoil, Dao'an led his disciples south to Xinye.

sentences.zh: 欲令玄宗在所流布，分遣弟子，各趣諸方。

translations.literal: Wishing to have the profound teaching spread wherever he went, he dispatched disciples each to various regions.
translations.idiomatic: Wishing to spread the profound teaching wherever he went, he sent disciples in different directions.

sentences.zh: 法汰詣揚州，法和入蜀，道安與慧遠之襄陽。

translations.literal: Fatai went to Yangzhou, Fahe entered Shu, and Dao'an went with Huiyuan to Xiangyang.
translations.idiomatic: Fatai went to Yangzhou, Fahe to Shu, and Dao'an with Huiyuan to Xiangyang.

sentences.zh: 道安後入苻堅，堅素欽德問，既見，宗以師禮。

translations.literal: Dao'an later entered the service of Fu Jian, who had long admired his virtue and learning; once they met, Fu Jian honored him with the rites due a teacher.
translations.idiomatic: Dao'an later entered the service of Fu Jian, who had long admired him; upon meeting, Fu Jian honored him as a teacher.

sentences.zh: 時西域有胡沙門鳩摩羅什，思通法門，道安思與講釋，每勸堅致羅什。

translations.literal: At that time in the Western Regions there was the barbarian monk Kumarajiva, whose thought penetrated the gates of the Dharma; Dao'an wished to discuss and explain with him and repeatedly urged Fu Jian to summon Kumarajiva.
translations.idiomatic: At that time in the Western Regions there was the monk Kumarajiva, whose understanding of the Dharma was profound; Dao'an wished to study with him and repeatedly urged Fu Jian to summon Kumarajiva.

sentences.zh: 什亦承安令問，謂之東方聖人，或時遙拜致敬。

translations.literal: Kumarajiva also received Dao'an's messages through transmission, calling him the sage of the East, and sometimes paid obeisance from afar.
translations.idiomatic: Kumarajiva also received Dao'an's messages and called him the sage of the East, sometimes paying obeisance from afar.

sentences.zh: 道安卒後二十餘載而羅什至長安，恨不及安，以為深慨。

translations.literal: More than twenty years after Dao'an died Kumarajiva arrived at Chang'an; he regretted not reaching Dao'an in time and felt deep regret.
translations.idiomatic: More than twenty years after Dao'an's death Kumarajiva arrived at Chang'an; he deeply regretted not having met him.

sentences.zh: 道安所正經義，與羅什譯出，符會如一，初無乖舛。

translations.literal: The scriptural meanings that Dao'an corrected and Kumarajiva's translations accorded as one, with no discrepancy at the outset.
translations.idiomatic: The scriptural meanings Dao'an had corrected matched Kumarajiva's translations perfectly, without the slightest discrepancy.

sentences.zh: 於是法旨大著中原。

translations.literal: Thereupon the purport of the Dharma greatly flourished in the Central Plains.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon Buddhist teaching flourished greatly in the Central Plains.

sentences.zh: 魏先建國於玄朔，風俗淳一，無為以自守，與西域殊絕，莫能往來。

translations.literal: Wei first established its state in the far north; customs were pure and unified, maintaining itself through non-action, utterly cut off from the Western Regions, unable to interact.
translations.idiomatic: When Wei first established its state in the far north, its customs were pure and simple, its people maintaining themselves through non-action; cut off from the Western Regions, they could not interact with them.

sentences.zh: 故浮圖之教，未之得聞，或聞而未信也。

translations.literal: Thus the teaching of the Buddha had not been heard, or if heard was not believed.
translations.idiomatic: Thus the Buddhist teaching had not reached them, or if heard was not believed.

sentences.zh: 及神元與魏、晉通聘，文帝久在洛陽，[13]昭成又至襄國，乃備究南夏佛法之事。

translations.literal: When Emperor Shenyuan exchanged envoys with Wei and Jin, Emperor Wendi long resided in Luoyang, and Emperor Zhaocheng also came to Xiangguo—they came to know fully the affairs of Southern China's Buddhist Dharma.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Shenyuan exchanged envoys with Wei and Jin, Emperor Wendi had long resided in Luoyang and Emperor Zhaocheng had also been at Xiangguo—they came to know fully the Buddhist affairs of southern China.

sentences.zh: 太祖平中山，經略燕趙，所逕郡國佛寺，見諸沙門、道士，皆致精敬，禁軍旅無有所犯。

translations.literal: When the Taizu pacified Zhongshan and planned Yan and Zhao, at Buddhist temples in the commanderies and states he passed, seeing shramanas and Daoist priests, he showed them refined respect and forbade the army from any violation.
translations.idiomatic: When Taizu pacified Zhongshan and campaigned in Yan and Zhao, at every monastery in the regions he passed he showed refined respect to monks and Daoist priests and forbade his troops from violating them.

sentences.zh: 帝好黃老，頗覽佛經。

translations.literal: The emperor favored Huang-Lao and read Buddhist scriptures considerably.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor favored Huang-Lao teachings and read Buddhist scriptures extensively.

sentences.zh: 但天下初定，戎車屢動，庶事草創，未建圖宇，招延僧眾也。

translations.literal: But when the realm was first settled, military campaigns were frequent, all affairs were in initial creation, and he had not yet built temples or recruited monastic assemblies.
translations.idiomatic: But with the realm newly settled, military campaigns frequent, and all affairs still being established, he had not yet built temples or recruited monks.

sentences.zh: 然時時旁求。

translations.literal: Yet from time to time he sought them out on the side.
translations.idiomatic: Yet he sought them out from time to time.

sentences.zh: 先是，有沙門僧朗，與其徒隱于泰山之琨

translations.literal: Before this, there was the shramana Seng Lang, who with his followers hid on Mount Tai in the Kun
translations.idiomatic: Earlier there was the monk Seng Lang, who with his followers had hidden on Mount Tai in the Kun

sentences.zh: 〈𤣩而〉

translations.literal: 〈qiu er〉
translations.idiomatic: 〈qiu'er〉

sentences.zh: 谷。

translations.literal: valley.
translations.idiomatic: valley.

sentences.zh: 帝遣使致書，以繒、素、旃罽、銀鉢為禮。

translations.literal: The emperor sent envoys with letters, offering silk, gauze, felt, and silver bowls as gifts.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor sent envoys with letters, offering silk, gauze, felt, and silver bowls as gifts.

sentences.zh: 今猶號曰朗公谷焉。

translations.literal: It is still called Langong Valley today.
translations.idiomatic: The place is still called Langong Valley today.

sentences.zh: 天興元年，下詔曰：「夫佛法之興，其來遠矣。

translations.literal: In the first year of Tianxing, an edict said: "The rise of the Buddha Dharma has come from afar.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Tianxing, an edict declared: "The rise of the Buddhist teaching came from afar.

sentences.zh: 濟益之功，冥及存沒，神蹤遺軌，信可依憑。

translations.literal: Its power to aid extends in obscurity to the living and dead; divine traces and transmitted paths may truly be relied upon.
translations.idiomatic: Its power to benefit extends in secret to the living and the dead; its divine traces and transmitted paths may truly be relied upon.

sentences.zh: 其敕有司，於京城建飾容範，修整宮舍，[14]令信向之徒，有所居止。」

translations.literal: Let the relevant offices in the capital city construct adorned images, repair palace halls, so that those who believe may have places to dwell."
translations.idiomatic: Let the relevant offices in the capital construct adorned images and repair palace halls so that believers may have places to dwell."

sentences.zh: 是歲，始作五級佛圖、耆闍崛山及須彌山殿，加以繢飾。

translations.literal: That year they first built a five-story pagoda, Mount Qijueju, and a Sumeru hall, adding painted decoration.
translations.idiomatic: That year they first built a five-story pagoda, a Mount Qijueju hall, and a Sumeru hall, all richly decorated.

sentences.zh: 別構講堂、禪堂及沙門座，莫不嚴具焉。

translations.literal: Separately they constructed lecture halls, meditation halls, and seats for shramanas, all rigorously complete.
translations.idiomatic: They also constructed lecture halls, meditation halls, and seats for monks, all rigorously appointed.

sentences.zh: 太宗踐位，遵太祖之業，亦好黃老，又崇佛法，京邑四方，建立圖像，仍令沙門敷導民俗。

translations.literal: When Emperor Taizong ascended the throne, he followed the Taizu's enterprise, also favoring Huang-Lao and further honoring the Buddha Dharma; within the capital and in all directions they established images, and still ordered shramanas to instruct the people in custom.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Taizong ascended the throne, he followed the Taizu's policies, also favoring Huang-Lao and further honoring Buddhism; images were established throughout the capital and the realm, and monks were ordered to instruct the people.

sentences.zh: 初，皇始中，趙郡有沙門法果，誡行精至，開演法籍。

translations.literal: At first, in Huangshi, in Zhao commandery there was the shramana Faguo, whose discipline and conduct were refined and perfect, opening and expounding the Dharma texts.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Huangshi era, in Zhao commandery there was the monk Faguo, whose discipline and conduct were refined, and who expounded the Buddhist scriptures.

sentences.zh: 太祖聞其名，詔以禮徵赴京師。

translations.literal: The Taizu heard his name and ordered him summoned to the capital with ritual courtesy.
translations.idiomatic: Taizu heard of him and ordered him summoned to the capital with ceremonial honor.

sentences.zh: 後以為道人統，綰攝僧徒。

translations.literal: Later he was made Director of the Way, overseeing the monastic community.
translations.idiomatic: Later he was appointed Director of the Way, overseeing the monastic community.

sentences.zh: 每與帝言，多所愜允，供施甚厚。

translations.literal: Whenever he spoke with the emperor, much was agreeable and approved; offerings and support were very generous.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever he spoke with the emperor, his words were well received; the offerings made to him were very generous.

sentences.zh: 至太宗，彌加崇敬，永興中，前後授以輔國、宜城子、忠信侯、安成公之號，皆固辭。

translations.literal: Under Emperor Taizong respect was further increased; in the Yongxing era, before and after he was offered the titles Assistant State, Marquis of Yicheng, Marquis of Zhongxin, and Duke of Ancheng—all firmly declined.
translations.idiomatic: Under Emperor Taizong he was further honored; during the Yongxing era he was repeatedly offered the titles Assistant State, Marquis of Yicheng, Marquis of Zhongxin, and Duke of Ancheng—all of which he firmly declined.

sentences.zh: 帝常親幸其居，以門小狹，不容輿輦，更廣大之。

translations.literal: The emperor often personally visited his residence; because the gate was small and narrow and could not accommodate the imperial carriage, it was enlarged.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor often visited his residence personally; because the gate was too narrow for the imperial carriage, it was enlarged.

sentences.zh: 年八十餘，泰常中卒。

translations.literal: At over eighty years of age, he died in the Taichang era.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the Taichang era at over eighty years of age.

sentences.zh: 未殯，帝三臨其喪，追贈老壽將軍、趙胡靈公。

translations.literal: Before the encoffining, the emperor thrice attended his mourning and posthumously enfeoffed him as General of Longevity and Duke of Zhaohuling.
translations.idiomatic: Before the encoffining, the emperor thrice attended his funeral and posthumously enfeoffed him as General of Longevity and Duke of Zhaohuling.

sentences.zh: 初，法果每言，太祖明叡好道，即是當今如來，沙門宜應盡禮，遂常致拜。

translations.literal: At first Faguo often said that the Taizu, wise and clear and fond of the Way, was the present-day Tathagata, and shramanas ought to pay him full obeisance; he therefore constantly performed bows.
translations.idiomatic: Faguo had often said that Taizu, wise and devoted to the Way, was the present-day Tathagata and that monks ought to pay him full obeisance; he therefore constantly bowed to him.

sentences.zh: 謂人曰：「能鴻道者人主也，我非拜天子，乃是禮佛耳。」

translations.literal: He told people: "Those who can spread the Way are rulers; I am not bowing to the Son of Heaven but rather paying obeisance to the Buddha."
translations.idiomatic: He told people: "Those who can spread the Way are rulers; I am not bowing to the Son of Heaven but paying obeisance to the Buddha."

sentences.zh: 法果四十，始為沙門。

translations.literal: Faguo at forty first became a shramana.
translations.idiomatic: Faguo did not become a monk until the age of forty.

sentences.zh: 有子曰猛，詔令襲果所加爵。

translations.literal: He had a son named Meng; an edict ordered him to inherit the titles Faguo had been granted.
translations.idiomatic: He had a son named Meng, whom an edict ordered to inherit the titles Faguo had been granted.

sentences.zh: 帝後幸廣宗，有沙門曇證，年且百歲。

translations.literal: Later when the emperor visited Guangzong, there was the shramana Tan Zheng, nearly a hundred years old.
translations.idiomatic: Later, when the emperor visited Guangzong, there was the monk Tan Zheng, nearly a hundred years old.

sentences.zh: 邀見於路，奉致果物。

translations.literal: He met the emperor on the road and presented fruits as offerings.
translations.idiomatic: He met the emperor on the road and presented fruit as offerings.

sentences.zh: 帝敬其年老志力不衰，亦加以老壽將軍號。

translations.literal: The emperor respected his advanced age and undiminished will and strength, and also granted him the title General of Longevity.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor respected his advanced age and undiminished vigor and also granted him the title General of Longevity.

sentences.zh: 是時，鳩摩羅什為姚興所敬，於長安草堂寺集義學八百人，重譯經本。

translations.literal: At that time Kumarajiva was honored by Yao Xing; at Chang'an's Caotang Temple he gathered eight hundred scholars of the teaching and retranslated the scriptural texts.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Kumarajiva was honored by Yao Xing; at Chang'an's Caotang Temple he gathered eight hundred scholars and retranslated the scriptures.

sentences.zh: 羅什聰辯有淵思，達東西方言。

translations.literal: Kumarajiva was clever and eloquent with profound thought, penetrating the languages of East and West.
translations.idiomatic: Kumarajiva was clever and eloquent with profound insight, mastering the languages of East and West.

sentences.zh: 時沙門道肜、[15]僧略、道恒、道𧝼、僧肇、曇影等，與羅什共相提挈，發明幽致。

translations.literal: At that time the shramanas Daoyin, Senglüe, Daoheng, Daofu, Sengzhao, Tan Ying, and others, together with Kumarajiva mutually assisted one another in elucidating abstruse meanings.
translations.idiomatic: The monks Daoyin, Senglüe, Daoheng, Daofu, Sengzhao, Tan Ying, and others worked with Kumarajiva to elucidate abstruse doctrines.

sentences.zh: 諸深大經論十有餘部，更定章句，辭義通明，至今沙門共所祖習。

translations.literal: Of the profound great sutras and treatises there were more than ten; they further fixed chapter divisions, with diction and meaning clear and penetrating—down to the present shramanas jointly take them as models for study.
translations.idiomatic: They revised more than ten major sutras and treatises, clarifying chapter divisions and making the meaning transparent—translations that monks still study today.

sentences.zh: 道肜等皆識學洽通，僧肇尤為其最。

translations.literal: Daoyin and the others were all learned and thoroughly penetrating; Sengzhao was especially foremost among them.
translations.idiomatic: Daoyin and the others were all learned and accomplished; Sengzhao was especially outstanding.

sentences.zh: 羅什之撰譯，僧肇常執筆，定諸辭義，注維摩經，又著數論，皆有妙旨，學者宗之。

translations.literal: In Kumarajiva's translations Sengzhao often held the brush, fixing the various meanings of terms; he annotated the Vimalakirti Sutra and also wrote several treatises, all with subtle purport, and scholars honored him.
translations.idiomatic: In Kumarajiva's translations Sengzhao often held the brush and fixed the terminology; he annotated the Vimalakirti Sutra and wrote several treatises, all with subtle insight, and scholars honored him.

sentences.zh: 又沙門法顯，慨律藏不具，自長安遊天竺。

translations.literal: There was also the shramana Faxian, who lamented that the vinaya treasury was incomplete and traveled from Chang'an to India.
translations.idiomatic: There was also the monk Faxian, who lamented that the vinaya collection was incomplete and traveled from Chang'an to India.

sentences.zh: 歷三十餘國，隨有經律之處，學其書語，譯而寫之。

translations.literal: Passing through more than thirty states, wherever there were scriptures and vinaya he learned their scripts and languages, translated and copied them.
translations.idiomatic: Passing through more than thirty countries, wherever he found scriptures and vinaya he learned the local languages, translated them, and copied them.

sentences.zh: 十年，乃於南海師子國，隨商人汎舟東下。

translations.literal: After ten years, at the Lion Kingdom of the Southern Sea, he followed merchants in a boat sailing east.
translations.idiomatic: After ten years, at the Lion Kingdom in the Southern Sea, he boarded a merchant ship sailing east.

sentences.zh: 晝夜昏迷，將二百日。

translations.literal: Day and night in dim confusion, nearly two hundred days passed.
translations.idiomatic: For nearly two hundred days he drifted in dim confusion day and night.

sentences.zh: 乃至青州長廣郡不其勞山，南下乃出海焉。

translations.literal: He finally reached Mount Lao in Buqi, Changguang commandery of Qing province, and going south then put out to sea.
translations.idiomatic: He finally reached Mount Lao at Buqi in Changguang commandery of Qing province, then sailed south out to sea.

sentences.zh: 是歲，神瑞二年也。

translations.literal: That year was the second year of Shenrui.
translations.idiomatic: That year was the second year of Shenrui.

sentences.zh: 法顯所逕諸國，傳記之，今行於世。

translations.literal: Faxian recorded the various states he passed through in a biography, which circulates in the world today.
translations.idiomatic: Faxian recorded the countries he visited in a travel account that still circulates today.

sentences.zh: 其所得律，通譯未能盡正。

translations.literal: The vinaya he obtained could not be fully corrected in translation.
translations.idiomatic: The vinaya he obtained could not be fully corrected in translation.

sentences.zh: 至江南，更與天竺禪師跋陀羅辯定之，謂之僧祇律，大備于前，為今沙門所持受。

translations.literal: Reaching Jiangnan, he further joined with the Indian meditation master Buddhabhadra in determining it, called the Mahasanghika Vinaya, greatly complete compared with before, and what shramanas today receive and uphold.
translations.idiomatic: In Jiangnan he worked with the Indian meditation master Buddhabhadra to finalize it; called the Mahasanghika Vinaya, it was far more complete than earlier versions and is what monks follow today.

sentences.zh: 先是，有沙門法領，從揚州入西域，得華嚴經本。

translations.literal: Before this, there was the shramana Faling, who from Yangzhou entered the Western Regions and obtained the Avatamsaka Sutra text.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier the monk Faling had traveled from Yangzhou into the Western Regions and obtained the Avatamsaka Sutra.

sentences.zh: 定律後數年，跋陀羅共沙門法業重加譯撰，宣行於時。

translations.literal: Several years after the vinaya was established, Buddhabhadra together with the shramana Faye again added translation and compilation, promulgating it in the age.
translations.idiomatic: Several years after the vinaya was established, Buddhabhadra and the monk Faye revised and translated it again, promulgating it widely.

sentences.zh: 世祖初即位，亦遵太祖、太宗之業，每引高德沙門，與共談論。

translations.literal: When Emperor Shizu first ascended the throne, he also followed the enterprises of the Taizu and Taizong, often inviting eminent shramanas to discuss with him.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Shizu first ascended the throne, he followed the policies of Taizu and Taizong, often inviting eminent monks to discuss doctrine with him.

sentences.zh: 於四月八日，輿諸佛像，行於廣衢，帝親御門樓，臨觀散花，以致禮敬。

translations.literal: On the eighth day of the fourth month he had Buddhist images borne in procession along the broad streets; the emperor personally manned the gate tower, viewing from above and scattering flowers to show ritual respect.
translations.idiomatic: On the eighth day of the fourth month he had Buddhist images borne in procession along the broad streets; the emperor personally manned the gate tower, scattering flowers from above in ritual homage.

sentences.zh: 先是，沮渠蒙遜在涼州，亦好佛法。

translations.literal: Before this, Juqu Mengxun in Liangzhou also favored the Buddha Dharma.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, Juqu Mengxun in Liangzhou had also favored Buddhism.

sentences.zh: 有罽賓沙門曇摩讖，習諸經論。

translations.literal: There was the Gandharan shramana Dharmakṣema, who studied various sutras and treatises.
translations.idiomatic: There was the Gandharan monk Dharmakṣema, who studied various sutras and treatises.

sentences.zh: 於姑臧，與沙門智嵩等，譯湼槃諸經十餘部。

translations.literal: At Guzang, together with the shramana Zhisong and others, he translated more than ten Nirvana sutras and related texts.
translations.idiomatic: At Guzang, together with the monk Zhisong and others, he translated more than ten Nirvana sutras and related texts.

sentences.zh: 又曉術數、禁呪，歷言他國安危，多所中驗。

translations.literal: He was also skilled in numerology and prohibitory spells, repeatedly speaking of other states' safety and peril, mostly hitting the mark in verification.
translations.idiomatic: He was also skilled in numerology and spells, repeatedly predicting the safety or peril of other states, mostly with accuracy.

sentences.zh: 蒙遜每以國事諮之。

translations.literal: Mengxun often consulted him on state affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Mengxun often consulted him on affairs of state.

sentences.zh: 神䴥中，帝命蒙遜送讖詣京師，惜而不遣。

translations.literal: In the Shenyi era the emperor ordered Mengxun to send Dharmakṣema to the capital; regretting it, he did not send him.
translations.idiomatic: In the Shenyi era the emperor ordered Mengxun to send Dharmakṣema to the capital, but Mengxun, regretting the loss, did not send him.

sentences.zh: 既而，懼魏威責，遂使人殺讖。

translations.literal: Later, fearing Wei might hold him accountable, he had someone kill Dharmakṣema.
translations.idiomatic: Later, fearing that Wei would hold him accountable, he had Dharmakṣema killed.

sentences.zh: 讖死之日，謂門徒曰：「今時將有客來，可早食以待之。」

translations.literal: On the day Dharmakṣema died, he told his disciples: "There will soon be a guest coming; you should eat early and wait for him."
translations.idiomatic: On the day of his death, Dharmakṣema told his disciples: "A guest will soon arrive; eat early and wait for him."

sentences.zh: 食訖而走使至。

translations.literal: When they had finished eating, the messenger arrived.
translations.idiomatic: When they had finished eating, the messenger arrived.

sentences.zh: 時人謂之知命。

translations.literal: People of the time called this knowing fate.
translations.idiomatic: People of the time called this foreknowledge of fate.

sentences.zh: 智嵩亦爽悟，篤志經籍。

translations.literal: Zhisong was also quick-witted and devoted in aspiration to the scriptures.
translations.idiomatic: Zhisong was also quick-witted and devoted to the scriptures.

sentences.zh: 後乃以新出經論，於涼土教授。

translations.literal: Later he used newly produced sutras and treatises to instruct in the Liang region.
translations.idiomatic: Later he taught the newly translated sutras and treatises in the Liang region.

sentences.zh: 辯論幽旨，著湼槃義記。

translations.literal: Debating abstruse meanings, he wrote a Commentary on the Meaning of the Nirvana.
translations.idiomatic: Debating abstruse doctrines, he wrote a Commentary on the Meaning of the Nirvana Sutra.

sentences.zh: 戒行峻整，門人齊肅。

translations.literal: His discipline and conduct were stern and ordered; his disciples were uniformly reverent.
translations.idiomatic: His discipline was stern and his disciples uniformly reverent.

sentences.zh: 知涼州將有兵役，與門徒數人，欲往胡地。

translations.literal: Knowing that Liangzhou would soon have military service, with several disciples he wished to go to the barbarian lands.
translations.idiomatic: Knowing that Liangzhou would soon see military action, he set out with several disciples for the barbarian lands.

sentences.zh: 道路飢饉，絕糧積日，弟子求得禽獸肉，請嵩強食。

translations.literal: On the road famine prevailed; for many days they had no grain; disciples obtained beast and bird meat and asked Zhisong to eat it by force.
translations.idiomatic: On the road famine prevailed; after many days without grain, disciples obtained meat and urged Zhisong to eat it.

sentences.zh: 嵩以戒自誓，遂餓死於酒泉之西山。

translations.literal: Zhisong swore by the precepts and starved to death on the western mountain of Jiuquan.
translations.idiomatic: Zhisong, bound by his vows, starved to death on the western mountain of Jiuquan.

sentences.zh: 弟子積薪焚其屍，骸骨灰燼，唯舌獨全，色狀不變。

translations.literal: Disciples heaped firewood and burned his corpse; of bones and ash only the tongue remained whole, its color and form unchanged.
translations.idiomatic: His disciples burned his body; of bones and ash only the tongue remained whole, its color unchanged.

sentences.zh: 時人以為誦說功報。

translations.literal: People of the time regarded this as the reward of recitation and preaching merit.
translations.idiomatic: People regarded this as the reward of his preaching merit.

sentences.zh: 涼州自張軌後，世信佛教。

translations.literal: From Zhang Gui onward Liangzhou for generations believed in Buddhism.
translations.idiomatic: From Zhang Gui onward the people of Liangzhou had believed in Buddhism for generations.

sentences.zh: 敦煌地接西域，道俗交得其舊式，村塢相屬，多有塔寺。

translations.literal: Dunhuang borders the Western Regions; clergy and laity alike obtained its old forms; villages and hamlets adjoined one another, many with pagodas and temples.
translations.idiomatic: Dunhuang bordered the Western Regions; clergy and laity alike followed its old customs; villages adjoined one another, many with pagodas and temples.

sentences.zh: 太延中，涼州平，徙其國人於京邑，沙門佛事皆俱東，象教彌增矣。

translations.literal: In the Taiyan era Liangzhou was pacified and its people moved to the capital; Buddhist affairs of shramanas all went east together, and the elephant teaching further increased.
translations.idiomatic: In the Taiyan era Liangzhou was pacified and its people moved to the capital; monks and Buddhist institutions all went east together, and Buddhism flourished further.

sentences.zh: 尋以沙門眾多，詔罷年五十已下者。

translations.literal: Soon because the shramana community was too numerous, an edict dismissed those fifty years of age and below.
translations.idiomatic: Soon, because the monastic community had grown too large, an edict dismissed those fifty years of age and below.

sentences.zh: 世祖初平赫連昌，得沙門惠始，姓張。

translations.literal: When Emperor Shizu first pacified Helian Chang, he obtained the shramana Huishi, surname Zhang.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Shizu first pacified Helian Chang, he obtained the monk Huishi, surnamed Zhang.

sentences.zh: 家本清河，聞羅什出新經，遂詣長安見之，觀習經典。

translations.literal: His family was originally from Qinghe; hearing that Kumarajiva was producing new sutras, he went to Chang'an to see him and studied the classics.
translations.idiomatic: His family was originally from Qinghe; hearing that Kumarajiva was producing new translations, he went to Chang'an to study under him.

sentences.zh: 坐禪於白渠北，晝則入城聽講，夕則還處靜坐。

translations.literal: He practiced meditation north of the White Canal; by day he entered the city to hear lectures, in the evening he returned to sit in stillness.
translations.idiomatic: He practiced meditation north of the White Canal, entering the city by day to hear lectures and returning each evening to meditate in stillness.

sentences.zh: 三輔有識多宗之。

translations.literal: Many learned men of the three metropolitan areas took him as their model.
translations.idiomatic: Many learned men of the capital region took him as their model.

sentences.zh: 劉裕滅姚泓，留子義真鎮長安，義真及僚佐皆敬重焉。

translations.literal: When Liu Yu destroyed Yao Hong, he left his son Yizhen to guard Chang'an; Yizhen and his staff all deeply respected Huishi.
translations.idiomatic: When Liu Yu destroyed Yao Hong, he left his son Yizhen to guard Chang'an; Yizhen and his staff all deeply respected Huishi.

sentences.zh: 義真之去長安也，赫連屈丐追敗之，道俗少長咸見坑戮。

translations.literal: When Yizhen left Chang'an, Helian Qujie pursued and defeated him; monks and laity, young and old, were all seen slaughtered.
translations.idiomatic: When Yizhen fled Chang'an, Helian Qujie pursued and defeated him; monks and laity of all ages were slaughtered.

sentences.zh: 惠始身被白刃，而體不傷。

translations.literal: Huishi's body was struck by bare blades yet was not harmed.
translations.idiomatic: Huishi's body was struck by bare blades yet was unharmed.

sentences.zh: 眾大怪異，言於屈丐。

translations.literal: The crowd greatly marveled and reported it to Qujie.
translations.idiomatic: The crowd marveled greatly and reported it to Qujie.

sentences.zh: 屈丐大怒，召惠始於前，以所持寶劍擊之，又不能害，乃懼而謝罪。

translations.literal: Qujie was greatly enraged, summoned Huishi before him, and struck him with the precious sword he held—it could not harm him either; he then feared and apologized.
translations.idiomatic: Qujie was enraged, summoned Huishi, and struck him with his sword—it could not harm him; he then feared and apologized.

sentences.zh: 統萬平，惠始到京都，多所訓導，時人莫測其迹。

translations.literal: When Tongwan was pacified, Huishi came to the capital and instructed many; people of the time could not fathom his traces.
translations.idiomatic: When Tongwan was pacified, Huishi came to the capital and instructed many; no one could fathom his ways.

sentences.zh: 世祖甚重之，每加禮敬。

translations.literal: Emperor Shizu greatly valued him and always added ritual respect.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Shizu greatly valued him and always showed him ritual respect.

sentences.zh: 始自習禪，至於沒世，稱五十餘年，未嘗寢臥。

translations.literal: From when he first practiced meditation until his death, called fifty-odd years, he never lay down to sleep.
translations.idiomatic: From when he first took up meditation until his death, more than fifty years, he never lay down to sleep.

sentences.zh: 或時跣行，雖履泥塵，初不汙足，色愈鮮白，世號之曰白脚師。

translations.literal: Sometimes he walked barefoot; though treading mud and dust, his feet were never soiled, his complexion ever fresher and whiter— the world called him the White-Footed Master.
translations.idiomatic: Sometimes he walked barefoot; though treading mud and dust, his feet were never soiled and his complexion grew ever fairer—the world called him the White-Footed Master.

sentences.zh: 太延中，臨終於八角寺，齊潔端坐，僧徒滿側，凝泊而絕。

translations.literal: In the Taiyan era he died at the Bajiao Temple, sitting upright in purity and stillness, monks filling his sides, passing away in serene concentration.
translations.idiomatic: In the Taiyan era he died at the Bajiao Temple, sitting upright in purity with monks surrounding him, passing away in serene concentration.

sentences.zh: 停屍十餘日，坐既不改，容色如一，舉世神異之。

translations.literal: The corpse rested more than ten days; his seated posture did not change and his complexion was as one—the whole world regarded it as supernatural.
translations.idiomatic: His body rested more than ten days without change of posture or complexion—the whole world regarded it as supernatural.

sentences.zh: 遂瘞寺內。

translations.literal: He was buried within the temple.
translations.idiomatic: He was buried within the temple.

sentences.zh: 至真君六年，制城內不得留瘞，乃葬於南郊之外。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Zhenjun, regulations forbade burial within the city walls, so he was buried outside the southern suburbs.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year of Zhenjun, regulations forbade burial within the city, so he was buried outside the southern suburbs.

sentences.zh: 始死十年矣，開殯儼然，初不傾壞。

translations.literal: Ten years after his death the coffin was opened—he was still dignified and had not decayed at all.
translations.idiomatic: Ten years after his death the coffin was opened—his body was still dignified and wholly undecayed.

sentences.zh: 送葬者六千餘人，莫不感慟。

translations.literal: More than six thousand people attended the funeral, none without grief.
translations.idiomatic: More than six thousand people attended the funeral, all grieving deeply.

sentences.zh: 中書監高允為其傳，頌其德迹。

translations.literal: Zhongshu Supervisor Gao Yun wrote his biography, praising his virtuous traces.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongshu Supervisor Gao Yun wrote his biography, praising his virtuous deeds.

sentences.zh: 惠始冢上，立石精舍，圖其形像。

translations.literal: At Huishi's tomb a stone shrine was erected, with his image painted.
translations.idiomatic: At Huishi's tomb a stone shrine was erected with his image painted within.

sentences.zh: 經毀法時，猶自全立。

translations.literal: When the Dharma was destroyed, it still stood whole by itself.
translations.idiomatic: Even when the Dharma was suppressed, the shrine still stood intact.

sentences.zh: 世祖即位，富於春秋。

translations.literal: When Emperor Shizu ascended the throne, he was in the prime of youth.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Shizu ascended the throne, he was still young.

sentences.zh: 既而銳志武功，每以平定禍亂為先。

translations.literal: Soon he was keen in martial achievement, always putting the pacification of calamity and disorder first.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he turned his keen attention to military achievement, always putting the pacification of disorder first.

sentences.zh: 雖歸宗佛法，敬重沙門，而未存覽經教，深求緣報之意。

translations.literal: Although he took refuge in the Buddha Dharma and respected shramanas, he did not yet peruse the scriptural teachings or deeply seek the meaning of karmic retribution.
translations.idiomatic: Although he honored Buddhism and respected monks, he did not study the scriptures or deeply seek the meaning of karmic retribution.

sentences.zh: 及得寇謙之道，帝以清淨無為，有仙化之證，遂信行其術。

translations.literal: When he obtained Kou Qianzhi's Way, the emperor regarded purity and non-action as having proof of immortal transformation and thus believed in and practiced his arts.
translations.idiomatic: When he encountered Kou Qianzhi's teachings, the emperor believed that purity and non-action offered proof of immortal transformation and practiced his arts.

sentences.zh: 時司徒崔浩，博學多聞，帝每訪以大事。

translations.literal: At that time Minister of Works Cui Hao was learned and widely informed; the emperor often consulted him on great affairs.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Minister of Works Cui Hao was learned and widely informed; the emperor often consulted him on important matters.

sentences.zh: 浩奉謙之道，尤不信佛，與帝言，數加非毀，常謂虛誕，為世費害。

translations.literal: Hao followed Qianzhi's Way and especially did not believe in Buddhism; speaking with the emperor, he repeatedly slandered it, often calling it empty and false, a harm and expense to the world.
translations.idiomatic: Hao followed Qianzhi's teachings and especially disbelieved Buddhism; he repeatedly slandered it to the emperor, calling it empty falsehood and a harm to the world.

sentences.zh: 帝以其辯博，頗信之。

translations.literal: The emperor, because of his eloquent learning, quite believed him.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor, impressed by his eloquence and learning, largely believed him.

sentences.zh: 會蓋吳反杏城，關中騷動，帝乃西伐，至於長安。

translations.literal: It happened that Gai Wu rebelled at Xingcheng and Guanzhong was in turmoil; the emperor then campaigned west and reached Chang'an.
translations.idiomatic: When Gai Wu rebelled at Xingcheng and Guanzhong was in turmoil, the emperor marched west as far as Chang'an.

sentences.zh: 先是，長安沙門種麥寺內，御騶牧馬於麥中，帝入觀馬。

translations.literal: Before this, Chang'an shramanas had planted wheat inside a temple; imperial grooms pastured horses in the wheat, and the emperor entered to inspect the horses.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, monks at Chang'an had planted wheat in their temple; imperial grooms pastured horses in the wheat, and the emperor entered to inspect the horses.

sentences.zh: 沙門飲從官酒，從官入其便室，見大有弓矢矛盾，出以奏聞。

translations.literal: A shramana gave wine to an attendant official; the attendant entered his privy chamber and saw a great store of bows, arrows, spears, and shields, and went out to report it.
translations.idiomatic: A monk gave wine to an attendant; the attendant entered his privy chamber and found a large store of bows, arrows, spears, and shields, which he reported.

sentences.zh: 帝怒曰：「此非沙門所用，當與蓋吳通謀，規害人耳！」

translations.literal: The emperor angrily said: "These are not what shramanas use—they must be in league with Gai Wu, plotting to harm people!"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor angrily said: "These are not what monks use—they must be in league with Gai Wu, plotting harm!"

sentences.zh: 命有司案誅一寺，閱其財產，大得釀酒具及州郡牧守富人所寄藏物，蓋以萬計。

translations.literal: He ordered the authorities to investigate and execute the entire monastery; examining its property, they found large quantities of brewing equipment and goods deposited for safekeeping by prefectural and commandery governors, shepherds, and wealthy men—altogether numbering in the tens of thousands.
translations.idiomatic: He ordered the authorities to investigate and execute the entire monastery; examining its property, they found brewing equipment and goods deposited by officials and wealthy men numbering in the tens of thousands.

sentences.zh: 又為屈室，與貴室女私行淫亂。

translations.literal: There were also hidden chambers where they privately committed sexual misconduct with women of noble families.
translations.idiomatic: There were also hidden chambers where they privately committed sexual misconduct with women of noble families.

sentences.zh: 帝既忿沙門非法，浩時從行，因進其說。

translations.literal: The emperor, already angry at the shramanas' illegal conduct, with Hao accompanying the journey, advanced his arguments.
translations.idiomatic: Already angry at the monks' illegal conduct, with Hao accompanying him on the campaign, the emperor accepted his arguments.

sentences.zh: 詔誅長安沙門，焚破佛像，敕留臺下四方令，一依長安行事。

translations.literal: An edict ordered the execution of Chang'an shramanas and the burning and destruction of Buddha images; it commanded the regional commissioners under the central government in all four directions to act according to the Chang'an precedent.
translations.idiomatic: An edict ordered the execution of Chang'an monks and the destruction of Buddha images; regional commissioners throughout the realm were commanded to follow the Chang'an precedent.

sentences.zh: 又詔曰：「彼沙門者，假西戎虛誕，妄生妖孽，非所以一齊政化，布淳德於天下也。

translations.literal: Another edict said: "Those shramanas borrow empty falsehoods from the Western barbarians and recklessly produce demonic evils—they are not the means to unify government and transform the people or spread pure virtue throughout the realm.
translations.idiomatic: Another edict declared: "Those monks borrow empty falsehoods from the Western barbarians and recklessly produce demonic evils—they cannot unify government, transform the people, or spread pure virtue throughout the realm.

sentences.zh: 自王公已下，有私養沙門者，皆送官曹，不得隱匿。

translations.literal: From kings and dukes downward, those who privately keep shramanas must all send them to the authorities; none may conceal them.
translations.idiomatic: From kings and dukes downward, anyone who privately keeps monks must send them to the authorities; none may conceal them.

sentences.zh: 限今年二月十五日，過期不出，沙門身死，容止者誅一門。」

translations.literal: The deadline is the fifteenth day of the second month of this year; those who fail to produce them after the deadline—the shramana dies, and whoever harbors him suffers execution of his entire household."
translations.idiomatic: The deadline is the fifteenth day of the second month of this year; after the deadline the monk dies, and whoever harbors him suffers execution of his entire household."

sentences.zh: 時恭宗為太子監國，素敬佛道。

translations.literal: At that time Emperor Gongzong as crown prince supervised the state and had always revered the Buddha Dharma.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Crown Prince Gongzong supervised the state and had always revered Buddhism.

sentences.zh: 頻上表，陳刑殺沙門之濫，又非圖像之罪。

translations.literal: He repeatedly submitted memorials stating that the execution of shramanas was excessive and that images were not guilty.
translations.idiomatic: He repeatedly submitted memorials arguing that executing monks was excessive and that images were not guilty.

sentences.zh: 今罷其道，杜諸寺門，世不修奉，土木丹青，自然毀滅。

translations.literal: Now if its Way is abolished and temple gates sealed, the world will not maintain worship—timber, earth, and painted colors will naturally perish.
translations.idiomatic: If its teaching is abolished and temple gates sealed, the world will cease worship—the structures will naturally decay.

sentences.zh: 如是再三，不許。

translations.literal: Thus repeatedly, but it was not permitted.
translations.idiomatic: He argued thus repeatedly, but was not permitted.

sentences.zh: 乃下詔曰：「昔後漢荒君，信惑邪偽，妄假睡夢，事胡妖鬼，以亂天常，自古九州之中無此也。

translations.literal: Then an edict was issued: "In former times the dissolute ruler of Later Han believed and was deluded by evil falsity, falsely borrowing dreams in sleep to serve barbarian demon ghosts and disorder the heavenly constants—never before in the Nine Provinces since antiquity.
translations.idiomatic: Then an edict was issued: "In former times the dissolute ruler of Later Han was deluded by evil falsity, falsely borrowing dreams to serve barbarian demon ghosts and disorder the heavenly order—never before in the Nine Provinces since antiquity.

sentences.zh: 夸誕大言，不本人情。

translations.literal: Extravagant and grand words, not rooted in human feeling.
translations.idiomatic: Extravagant and grand words, not rooted in human nature.

sentences.zh: 叔季之世，闇君亂主，莫不眩焉。

translations.literal: In the declining age, benighted rulers and disorderly lords were all dazzled by it.
translations.idiomatic: In declining ages, benighted rulers and disorderly lords were all dazzled by it.

sentences.zh: 由是政教不行，禮義大壞，鬼道熾盛，視王者之法，蔑如也。

translations.literal: Hence government and teaching did not prevail, ritual and righteousness greatly collapsed, the ghostly Way flourished extravagantly, and they treated the king's law with contempt.
translations.idiomatic: Hence government and teaching failed, ritual and righteousness collapsed, the demonic Way flourished, and they treated the king's law with contempt.

sentences.zh: 自此以來，代經亂禍，天罰亟行，生民死盡，五服之內，鞠為丘墟，千里蕭條，不見人迹，皆由於此。

translations.literal: From then on, generation after generation experienced disorder and calamity; heaven's punishment repeatedly fell, the people died out, within the five degrees of mourning all became ruins, for a thousand li desolate with no human trace—all because of this.
translations.idiomatic: From then on generation after generation suffered disorder and calamity; heaven's punishment fell repeatedly, the people perished, the land within the five degrees of mourning became ruins, and for a thousand li none could be seen—all because of this.

sentences.zh: 朕承天緒，屬當窮運之弊，欲除偽定真，復羲農之治。

translations.literal: I have received heaven's succession and happen to face the ills of an exhausted age; I wish to eliminate the false and fix the true, restoring the governance of Fu Xi and Shen Nong.
translations.idiomatic: I have received heaven's mandate and face the ills of an exhausted age; I wish to eliminate the false and establish the true, restoring the governance of Fuxi and Shennong.

sentences.zh: 其一切盪除胡神，滅其蹤迹，庶無謝於風氏矣。

translations.literal: Let all barbarian gods be thoroughly swept away and their traces extinguished, so that we may not fail the clan of Feng.
translations.idiomatic: Let all barbarian gods be thoroughly swept away and their traces extinguished, so that we may not fail our ancestors.

sentences.zh: 自今以後，敢有事胡神及造形像泥人、銅人者，門誅。

translations.literal: From now on, whoever dares serve barbarian gods or make images of clay or bronze men shall suffer execution of the household.
translations.idiomatic: From now on, whoever dares serve barbarian gods or make images of clay or bronze shall suffer execution of the household.

sentences.zh: 雖言胡神，問今胡人，共云無有。

translations.literal: Though they speak of barbarian gods, if one asks the barbarians of today, they all say there are none.
translations.idiomatic: Though they speak of barbarian gods, if one asks the barbarians of today, they all say there are none.

sentences.zh: 皆是前世漢人無賴子弟劉元真、呂伯強之徒，接乞胡之誕言，[16]用老莊之虛假，附而益之，皆非真實。

translations.literal: All are worthless sons of Han from former ages, men like Liu Yuanzhen and Lü Boqiang, who adopted the wild words of begging barbarians, using the empty falsity of Laozi and Zhuangzi, adding to and embellishing them—none is true.
translations.idiomatic: All are worthless Han men of former ages like Liu Yuanzhen and Lü Boqiang, who adopted the wild words of barbarian beggars, using the empty falsity of Laozi and Zhuangzi and embellishing them—none is true.

sentences.zh: 至使王法廢而不行，蓋大姦之魁也。

translations.literal: They caused the king's law to fall into disuse and not be carried out—these are truly the ringleaders of great wickedness.
translations.idiomatic: They caused the king's law to fall into disuse—these are truly the ringleaders of great wickedness.

sentences.zh: 有非常之人，然後能行非常之事。

translations.literal: Only an extraordinary man can then perform an extraordinary deed.
translations.idiomatic: Only an extraordinary man can perform an extraordinary deed.

sentences.zh: 非朕孰能去此歷代之偽物！

translations.literal: If not I, who can remove these false things of successive ages!
translations.idiomatic: If not I, who can remove these false things of successive ages!

sentences.zh: 有司宣告征鎮諸軍、刺史，諸有佛圖形像及胡經，盡皆擊破焚燒，沙門無少長悉坑之。」

translations.literal: Let the relevant offices proclaim to the campaigning armies of the regions and the prefects: wherever there are Buddhist pagoda images and barbarian scriptures, let all be smashed and burned, and shramanas young and old all buried alive."
translations.idiomatic: Let the relevant offices proclaim to the armies and prefects: wherever there are Buddhist images and barbarian scriptures, let all be smashed and burned, and monks young and old all buried alive."

sentences.zh: 是歲，真君七年三月也。

translations.literal: That year was the third month of the seventh year of Zhenjun.
translations.idiomatic: That year was the third month of the seventh year of Zhenjun.
