sentences.zh: 恭宗言雖不用，然猶緩宣詔書，遠近皆豫聞知，得各為計。

translations.literal: Although Gongzong's words were not adopted, he still slowed the promulgation of the edict so that distant and near all heard in advance and could each make plans.
translations.idiomatic: Although Gongzong's words were not adopted, he still delayed promulgation of the edict so that distant and near all heard in advance and could make plans.

sentences.zh: 四方沙門，多亡匿獲免，在京邑者，亦蒙全濟。

translations.literal: Shramanas in all directions mostly fled and hid to escape; those in the capital also mostly escaped intact.
translations.idiomatic: Monks throughout the realm mostly fled and hid to escape; those in the capital also mostly survived.

sentences.zh: 金銀寶像及諸經論，大得秘藏。

translations.literal: Gold, silver, Buddha images, and various scriptures and treatises were greatly hidden away in secret.
translations.idiomatic: Gold, silver, Buddha images, and scriptures were greatly hidden away in secret.

sentences.zh: 而土木宮塔，聲教所及，莫不畢毀矣。

translations.literal: But earthen and wooden palace pagodas wherever the teaching's sound reached were all utterly destroyed.
translations.idiomatic: But earthen and wooden temples wherever the teaching had reached were all utterly destroyed.

sentences.zh: 始謙之與浩同從車駕，苦與浩諍，浩不肯，謂浩曰：「卿今促年受戮，滅門戶矣。」

translations.literal: At first Qianzhi and Hao accompanied the imperial carriage together; Qianzhi bitterly argued with Hao but Hao would not agree; Qianzhi said to Hao: "You will soon die young by execution, and your household will be extinguished."
translations.idiomatic: At first Qianzhi and Hao accompanied the imperial carriage together; Qianzhi bitterly argued with Hao, who would not agree; Qianzhi told Hao: "You will soon die by execution, and your household will be extinguished."

sentences.zh: 後四年，浩誅，備五刑，時年七十。

translations.literal: Four years later Hao was executed, suffering all five punishments, at the age of seventy.
translations.idiomatic: Four years later Hao was executed, suffering all five punishments, at the age of seventy.

sentences.zh: 浩既誅死，帝頗悔之。

translations.literal: After Hao was executed and died, the emperor quite regretted it.
translations.idiomatic: After Hao was executed, the emperor deeply regretted it.

sentences.zh: 業已行，難中修復。

translations.literal: What had already been done was hard to repair midway.
translations.idiomatic: What had already been done could not easily be undone.

sentences.zh: 恭宗潛欲興之，未敢言也。

translations.literal: Gongzong secretly wished to revive it but did not dare speak.
translations.idiomatic: Gongzong secretly wished to revive Buddhism but did not dare speak.

sentences.zh: 佛淪廢終帝世，積七八年。

translations.literal: Buddhism was abolished to the end of the emperor's reign, accumulating seven or eight years.
translations.idiomatic: Buddhism was suppressed to the end of the emperor's reign, for seven or eight years.

sentences.zh: 然禁稍寬㢮，篤信之家，得密奉事，沙門專至者，猶竊法服誦習焉。

translations.literal: Yet the prohibition gradually relaxed; families of devout faith could secretly maintain worship, and shramanas who came especially still secretly wore religious garb and recited and studied.
translations.idiomatic: Yet the prohibition gradually relaxed; devout families could secretly maintain worship, and dedicated monks still secretly wore religious garb and studied.

sentences.zh: 唯不得顯行於京都矣。

translations.literal: Only they could not practice openly in the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Only they could not practice openly in the capital.

sentences.zh: 先是，沙門曇曜有操尚，又為恭宗所知禮。

translations.literal: Before this, the shramana Tanyao had integrity and was also known and honored by Gongzong.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, the monk Tanyao had integrity and was also known and honored by Gongzong.

sentences.zh: 佛法之滅，沙門多以餘能自效，還俗求見。

translations.literal: When the Buddha Dharma was extinguished, shramanas mostly used remaining skills to offer service, returning to the laity to seek audience.
translations.idiomatic: When Buddhism was suppressed, monks mostly used other skills to offer service, returning to lay life to seek audience.

sentences.zh: 曜誓欲守死，恭宗親加勸喻，至於再三，不得已，乃止。

translations.literal: Tanyao vowed to guard unto death; Gongzong personally urged and admonished him again and again; having no alternative, he then stopped.
translations.idiomatic: Tanyao vowed to die rather than comply; Gongzong personally urged him again and again; having no alternative, he desisted.

sentences.zh: 密持法服器物，不暫離身，聞者歎重之。

translations.literal: Secretly he held religious garments and implements and did not briefly leave his person; those who heard sighed and honored him.
translations.idiomatic: He secretly held religious garments and implements and never left them; those who heard admired him.

sentences.zh: 高宗踐極，下詔曰：「夫為帝王者，必祗奉明靈，顯彰仁道，其能惠著生民，濟益群品者，雖在古昔，猶序其風烈。

translations.literal: When Emperor Gaozong ascended the throne, an edict said: "Those who become emperors must reverently serve bright spirits and manifest benevolent Way; those who can show kindness to the living people and aid and benefit the multitude—even in ancient times their meritorious conduct is recorded.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Gaozong ascended the throne, an edict declared: "Those who become emperors must reverently serve bright spirits and manifest the benevolent Way; those who show kindness to the people and benefit the multitude—even in ancient times their merit is recorded.

sentences.zh: 是以春秋嘉崇明之禮，祭典載功施之族。

translations.literal: Therefore the Spring and Autumn Annals praise the rites of bright veneration, and the sacrificial regulations record clans of meritorious bestowal.
translations.idiomatic: Therefore the Spring and Autumn Annals praise the rites of bright veneration, and the sacrificial regulations record clans of meritorious service.

sentences.zh: 況釋迦如來功濟大千，惠流塵境，等生死者歎其達觀，覽文義者，貴其妙明，助王政之禁律，益仁智之善性，排斥群邪，開演正覺。

translations.literal: How much more does Shakyamuni Tathagata's merit aid the great thousand worlds and his grace flow through the dusty realm; those who equalize birth and death sigh at his penetrating vision, and those who peruse literary meanings treasure his subtle illumination, aiding the prohibitions and laws of royal government and increasing the good nature of benevolence and wisdom, repelling the multitude of devils and opening and developing right awakening.
translations.idiomatic: How much more does the Buddha Shakyamuni, whose merit aids the great thousand worlds and whose grace flows through the realm; those who contemplate birth and death admire his penetrating vision, and those who study doctrine treasure his subtle illumination, aiding royal law and increasing benevolence and wisdom, repelling evil and opening right awakening.

sentences.zh: 故前代已來，莫不崇尚，亦我國家常所尊事也。

translations.literal: Therefore former ages have not failed to honor it, and our state has also constantly respected and served it.
translations.idiomatic: Therefore former ages have not failed to honor it, and our state has also constantly respected it.

sentences.zh: 世祖太武皇帝，開廣邊荒，德澤遐及。

translations.literal: Emperor Taizu Taowu opened and broadened the distant frontier; his virtue and grace reached far.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Taizu Taowu opened the distant frontier; his virtue and grace reached far.

sentences.zh: 沙門道士善行純誠，惠始之倫，無遠不至，風義相感，往往如林。

translations.literal: Shramanas and Daoist priests of pure conduct and sincere practice, men like Huishi, came from afar without fail; wind and righteousness mutually moved them, gathering often like a forest.
translations.idiomatic: Monks and Daoist priests of pure conduct, men like Huishi, came from afar without fail; drawn by wind and righteousness, they gathered like a forest.

sentences.zh: 夫山海之深，怪物多有，姦淫之徒，得容假託，講寺之中，致有兇黨。

translations.literal: In the depths of mountains and seas there are many strange creatures; licentious and depraved persons could borrow false pretense—in lecture temples there came to be violent factions.
translations.idiomatic: In the depths of mountains and seas there are many strange things; depraved persons could borrow false pretense—in temples there came to be violent factions.

sentences.zh: 是以先朝因其瑕釁，戮其有罪。

translations.literal: Therefore the former court, because of their flaws and offenses, executed those guilty.
translations.idiomatic: Therefore the former court, because of their offenses, executed the guilty.

sentences.zh: 有司失旨，一切禁斷。

translations.literal: The relevant offices missed the intent and prohibited everything.
translations.idiomatic: The relevant offices missed the intent and prohibited everything.

sentences.zh: 景穆皇帝每為慨然，值軍國多事，未遑修復。

translations.literal: Emperor Jingmu often sighed over this; with military and state affairs numerous, he had not yet been able to restore it.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Jingmu often sighed over this; with military and state affairs pressing, he had not yet restored it.

sentences.zh: 朕承洪緒，君臨萬邦，思述先志，以隆斯道。

translations.literal: I have received the great succession and rule the myriad states, thinking to follow the former will and elevate this Way.
translations.idiomatic: I have received the great succession and rule the myriad states, thinking to follow the former will and elevate this teaching.

sentences.zh: 今制諸州郡縣，於眾居之所，各聽建佛圖一區，任其財用，不制會限。

translations.literal: Now it is ordered that in all prefectures, commanderies, and counties, in places where people dwell, each may build one Buddhist pagoda as their resources allow, without fixed quota.
translations.idiomatic: Now it is ordered that in all prefectures, commanderies, and counties, in places where people dwell, each may build one Buddhist pagoda as their resources allow, without fixed quota.

sentences.zh: 其好樂道法，欲為沙門，不問長幼，出於良家，性行素篤，無諸嫌穢，鄉里所明者，聽其出家。

translations.literal: Those who delight in the Way and wish to become shramanas, regardless of age, if from good families with conduct always sincere and without various defilements, clear to the village, may be permitted to leave home.
translations.idiomatic: Those who delight in the Way and wish to become monks, regardless of age, if from good families of sincere conduct without defilement, known to their village, may be permitted to leave home.

sentences.zh: 率大州五十，小州四十人，其郡遙遠臺者十人。

translations.literal: Large provinces fifty persons, small provinces forty; commanderies far from the capital ten.
translations.idiomatic: Large provinces fifty persons, small provinces forty; distant commanderies ten.

sentences.zh: 各當局分，皆足以化惡就善，播揚道教也。」

translations.literal: Each in their jurisdiction, all sufficient to transform evil toward good and spread and raise the Way teaching."
translations.idiomatic: Each in their jurisdiction, all sufficient to transform evil toward good and spread the teaching."

sentences.zh: 天下承風，朝不及夕，往時所毀圖寺，仍還修矣。

translations.literal: The realm received the wind; court did not reach evening before former destroyed pagoda temples were restored.
translations.idiomatic: The realm received the edict; before evening former destroyed temples were restored.

sentences.zh: 佛像經論，皆復得顯。

translations.literal: Buddha images, scriptures, and treatises all again became manifest.
translations.idiomatic: Buddha images, scriptures, and treatises all again became manifest.

sentences.zh: 京師沙門師賢，本罽賓國王種人，少入道，東遊涼城，涼平赴京。

translations.literal: The capital shramana Shixian was originally of the kingly clan of Kapisa; in youth he entered the Way, traveled east to Liang city, and when Liang was pacified went to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: The capital monk Shixian was originally of the kingly clan of Kapisa; in youth he entered the monastic life, traveled east to Liang city, and when Liang was pacified went to the capital.

sentences.zh: 罷佛法時，師賢假為醫術還俗，而守道不改。

translations.literal: When the Buddha Dharma was abolished, Shixian feigned returning to the laity through medical arts but did not change in guarding the Way.
translations.idiomatic: When Buddhism was suppressed, Shixian feigned returning to lay life through medical arts but did not abandon the Way.

sentences.zh: 於修復日，即反沙門，其同輩五人。

translations.literal: On the day of restoration he immediately returned to being a shramana, with five companions of his generation.
translations.idiomatic: On the day of restoration he immediately returned to monastic life, with five companions.

sentences.zh: 帝乃親為下髮。

translations.literal: The emperor personally performed the tonsure for them.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor personally performed the tonsure for them.

sentences.zh: 師賢仍為道人統。

translations.literal: Shixian was again made Director of the Way.
translations.idiomatic: Shixian was again made Director of the Way.

sentences.zh: 是年，詔有司為石像，令如帝身。

translations.literal: That year an edict ordered the relevant offices to make a stone image, commanded to resemble the emperor's person.
translations.idiomatic: That year an edict ordered the relevant offices to make a stone image in the emperor's likeness.

sentences.zh: 既成，顏上足下，各有黑石，冥同帝體上下黑子。

translations.literal: When completed, on the face and on the feet above and below there were black stones, darkly identical to the black moles on the emperor's body above and below.
translations.idiomatic: When completed, on the face and feet there were black stones, identical to the black moles on the emperor's body.

sentences.zh: 論者以為純誠所感。

translations.literal: Discussants regarded it as moved by pure sincerity.
translations.idiomatic: Commentators regarded it as a response to pure sincerity.

sentences.zh: 興光元年秋，敕有司於五級大寺內，[17]為太祖已下五帝，鑄釋迦立像五，各長一丈六尺，都用赤金二十五萬斤。

translations.literal: In autumn of the first year of Xingguang, an edict ordered the relevant offices within the five-story great temple to cast five standing Shakyamuni images for the Five Emperors from the Taizu down, each one zhang and six chi in height, using altogether two hundred fifty thousand jin of red gold.
translations.idiomatic: In autumn of the first year of Xingguang, an edict ordered the casting within the five-story great temple of five standing Shakyamuni images for the Five Emperors from Taizu down, each one zhang and six chi tall, using two hundred fifty thousand jin of red gold.

sentences.zh: [18]太安初，有師子國胡沙門邪奢遺多、浮陀難提等五人，奉佛像三，到京都。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Tai'an, five barbarian shramanas from the Lion Kingdom including Yixie Yiduo and Fotu Nandi came to the capital, presenting three Buddha images.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Tai'an, five foreign monks from the Lion Kingdom including Yixie Yiduo and Fotu Nandi came to the capital, presenting three Buddha images.

sentences.zh: 皆云，備歷西域諸國，見佛影迹及肉髻，外國諸王相承，咸遣工匠，摹寫其容，莫能及難提所造者，去十餘步，視之炳然，轉近轉微。

translations.literal: All said they had fully traversed the states of the Western Regions, seen Buddha's shadow traces and cranial protuberance; foreign kings in succession all sent craftsmen to copy his appearance, but none could equal what Nandi made—at more than ten paces it was bright and clear, drawing nearer it grew subtle.
translations.idiomatic: All said they had traversed the states of the Western Regions and seen the Buddha's shadow and cranial protuberance; foreign kings had sent craftsmen to copy his appearance, but none equaled Nandi's work—at more than ten paces it was bright and clear, drawing nearer it grew subtle.

sentences.zh: 又沙勒胡沙門，赴京師致佛鉢并畫像迹。

translations.literal: There was also a barbarian shramana from Shule who came to the capital presenting a Buddha bowl and painted image traces.
translations.idiomatic: There was also a foreign monk from Shule who came to the capital presenting a Buddha bowl and painted image traces.

sentences.zh: 和平初，師賢卒。

translations.literal: In the beginning of Heping, Shixian died.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Heping, Shixian died.

sentences.zh: 曇曜代之，更名沙門統。

translations.literal: Tanyao replaced him and was renamed Director of Shramanas.
translations.idiomatic: Tanyao replaced him and was renamed Director of Monks.

sentences.zh: 初曇曜以復佛法之明年，自中山被命赴京，值帝出，見于路，御馬前銜曜衣，時以為馬識善人。

translations.literal: At first, in the year after Tanyao restored the Buddha Dharma, he was ordered from Zhongshan to the capital; meeting the emperor on the road, the imperial horse went before him and held Tanyao's garment in its mouth—at the time people said the horse recognized a good man.
translations.idiomatic: In the year after Tanyao restored Buddhism, he was ordered from Zhongshan to the capital; meeting the emperor on the road, the imperial horse went before him and held his garment in its mouth—people said the horse recognized a good man.

sentences.zh: 帝後奉以師禮。

translations.literal: The emperor later honored him with the rites due a teacher.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor later honored him with the rites due a teacher.

sentences.zh: 曇曜白帝，於京城西武州塞，鑿山石壁，開窟五所，鐫建佛像各一。

translations.literal: Tanyao told the emperor that at Wuzhou Pass west of the capital he should cut into the stone cliff and open five caves, carving and establishing one Buddha image in each.
translations.idiomatic: Tanyao told the emperor to cut into the stone cliff at Wuzhou Pass west of the capital and open five caves, carving one Buddha image in each.

sentences.zh: 高者七十尺，次六十尺，彫飾奇偉，冠於一世。

translations.literal: The tallest seventy chi, the next sixty chi—carved and adorned wonderfully, foremost in the age.
translations.idiomatic: The tallest seventy chi, the next sixty chi—wonderfully carved and adorned, foremost in the age.

sentences.zh: 曇曜奏：平齊戶及諸民，有能歲輸穀六十斛入僧曹者，即為「僧祇戶」，粟為「僧祇粟」，至於儉歲，賑給飢民。

translations.literal: Tanyao memorialized: households pacified from Qi and various people who could yearly deliver sixty hu of grain to the monastic treasury would be made 'sangha households,' the grain 'sangha grain'; in lean years it would relieve the hungry people.
translations.idiomatic: Tanyao memorialized: households pacified from Qi and others who could yearly deliver sixty hu of grain to the monastic treasury would become sangha households, the grain sangha grain; in lean years it would relieve the hungry.

sentences.zh: 又請民犯重罪及官奴以為「佛圖戶」，以供諸寺掃洒，歲兼營田輸粟。

translations.literal: He also requested that people who committed serious crimes and government slaves be made 'pagoda households' to supply all temples with sweeping, each year also farming fields and delivering grain.
translations.idiomatic: He also requested that people who committed serious crimes and government slaves become pagoda households to supply temples with sweeping and farming, delivering grain each year.

sentences.zh: 高宗並許之。

translations.literal: Emperor Gaozong all permitted it.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Gaozong permitted all of this.

sentences.zh: 於是僧祇戶、粟及寺戶，徧於州鎮矣。

translations.literal: Thereupon sangha households, grain, and temple households spread throughout the provinces and garrisons.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon sangha households, sangha grain, and temple households spread throughout the provinces and garrisons.

sentences.zh: 曇曜又與天竺沙門常那邪舍等，譯出新經十四部。

translations.literal: Tanyao also together with the Indian shramana Changnayeshe and others translated fourteen new sutras.
translations.idiomatic: Tanyao also together with the Indian monk Changnayeshe and others translated fourteen new sutras.

sentences.zh: 又有沙門道進、僧超、法存等，並有名於時，演唱諸異。

translations.literal: There were also shramanas Daojin, Sengchao, Facun, and others, all famous in the age, lecturing on various extraordinary teachings.
translations.idiomatic: There were also monks Daojin, Sengchao, Facun, and others, all famous in the age, lecturing on various teachings.

translations.literal: [Editorial collation note 19.]
translations.idiomatic: [Editorial note 19.]

sentences.zh: 顯祖即位，敦信尤深，覽諸經論，好老莊。

translations.literal: When Emperor Xianzu ascended the throne, his devout faith was especially deep; he perused various scriptures and treatises and favored Laozi and Zhuangzi.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xianzu ascended the throne, his devout faith was especially deep; he studied various scriptures and favored Laozi and Zhuangzi.

sentences.zh: 每引諸沙門及能談玄之士，與論理要。

translations.literal: He often invited various shramanas and masters able to discuss the abstruse to debate essential principles with him.
translations.idiomatic: He often invited monks and masters able to discuss the abstruse to debate essential principles with him.

sentences.zh: 初高宗太安末，劉駿於丹陽中興寺設齋。

translations.literal: At first, in the last years of Tai'an under Emperor Gaozong, Liu Jun set up a fast at Zhongxing Temple in Danyang.
translations.idiomatic: At first, in the last years of Tai'an under Emperor Gaozong, Liu Jun set up a fast at Zhongxing Temple in Danyang.

sentences.zh: 有一沙門，容止獨秀，舉眾往目，皆莫識焉。

translations.literal: There was one shramana of unique bearing and deportment; the whole assembly looked toward him, yet none recognized him.
translations.idiomatic: There was one monk of unique bearing and deportment; the whole assembly looked toward him, yet none recognized him.

sentences.zh: 沙門惠璩起問之，答名惠明。

translations.literal: The shramana Huiqu rose to question him; he answered that his name was Huiming.
translations.idiomatic: The monk Huiqu rose to question him; he answered that his name was Huiming.

sentences.zh: 又問所住，答云，從天安寺來。

translations.literal: He asked where he resided; he answered that he had come from Tian'an Temple.
translations.idiomatic: He asked where he lived; the monk answered that he had come from Tian'an Temple.

sentences.zh: 語訖，忽然不見。

translations.literal: When the talk was finished, he suddenly vanished from sight.
translations.idiomatic: When they had finished speaking, he suddenly vanished.

sentences.zh: 駿君臣以為靈感，改中興為天安寺。

translations.literal: Liu Jun and his courtiers took it as a numinous inspiration and renamed Zhongxing Temple Tian'an Temple.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Jun and his courtiers regarded it as a divine sign and renamed Zhongxing Temple Tian'an Temple.

sentences.zh: 是後七年而帝踐祚，號天安元年。

translations.literal: Seven years after this the emperor ascended the throne, and the era was named Tian'an, Year One.
translations.idiomatic: Seven years later the emperor took the throne, taking the reign title Tian'an, Year One.

sentences.zh: 是年，劉彧徐州刺史薛安都始以城地來降。

translations.literal: That year, Xue Andu, Liu Yu's regional inspector of Xuzhou, first came over in surrender with his city and territory.
translations.idiomatic: That year Xue Andu, regional inspector of Xuzhou under Liu Yu, first surrendered with his city and territory.

sentences.zh: 明年，盡有淮北之地。

translations.literal: The next year, they wholly possessed the lands north of the Huai.
translations.idiomatic: The next year the Wei wholly took possession of the lands north of the Huai.

sentences.zh: 其歲，高祖誕載。

translations.literal: That same year, Emperor Gaozu was born.
translations.idiomatic: That same year Emperor Gaozu was born.

sentences.zh: 於時起永寧寺，構七級佛圖，高三百餘尺，基架博敞，為天下第一。

translations.literal: At that time Yongning Temple was erected, with a seven-tier pagoda more than three hundred chi high; its foundation and frame were broad and spacious—the foremost in the realm.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Yongning Temple was built, with a seven-story pagoda over three hundred chi high; its foundation and frame were vast and spacious—the greatest under Heaven.

sentences.zh: 又於天宮寺，造釋迦立像。

translations.literal: At Tiangong Temple as well, a standing image of Shakyamuni was made.
translations.idiomatic: At Tiangong Temple they also cast a standing image of Shakyamuni.

sentences.zh: 高四十三尺，用赤金十萬斤，黃金六百斤。

translations.literal: It stood forty-three chi high, using one hundred thousand jin of red gold and six hundred jin of yellow gold.
translations.idiomatic: It stood forty-three chi high and consumed one hundred thousand jin of copper alloy and six hundred jin of gold.

sentences.zh: 皇興中，又構三級石佛圖。

translations.literal: In the Huangxing era, a three-tier stone pagoda was also built.
translations.idiomatic: During Huangxing, a three-tier stone pagoda was also constructed.

sentences.zh: 榱棟楣楹，上下重結，大小皆石，高十丈。

translations.literal: Rafters, beams, lintels, and columns—all bound in layers above and below, every part of stone—stood ten zhang high.
translations.idiomatic: Rafters, beams, lintels, and columns were layered one upon another, all carved from stone, ten zhang high.

sentences.zh: 鎮固巧密，為京華壯觀。

translations.literal: Solid, cunningly wrought and finely dense, it was a magnificent sight of the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Solid and exquisitely crafted, it was a grand spectacle of the capital.

sentences.zh: 高祖踐位，顯祖移御北苑崇光宮，覽習玄籍。

translations.literal: When Emperor Gaozu ascended the throne, Emperor Xianzu moved his residence to Chongguang Palace in the northern park and perused and studied abstruse texts.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Gaozu came to the throne, Emperor Xianzu moved to Chongguang Palace in the northern park to study abstruse texts.

sentences.zh: 建鹿野佛圖於苑中之西山，去崇光右十里，巖房禪堂，禪僧居其中焉。

translations.literal: A Deer Park pagoda was built on the western hill within the park, ten li to the right of Chongguang; cliff chambers and meditation halls stood there, with meditation monks dwelling within.
translations.idiomatic: On the western hill within the park he built the Deer Park pagoda, ten li east of Chongguang; cliff chambers and meditation halls were built there, and meditation monks dwelt within.

sentences.zh: 延興二年夏四月，詔曰：「比丘不在寺舍，遊涉村落，交通姦猾，經歷年歲。

translations.literal: In the fourth month of summer in the second year of Yanxing, an edict said: "Bhikkhus have not remained in monastic quarters but wander through villages, mixing with the crafty and devious, and this has gone on for years.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month of summer, Yanxing year 2, an edict said: "Bhikkhus have not remained in their monasteries but roam through villages, consorting with the crafty and dishonest, and this has gone on for years.

sentences.zh: 令民間五五相保，不得容止。

translations.literal: Order the people to guarantee one another in groups of five, and they shall not give them lodging.
translations.idiomatic: Households shall guarantee one another in groups of five, and none shall give them shelter.

sentences.zh: 無籍之僧，精加隱括，有者送付州鎮，其在畿郡，送付本曹。

translations.literal: Monks without registry shall be rigorously investigated; those found shall be sent to their provincial garrisons, and in the capital districts, to the responsible bureau.
translations.idiomatic: Unregistered monks shall be rigorously sought out; those found shall be sent to provincial garrisons, and in the capital districts to the responsible bureau.

sentences.zh: 若為三寶巡民教化者，在外齎州鎮維那文移，在臺者齎都維那等印牒，然後聽行。

translations.literal: If they travel among the people to teach in behalf of the Three Treasures, those outside the capital shall carry writs from the provincial or garrison sangha overseers; those at court shall carry sealed passes from the chief sangha overseer and others—only then may they proceed.
translations.idiomatic: If they travel to preach the Dharma on behalf of the Three Treasures, those in the provinces shall carry writs from sangha overseers, and those at court sealed passes from the chief sangha overseer—only then may they travel.

sentences.zh: 違者加罪。」

translations.literal: Violators shall be punished."
translations.idiomatic: Violators shall be punished."

sentences.zh: 又詔曰：「內外之人，興建福業，造立圖寺，高敞顯博，亦足以輝隆至教矣。

translations.literal: An edict also said: "People within and without, in raising meritorious works and building pagodas and temples—grand, spacious, and imposing—do enough to glorify and exalt the supreme teaching.
translations.idiomatic: Another edict said: "People everywhere, in raising meritorious works and building pagodas and temples—grand and imposing—do enough to glorify the supreme teaching.

sentences.zh: 然無知之徒，各相高尚，貧富相競，費竭財產，務存高廣，傷殺昆蟲含生之類。

translations.literal: Yet the ignorant vie with one another in ostentation; rich and poor compete, exhausting their property to make things ever loftier and broader, killing insects and all creatures that bear life.
translations.idiomatic: Yet the ignorant vie in ostentation; rich and poor compete, exhausting their wealth to build ever higher and broader, killing insects and every living creature.

sentences.zh: 苟能精致，累土聚沙，福鍾不朽。

translations.literal: If one can be refined and meticulous, piling earth and gathering sand, merit will endure unfading.
translations.idiomatic: If one is refined and sincere, even piling earth and gathering sand will forge merit that endures forever.

sentences.zh: 欲建為福之因，未知傷生之業。

translations.literal: They wish to plant causes of merit, yet do not realize the karma of harming life.
translations.idiomatic: They seek to lay the seeds of merit, unaware of the karma of taking life.

sentences.zh: 朕為民父母，慈養是務。

translations.literal: I am the parent of the people; nurturing them with compassion is my task.
translations.idiomatic: As parent of the people, my task is to nurture them with compassion.

sentences.zh: 自今一切斷之。」

translations.literal: From now on, all of this is forbidden."
translations.idiomatic: From now on, all of this is forbidden."

sentences.zh: 又詔曰：「夫信誠則應遠，行篤則感深，歷觀先世靈瑞，乃有禽獸易色，草木移性。

translations.literal: Another edict said: "Where faith is sincere, responses reach far; where conduct is steadfast, stirrings run deep. Looking back at numinous omens of former ages, there have been birds and beasts changing color and grasses and trees shifting nature.
translations.idiomatic: Another edict said: "Where faith is sincere, blessings reach far; where conduct is devout, stirrings run deep. Looking back at numinous omens of former ages, birds and beasts changed color and grasses and trees shifted nature.

sentences.zh: 濟州東平郡，靈像發輝，變成金銅之色。

translations.literal: In Dongping Commandery of Jizhou, a numinous image radiated light and turned to the color of gold and bronze.
translations.idiomatic: In Dongping Commandery, Jizhou, a numinous image radiated light and turned gold-bronze in color.

sentences.zh: 殊常之事，絕於往古；

translations.literal: An extraordinary event, unmatched since antiquity;
translations.idiomatic: An event without parallel since antiquity;

sentences.zh: 熙隆妙法，理在當今。

translations.literal: the flourishing splendor of the wondrous Dharma rightly belongs to the present age.
translations.idiomatic: the flourishing splendor of the wondrous Dharma belongs to the present age.

sentences.zh: 有司與沙門統曇曜令州送像達都，使道俗咸覩實相之容，普告天下，皆使聞知。」

translations.literal: The responsible offices together with the shramana director Tanyao shall order the province to send the image to the capital, so that clergy and laity alike may behold the true form, and proclaim it throughout the realm so that all may hear and know."
translations.idiomatic: The responsible offices, together with sangha director Tanyao, shall order the province to send the image to the capital, so clergy and laity alike may behold its true form, and announce it throughout the realm for all to hear."

sentences.zh: 三年十二月，顯祖因田鷹獲鴛鴦一，其偶悲鳴，上下不去。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month of the third year, while hawking in the fields, Emperor Xianzu caught a mandarin duck; its mate wailed in grief and circled above and below, refusing to leave.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month of year 3, while hawking, Emperor Xianzu caught a mandarin duck; its mate cried mournfully and circled overhead, refusing to leave.

sentences.zh: 帝乃惕然，問左右曰：「此飛鳴者，為雌為雄？」

translations.literal: The emperor grew alert and uneasy, and asked those beside him: "Of this bird crying in flight—is it female or male?"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor grew troubled and asked his attendants: "This bird crying as it flies—is it female or male?"

sentences.zh: 左右對曰：「臣以為雌。」

translations.literal: Those beside him answered: "Your servant takes it to be the female."
translations.idiomatic: His attendants answered: "Your servant believes it is the female."

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「何以知？」

translations.literal: The emperor said: "How do you know?"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor asked: "How do you know?"

sentences.zh: 對曰：「陽性剛，陰性柔，以剛柔推之，必是雌矣。」

translations.literal: They answered: "The yang nature is hard, the yin nature soft; judging by hard and soft, it must be the female."
translations.idiomatic: They answered: "Yang is hard and yin is soft; by that reasoning, it must be the female."

sentences.zh: 帝乃慨然而歎曰：「雖人鳥事別，至於資識性情，竟何異哉！」

translations.literal: The emperor sighed deeply and said: "Though the affairs of humans and birds differ, in their innate awareness and emotional nature, how are they ultimately different!"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor sighed and said: "Though the affairs of humans and birds differ, in awareness and feeling, how are they ultimately different!"

sentences.zh: 於是下詔，禁斷鷙鳥，不得畜焉。

translations.literal: Thereupon he issued an edict forbidding raptors; they were not to be kept.
translations.idiomatic: He then issued an edict forbidding the keeping of birds of prey.

sentences.zh: 承明元年八月，高祖於永寧寺，設太法供，度良家男女為僧尼者百有餘人，帝為剃髮，施以僧服，令修道戒，資福於顯祖。

translations.literal: In the eighth month of Chengming year 1, at Yongning Temple Emperor Gaozu set out a great dharma offering and tonsured more than a hundred sons and daughters of good families as monks and nuns; the emperor personally shaved their heads, gave them monastic robes, and had them observe the precepts, accruing merit for Emperor Xianzu.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month of Chengming 1, at Yongning Temple Emperor Gaozu held a great dharma offering and tonsured more than one hundred sons and daughters of good families as monks and nuns; the emperor shaved their heads himself, clothed them in robes, and had them observe the precepts for the merit of Emperor Xianzu.

sentences.zh: 是月，又詔起建明寺。

translations.literal: That same month, an edict also ordered the building of Jianming Temple.
translations.idiomatic: That month an edict also ordered Jianming Temple built.

sentences.zh: 太和元年二月，幸永寧寺設齋，赦死罪囚。

translations.literal: In the second month of Taihe year 1, he visited Yongning Temple to hold a fast and pardoned prisoners condemned to death.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month of Taihe 1, he visited Yongning Temple for a fast and pardoned prisoners under sentence of death.

sentences.zh: 三月，又幸永寧寺設會，行道聽講，命中、祕二省與僧徒討論佛義，施僧衣服、寶器有差。

translations.literal: In the third month he again visited Yongning Temple for an assembly, circumambulating, chanting, and listening to lectures; he ordered the Central and Secretarial Secretariats to debate Buddhist doctrine with the monks, bestowing robes and precious vessels in graded measure.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month he again visited Yongning Temple for an assembly of chanting and sermons, and ordered the Central and Secretarial Secretariats to debate Buddhist doctrine with the monks, granting robes and precious vessels in graded amounts.

sentences.zh: 又於方山太祖營壘之處，建思遠寺。

translations.literal: At Mount Fang, where the Grand Ancestor had encamped, Siyuan Temple was also built.
translations.idiomatic: At Mount Fang, where the Grand Ancestor had once encamped, he also built Siyuan Temple.

sentences.zh: 自興光至此，[20]京城內寺新舊且百所，僧尼二千餘人，四方諸寺六千四百七十八，僧尼七萬七千二百五十八人。

translations.literal: From Xingguang down to this time,[20] old and new temples within the capital numbered nearly a hundred, with more than two thousand monks and nuns; temples throughout the realm numbered six thousand four hundred seventy-eight, with seventy-seven thousand two hundred fifty-eight monks and nuns.
translations.idiomatic: From the Xingguang era to this time,[20] old and new temples in the capital numbered nearly one hundred, with more than two thousand monks and nuns; temples throughout the realm numbered 6,478, with 77,258 monks and nuns.

sentences.zh: 四年春，詔以鷹師為報德寺。

translations.literal: In the spring of the fourth year, an edict converted the falconers' compound into Baode Temple.
translations.idiomatic: In spring of year 4, an edict converted the falconers' compound into Baode Temple.

sentences.zh: [21]九年秋，有司奏，上谷郡比丘尼惠香，在北山松樹下死，屍形不壞。

translations.literal: [21] In the autumn of the ninth year, the responsible offices memorialized: the bhikkhuni Huixiang of Shanggu Commandery died beneath a pine on the northern hill, and her corpse did not decay.
translations.idiomatic: [21] In the autumn of year 9, the offices reported: the bhikkhuni Huixiang of Shanggu Commandery died beneath a pine on the northern hill, and her corpse did not decay.

sentences.zh: 爾來三年，士女觀者有千百。

translations.literal: In the three years since, men and women who came to view her numbered in the thousands.
translations.idiomatic: In the three years since, thousands of men and women came to see her.

sentences.zh: 於時人皆異之。

translations.literal: At the time all regarded it as extraordinary.
translations.idiomatic: At the time everyone regarded it as extraordinary.

sentences.zh: 十年冬，有司又奏：「前被敕以勒籍之初，愚民僥倖，假稱入道，以避輸課，其無籍僧尼罷遣還俗。

translations.literal: In the winter of the tenth year, the offices again memorialized: "Previously, when ordered to compile the registry at the outset, foolish commoners took advantage, falsely claiming entrance into the Way to evade tax and corvée; monks and nuns without registry were dismissed and returned to lay status.
translations.idiomatic: In winter of year 10, the offices again reported: "Previously, when ordered to compile the registry, commoners took advantage by falsely entering the clergy to evade taxes and corvée; unregistered monks and nuns were dismissed and returned to lay life.

sentences.zh: 重被旨，所檢僧尼，寺主、維那當寺隱審。

translations.literal: Again receiving the imperial order, of the monks and nuns inspected, the abbot and sangha overseer of each temple shall conduct a secret review on site.
translations.idiomatic: Under renewed orders, the monks and nuns under review were to be secretly vetted on site by each temple's abbot and sangha overseer.

sentences.zh: 其有道行精勤者，聽仍在道；

translations.literal: Those of genuine conduct and diligent practice were permitted to remain in orders;
translations.idiomatic: Those of genuine virtue and diligent practice were allowed to remain in orders;

sentences.zh: 為行凡粗者，有籍無籍，悉罷歸齊民。

translations.literal: those of vulgar and crude conduct, whether registered or not, were all dismissed and returned to ordinary people.
translations.idiomatic: those of vulgar conduct, registered or not, were all dismissed and returned to ordinary subjecthood.

sentences.zh: 今依旨簡遣，其諸州還俗者，僧尼合一千三百二十七人。」

translations.literal: Now, in accordance with the order, after review and dismissal, monks and nuns returned to lay life in the various provinces totaled one thousand three hundred twenty-seven."
translations.idiomatic: Following the order, monks and nuns returned to lay life across the provinces totaled 1,327."

sentences.zh: 奏可。

translations.literal: The memorial was approved.
translations.idiomatic: The memorial was approved.

sentences.zh: 十六年詔：「四月八日、七月十五日，聽大州度一百人為僧尼，中州五十人，下州二十人，以為常準，著於令。」

translations.literal: In the sixteenth year an edict said: "On the eighth day of the fourth month and the fifteenth day of the seventh month, large provinces may tonsure one hundred persons as monks and nuns, medium provinces fifty, small provinces twenty—this shall be the standing norm, written into the statutes."
translations.idiomatic: In year 16 an edict said: "On the eighth day of the fourth month and the fifteenth day of the seventh month, large provinces may tonsure 100 persons as monks and nuns, medium provinces 50, and small provinces 20—this shall be the standing norm, recorded in statute."

sentences.zh: 十七年，詔立僧制四十七條。

translations.literal: In the seventeenth year, an edict established forty-seven articles of monastic regulation.
translations.idiomatic: In year 17, an edict established forty-seven articles of monastic regulation.

sentences.zh: 十九年四月，帝幸徐州白塔寺。

translations.literal: In the fourth month of the nineteenth year, the emperor visited White Pagoda Temple in Xuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month of year 19, the emperor visited White Pagoda Temple in Xuzhou.

sentences.zh: 顧謂諸王及侍官曰：「此寺近有名僧嵩法師，受成實論於羅什，在此流通。

translations.literal: Turning to the princes and attendant officials he said: "Near this temple lived the renowned monk Master Song, who received the Treatise on the Completion of Truth from Kumārajīva and propagated it here.
translations.idiomatic: Turning to the princes and attendants he said: "Near this temple lived the renowned Master Song, who received the Treatise on the Completion of Truth from Kumārajīva and propagated it here.

sentences.zh: 後授淵法師，淵法師授登、紀二法師。

translations.literal: Later he transmitted it to Master Yuan, and Master Yuan transmitted it to Masters Deng and Ji.
translations.idiomatic: Later he transmitted it to Master Yuan, who transmitted it to Masters Deng and Ji.

sentences.zh: 朕每玩成實論，可以釋人染情，[22]故至此寺焉。」

translations.literal: I often cherish the Treatise on the Completion of Truth—it can release people from defiled passions,[22] and so I have come to this temple."
translations.idiomatic: I often study the Treatise on the Completion of Truth—it can release people from defiled passions,[22] and so I have come to this temple."

sentences.zh: 時沙門道登，雅有義業，為高祖眷賞，恒侍講論。

translations.literal: At that time the shramana Daodeng, possessed of elegant mastery of Buddhist doctrine, won Emperor Gaozu's fond esteem and constantly attended him for lecturing and debate.
translations.idiomatic: At that time the monk Daodeng, a master of Buddhist doctrine, won Emperor Gaozu's esteem and constantly attended him in lecture and debate.

sentences.zh: 曾於禁內與帝夜談，同見一鬼。

translations.literal: Once, within the palace precincts, he talked with the emperor by night and they together saw a ghost.
translations.idiomatic: Once, within the palace, he talked with the emperor by night and they both saw a ghost.

sentences.zh: 二十年卒，高祖甚悼惜之，詔施帛一千匹。

translations.literal: In the twentieth year he died; Emperor Gaozu greatly mourned and lamented him, and ordered a gift of one thousand bolts of silk.
translations.idiomatic: In year 20 he died; Emperor Gaozu greatly mourned him and ordered a gift of one thousand bolts of silk.

sentences.zh: 又設一切僧齋，并命京城七日行道。

translations.literal: A great feast for all monks was also held, and the capital was ordered to perform ritual circumambulation for seven days.
translations.idiomatic: He also held a feast for all monks and ordered seven days of ritual chanting throughout the capital.

sentences.zh: 又詔：「朕師登法師奄至徂背，痛怛摧慟，不能已已。

translations.literal: An edict also said: "My teacher Master Deng has suddenly reached his end; anguish crushes me and grief will not cease.
translations.idiomatic: An edict also said: "My teacher Master Deng has suddenly passed away; grief overwhelms me and will not cease.

sentences.zh: 比藥治慎喪，未容即赴，便準師義，哭諸門外。」

translations.literal: For the moment, while taking medicine and observing funeral restraint, I cannot go at once; I shall therefore follow my teacher's teaching and weep outside the gates."
translations.idiomatic: As I am taking medicine and observing mourning restraint, I cannot go at once; I shall follow my teacher's teaching and weep outside the gates."

sentences.zh: 緇素榮之。

translations.literal: Clergy and laity alike honored this.
translations.idiomatic: Clergy and laity alike honored this.

sentences.zh: [23]又有西域沙門名跋陀，有道業，深為高祖所敬信。

translations.literal: [23] There was also a Western Regions shramana named Batuo, of accomplished way and merit, deeply honored and trusted by Emperor Gaozu.
translations.idiomatic: [23] There was also a Western Regions monk named Batuo, accomplished in the Way, deeply honored and trusted by Emperor Gaozu.

sentences.zh: 詔於少室山陰，立少林寺而居之，公給衣供。

translations.literal: An edict ordered Shaolin Temple established on the northern slope of Mount Shaoshi for him to dwell in; the state supplied food and robes.
translations.idiomatic: An edict ordered Shaolin Temple built on the northern slope of Mount Shaoshi for his residence, with state provision of food and robes.

sentences.zh: 二十一年五月，詔曰：「羅什法師可謂神出五才，志入四行者也。

translations.literal: In the fifth month of the twenty-first year, an edict said: "Master Kumārajīva may be called one whose spirit surpasses the five talents and whose resolve enters the four practices.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month of year 21, an edict said: "Master Kumārajīva may be called one whose spirit surpasses all five talents and whose resolve fulfills the four practices.

sentences.zh: 今常住寺，猶有遺地，欽悅修蹤，情深遐遠，可於舊堂所，為建三級浮圖。

translations.literal: Now at Changzhu Temple there is still surviving land; in reverent delight at his cultivated traces and with affection deep and far-reaching, a three-tier pagoda may be built at the site of his old hall.
translations.idiomatic: At Changzhu Temple surviving land remains; in reverence for his cultivated path, a three-tier pagoda shall be built at the site of his old hall.

sentences.zh: 又見逼昏虐，為道殄軀，既暫同俗禮，應有子胤，可推訪以聞，當加叙接。」

translations.literal: Also, seeing that he was driven by a brutal age and gave his body for the Way, and had briefly conformed to lay custom, he ought to have descendants; they may be sought out and reported, and shall receive favor and support."
translations.idiomatic: He was harried by a brutal age and gave his life for the Way; having briefly followed lay custom, he ought to have descendants—seek them out and report, and they shall receive favor."

sentences.zh: 先是，立監福曹，又改為昭玄，備有官屬，以斷僧務。

translations.literal: Previously the Directorate of Monastic Blessings had been established, then renamed Zhaoxuan, fully staffed with officials to adjudicate monastic affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Previously the Directorate of Monastic Blessings was established, then renamed Zhaoxuan, fully staffed to adjudicate monastic affairs.

sentences.zh: 高祖時，沙門道順、惠覺、僧意、惠紀、僧範、道弁、惠度、智誕、僧顯、僧義、僧利，並以義行知重。

translations.literal: In Emperor Gaozu's time, shramanas Daoshun, Huijue, Sengyi, Huiji, Sengfan, Daobian, Huidu, Zhidan, Sengxian, Sengyi, and Sengli were all honored for their mastery of doctrine and conduct.
translations.idiomatic: During Emperor Gaozu's reign, monks Daoshun, Huijue, Sengyi, Huiji, Sengfan, Daobian, Huidu, Zhidan, Sengxian, Sengyi, and Sengli were all honored for doctrine and conduct.

sentences.zh: 世宗即位，永平元年秋，詔曰：緇素既殊，法律亦異。

translations.literal: When Emperor Shizong ascended the throne, in the autumn of Yongping year 1 an edict said: The black-robed and the white-robed are distinct, and the laws likewise differ.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xuanwu ascended the throne, in autumn of Yongping 1 an edict said: Clergy and laity are distinct, and the laws likewise differ.

sentences.zh: 故道教彰於互顯，[24]禁勸各有所宜。

translations.literal: Therefore the Buddhist teaching manifests in mutual illumination,[24] and prohibitions and exhortations each suit their place.
translations.idiomatic: Therefore the Buddhist teaching manifests across the visible and invisible realms,[24] and prohibitions and encouragements each suit their place.

sentences.zh: 自今已後，眾僧犯殺人已上罪者，仍依俗斷，餘犯悉付昭玄，以內律僧制治之。

translations.literal: From now on, when monks commit crimes of murder and above, they shall still be judged by secular law; all other offenses shall be handed to Zhaoxuan and adjudicated under the internal Vinaya and monastic regulations.
translations.idiomatic: From now on, monks who commit murder or greater crimes shall still be judged under secular law; all other offenses shall go to Zhaoxuan for adjudication under Vinaya and monastic regulations.

sentences.zh: [25]二年冬，沙門統惠深上言：「僧尼浩曠，清濁混流，不遵禁典，精粗莫別。

translations.literal: [25] In the winter of the second year, the shramana director Huishen submitted: "Monks and nuns are vast in number; the pure and the foul mingle; they do not observe the prohibitory codes, and the refined cannot be distinguished from the coarse.
translations.idiomatic: [25] In winter of year 2, sangha director Huishen submitted: "Monks and nuns are vast in number; the pure and corrupt mingle; they do not observe the codes, and the worthy cannot be distinguished from the unworthy.

sentences.zh: 輒與經律法師群議立制：諸州、鎮、郡維那、上坐、寺主，各令戒律自修，咸依內禁，若不解律者，退其本次。

translations.literal: I have accordingly conferred with Vinaya masters to establish regulations: sangha overseers, senior seats, and abbots of provinces, garrisons, and commanderies shall each be ordered to cultivate the precepts themselves and all conform to internal prohibitions; those who do not understand the Vinaya shall be removed from their rank.
translations.idiomatic: I have met with Vinaya masters to establish regulations: sangha overseers, senior seats, and abbots in provinces, garrisons, and commanderies must each keep the precepts and obey internal regulations; those who do not know the Vinaya shall be demoted.

sentences.zh: 又，出家之人，不應犯法，積八不淨物。

translations.literal: Further, those who leave home should not break the law by amassing the eight kinds of impure possessions.
translations.idiomatic: Further, those who leave home must not break the law by amassing the eight impure possessions.

sentences.zh: 然經律所制，通塞有方。

translations.literal: Yet what the sutras and Vinaya prescribe has its methods of permitting and forbidding.
translations.idiomatic: Yet what sutras and Vinaya prescribe allows for flexibility in what is permitted and forbidden.

sentences.zh: 依律，車牛淨人，[26]不淨之物，不得為己私畜。

translations.literal: According to the Vinaya, carts, oxen, menials,[26] and impure possessions may not be kept for private use.
translations.idiomatic: Under the Vinaya, carts, oxen, temple servants,[26] and impure goods may not be kept for private use.

sentences.zh: 唯有老病年六十以上者，限聽一乘。

translations.literal: Only for the aged and ill of sixty years and above is one mount permitted as a limit.
translations.idiomatic: Only for the aged and ill sixty and above is one mount permitted.

sentences.zh: 又，比來僧尼，或因三寶，出貸私財。

translations.literal: Further, recently monks and nuns have, using the Three Treasures as pretext, lent out private wealth beyond provincial borders.
translations.idiomatic: Further, recently monks and nuns have lent out private wealth beyond provincial borders under cover of the Three Treasures.

sentences.zh: 緣州外。

translations.literal: From now on this is forbidden.
translations.idiomatic: From now on this is forbidden.

sentences.zh: [27]又，出家捨著，本無凶儀，不應廢道從俗。

translations.literal: [27] Further, those who leave home and put on the robes originally have no mourning rites; they should not abandon the Way to follow custom.
translations.idiomatic: [27] Further, those who leave home originally have no mourning rites; they must not abandon the Way to follow lay custom.

sentences.zh: 其父母三師，遠聞凶問，聽哭三日。

translations.literal: For parents and the three teachers, if mourning news arrives from afar, weeping for three days is permitted.
translations.idiomatic: For parents and the three teachers, if death news arrives from afar, weeping for three days is permitted.

sentences.zh: 若在見前，限以七日。

translations.literal: If present at the death, the limit is seven days.
translations.idiomatic: If present at the death, the limit is seven days.

sentences.zh: 或有不安寺舍，遊止民間，亂道生過，皆由此等。

translations.literal: Some who do not settle in monastic quarters wander and lodge among the people—disorder in the Way and offenses arise, all from such persons.
translations.idiomatic: Some who fail to settle in monasteries lodge among the people—disorder and offenses in the Way arise from such persons.

sentences.zh: 若有犯者，脫服還民。

translations.literal: If any violate this, they shall remove their robes and return to lay status.
translations.idiomatic: Violators shall remove their robes and return to lay life.

sentences.zh: 其有造寺者，限僧五十以上，啟聞聽造。

translations.literal: Those who would build a temple are limited to cases with fifty or more monks; they must report and receive permission before building.
translations.idiomatic: To build a temple requires fifty or more monks; one must report and receive permission to build.

sentences.zh: 若有輒營置者，處以違敕之罪，其寺僧眾擯出外州。

translations.literal: If any erect one on their own authority, they shall be punished for violating an edict, and the monks of that temple shall be expelled to outer provinces.
translations.idiomatic: Unauthorized construction shall be punished as violation of an edict, and that temple's monks shall be expelled to outer provinces.

sentences.zh: [28]僧尼之法，不得為俗人所使。

translations.literal: [28] By the law for monks and nuns, they may not be employed by lay people.
translations.idiomatic: [28] By monastic law, monks and nuns may not serve lay people.

sentences.zh: 若有犯者，還配本屬。

translations.literal: Violators shall be returned and assigned to their home jurisdiction.
translations.idiomatic: Violators shall be returned to their home jurisdiction.

sentences.zh: 其外國僧尼來歸化者，求精檢有德行合三藏者聽住，若無德行，遣還本國，若其不去，依此僧制治罪。」

translations.literal: Foreign monks and nuns who come to submit to our civilization—if upon rigorous inspection they possess virtue and are versed in the Tripitaka, they may remain; if lacking virtue, they shall be sent back to their homeland; if they refuse to leave, they shall be punished under these monastic regulations."
translations.idiomatic: Foreign monks and nuns who come to submit—if found virtuous and versed in the Tripitaka, they may stay; if lacking virtue, send them home; if they refuse to leave, punish them under these regulations."

sentences.zh: 詔從之。

translations.literal: The edict approved it.
translations.idiomatic: The edict approved it.

sentences.zh: 先是，於恒農荊山造珉玉丈六像一。

translations.literal: Previously, a sixteen-foot image of fine jade was made at Jing Mountain in Hengnong.
translations.idiomatic: Previously, a sixteen-foot image of fine jade was made at Jing Mountain in Hengnong.

sentences.zh: 三年冬，迎置於洛濱之報德寺，世宗躬觀致敬。

translations.literal: In the winter of the third year it was brought and installed at Baode Temple on the Luo riverbank; Emperor Shizong personally viewed it and paid reverence.
translations.idiomatic: In winter of year 3 it was installed at Baode Temple on the Luo embankment; Emperor Xuanwu viewed it in person and paid reverence.

sentences.zh: 四年夏，詔曰：「僧祇之粟，本期濟施，儉年出貸，豐則收入。

translations.literal: In the summer of the fourth year an edict said: "Sangha grain was originally intended for relief and giving; in lean years it is lent out, in plentiful years it is collected in.
translations.idiomatic: In summer of year 4 an edict said: "Sangha grain was originally meant for charity; in lean years it is lent out, in abundant years it is collected in.

sentences.zh: 山林僧尼，隨以給施；

translations.literal: Monks and nuns dwelling in mountain forests were likewise granted provisions;
translations.idiomatic: Monks and nuns in remote mountain monasteries were likewise granted their share of the grain;

sentences.zh: 民有窘弊，亦即賑之。

translations.literal: When the people suffered distress and hardship, [grain] was also used to relieve them.
translations.idiomatic: When commoners fell into want and hardship, they too were supported from the fund.

sentences.zh: 但主司冒利，規取贏息，及其徵責，不計水旱，或償利過本，或翻改券契，侵蠹貧下，莫知紀極。

translations.literal: But the officials in charge coveted profit, scheming to extract surplus interest; when they collected debts they reckoned neither flood nor drought; sometimes interest repaid exceeded the principal, sometimes initial contracts were reversed and rewritten; they wormed into and devoured the poor below, without limit or measure.
translations.idiomatic: But the officials in charge chased profit and extracted exorbitant interest. When they pressed for repayment they took no account of flood or drought; sometimes interest payments exceeded the principal, sometimes original loan contracts were torn up and rewritten. They preyed upon the poor without limit.

sentences.zh: 細民嗟毒，歲月滋深。

translations.literal: Petty people lamented in bitterness; month and year it grew deeper.
translations.idiomatic: The suffering of humble folk deepened with every passing year.

sentences.zh: 非所以矜此窮乏，宗尚慈拯之本意也。

translations.literal: This is not the means to pity these poor and destitute—it misses the original purpose of esteeming and upholding compassionate rescue.
translations.idiomatic: This was far from the original intent of cherishing the destitute and upholding compassionate relief.

sentences.zh: 自今已後，不得專委維那、都尉，[29]可令刺史共加監括。

translations.literal: From today onward, [the matter] may not be entrusted solely to chief stewards and commandants;[29] let prefects jointly add supervisory inspection.
translations.idiomatic: Henceforth the fund shall not be left entirely to monastery stewards and commandants;[29] prefects shall jointly supervise and audit the accounts.

sentences.zh: 尚書檢諸有僧祇穀之處，州別列其元數，出入贏息，賑給多少，并貸償歲月，見在未收，上臺錄記。

translations.literal: The Ministry of State Affairs shall inspect all places with sangha-grain stores; each province shall separately list its original amounts, income and surplus interest, how much was distributed in relief, and the year and month of lending and repayment; what remains uncollected shall be recorded and reported upward.
translations.idiomatic: The Ministry shall inspect every district maintaining sangha-grain reserves. Each province shall report original quantities, income and surplus interest, amounts disbursed for relief, and the dates of all loans and repayments; outstanding balances shall be registered and submitted to the capital.

sentences.zh: 若收利過本，及翻改初券，依律免之，勿復徵責。

translations.literal: If interest collected exceeded the principal, or the initial contract was reversed and rewritten, according to law they are exempt—do not collect further demands.
translations.idiomatic: Where interest has exceeded principal or initial contracts were illegally altered, the debtors shall be released by law and no further collection permitted.

sentences.zh: 或有私債，轉施償僧，即以丐民，不聽收檢。

translations.literal: If there were private debts transferred and assigned to repay monks, they were then applied to beggar-commoners; [such debts] may not be collected or seized.
translations.idiomatic: Private debts reassigned to monks for collection and then applied against the poor shall not be enforced.

sentences.zh: 後有出貸，先盡貧窮，徵債之科，一準舊格。

translations.literal: For future lending, the destitute and poor come first; the standards for debt collection follow the old regulations entirely.
translations.idiomatic: Future loans shall go first to the truly impoverished; debt collection shall follow existing regulations to the letter.

sentences.zh: 富有之家，不聽輒貸。

translations.literal: Wealthy households may not be lent to at will.
translations.idiomatic: Wealthy families may not receive loans.

sentences.zh: 脫仍冒濫，依法治罪。」

translations.literal: If they still fraudulently abuse [the system], punish according to law.'
translations.idiomatic: Anyone who continues to abuse the system shall be punished according to law."

sentences.zh: 又尚書令高肇奏言：「謹案：故沙門統曇曜，昔於承明元年，奏涼州軍戶趙苟子等二百家為僧祇戶，立課積粟，擬濟飢年，不限道俗，皆以拯施。

translations.literal: Again, Minister of State Affairs Gao Zhao memorialized: 'Carefully investigated: the late Supervisor of Monks Tan Yao, in the past in the first year of Chengming, memorialized that two hundred households of military registrants including Zhao Gouzi of Liang Province be made sangha-grain households, establishing tax levies to accumulate grain, intending to relieve famine years—without distinction of clergy or laity, all were to be saved and bestowed.
translations.idiomatic: Minister of State Affairs Gao Zhao also submitted a memorial: "Upon investigation: the late Supervisor of Monks Tan Yao, in the first year of the Chengming reign, had recommended that two hundred military-registration households in Liang Province, including Zhao Gouzi and others, be registered as sangha-grain households, with taxes levied to accumulate grain for famine relief—open to both clergy and laity alike.

sentences.zh: 又依內律，僧祇戶不得別屬一寺。

translations.literal: Again, according to internal monastic law, sangha-grain households may not be separately attached to a single monastery.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, under internal monastic law, sangha-grain households could not be assigned exclusively to any single monastery.

sentences.zh: 而都維那僧暹、僧頻等，進違成旨，退乖內法，肆意任情，奏求逼召，致使吁嗟之怨，盈於行道，棄子傷生，自縊溺死，五十餘人。

translations.literal: Yet chief stewards the monks Xian and Pin and others, advancing violated the established decree, retreating contravened internal law, acted willfully according to whim, memorialized and sought forced summons, causing lamentation and resentment to fill the roads, children abandoned and lives harmed, self-strangulation and drowning—more than fifty persons.
translations.idiomatic: Yet the chief stewards, the monks Xian and Pin, and others defied the imperial decree and violated monastic law. Acting on whim, they petitioned for forced conscription, provoking such anguish that the roads rang with lamentation—children were abandoned, lives were lost, and more than fifty people hanged or drowned themselves.

sentences.zh: 豈是仰贊聖明慈育之意，深失陛下歸依之心。

translations.literal: How could this uphold the meaning of the sage's bright compassionate nurture, or deeply fulfill Your Majesty's heart of refuge and reliance?
translations.idiomatic: Surely this could not honor the sage emperor's intent of compassionate nurture, nor satisfy Your Majesty's devotion to the faith.

sentences.zh: 遂令此等，行號巷哭，叫訴無所，至乃白羽貫耳，列訟宮闕。

translations.literal: Thus these people went crying through the lanes, with nowhere to plead; some pierced their ears with white feathers and lined up to sue at the palace gates.
translations.idiomatic: These people took to the streets wailing, with nowhere to turn for redress; some thrust white feathers through their ears and queued before the palace gates to petition.

sentences.zh: 悠悠之人，尚為哀痛，況慈悲之士，而可安之。

translations.literal: Even indifferent people were moved to sorrow—how much more so men of compassion, who could rest content?
translations.idiomatic: Even the indifferent were moved to grief—how could men of compassion remain unmoved?

sentences.zh: 請聽苟子等還鄉課輸，儉乏之年，周給貧寡，若有不虞，以擬邊捍。

translations.literal: I request that Gouzi and the others be allowed to return to their native districts to pay taxes and levies; in years of scarcity, [grain] should be distributed to the poor and destitute; if unforeseen events arise, let it serve to support frontier defense.
translations.idiomatic: I ask that Gouzi and the others be permitted to return home and resume tax payments; in lean years the grain should relieve the poor and needy, and in emergencies it may be used to support frontier defense.

sentences.zh: 其暹等違旨背律，謬奏之愆，請付昭玄，依僧律推處。」

translations.literal: As for Xian and the others, who violated the decree and contravened the law in their erroneous memorial—their fault should be referred to the Bureau of Monastic Affairs and adjudicated according to monastic law.'
translations.idiomatic: As for Xian and his associates, who defied the decree and violated the law in their wrongful petition, I ask that the case be referred to the Bureau of Monastic Affairs for adjudication under monastic law."

sentences.zh: 詔曰：「暹等特可原之，餘如奏。」

translations.literal: The edict said: 'Xian and the others are specially pardoned; the rest as memorialized.'
translations.idiomatic: The edict replied: "Xian and the others are specially pardoned; the remainder as submitted."

sentences.zh: 世宗篤好佛理，每年常於禁中，親講經論，廣集名僧，標明義旨。

translations.literal: Emperor Shizong was deeply devoted to Buddhist doctrine; every year within the palace he personally lectured on sutras and treatises, broadly gathering eminent monks to clarify the meaning and purport.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Shizong was deeply devoted to Buddhist doctrine. Each year within the palace he personally expounded sutras and treatises, gathering eminent monks to clarify their meaning.

sentences.zh: 沙門條錄，為內起居焉。

translations.literal: Records of monks served as inner household registers.
translations.idiomatic: Registers of monks served as the inner court's household rolls.

sentences.zh: 上既崇之，下彌企尚。

translations.literal: Since the ruler above honored it, those below all the more looked up and esteemed it.
translations.idiomatic: With the emperor above honoring the faith, those below looked up to it all the more.

sentences.zh: 至延昌中，天下州郡僧尼寺，[30]積有一萬三千七百二十七所，徒侶逾眾。

translations.literal: By the Yanchang period, Buddhist and monastic temples throughout the empire's provinces and commanderies[30] numbered thirteen thousand seven hundred and twenty-seven in all, with disciples exceeding the multitude.
translations.idiomatic: By the Yanchang period, Buddhist temples and nunneries throughout the empire's provinces and commanderies[30] totaled 13,727, with monastics far outnumbering the laity.

sentences.zh: 熙平元年，詔遣沙門惠生使西域，採諸經律。

translations.literal: In the first year of Xiping, an edict dispatched the monk Huisheng as envoy to the Western Regions to collect various sutras and vinaya texts.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Xiping, an edict dispatched the monk Huisheng as envoy to the Western Regions to collect sutras and vinaya texts.

sentences.zh: 正光三年冬，還京師。

translations.literal: In the winter of the third year of Zhengguang, he returned to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: In the winter of the third year of Zhengguang, he returned to the capital.

sentences.zh: 所得經論一百七十部，行於世。

translations.literal: The sutras and treatises obtained—one hundred and seventy works in all—circulated in the world.
translations.idiomatic: The one hundred and seventy sutras and treatises he brought back circulated throughout the realm.

sentences.zh: 二年春，靈太后令曰：「年常度僧，依限大州應百人者，州郡於前十日解送三百人，其中州二百人，小州一百人。

translations.literal: In the spring of the second year, Empress Dowager Ling ordered: 'Each year when ordaining monks, according to the quota a great province should have one hundred persons—the province and commandery ten days beforehand shall submit three hundred candidates, of whom two hundred are for a medium province and one hundred for a small province.
translations.idiomatic: In the spring of the second year, Empress Dowager Ling decreed: "For the annual ordination of monks, where a great province's quota is one hundred, the province and commandery shall ten days in advance submit three hundred candidates—two hundred for a medium province, one hundred for a small one.

sentences.zh: 州統、維那與官及精練簡取充數。

translations.literal: The provincial supervisor, chief steward, officials, and those skilled in selection shall choose to fill the quota.
translations.idiomatic: The provincial supervisor, chief steward, officials, and skilled examiners shall select candidates to fill the quota.

sentences.zh: [31]若無精行，不得濫採。

translations.literal: [31]If there is no refined conduct, they may not be recklessly chosen.
translations.idiomatic: [31]Those without genuine spiritual attainment may not be recklessly ordained.

sentences.zh: 若取非人，刺史為首，以違旨論，太守、縣令、綱僚節級連坐，統及維那移五百里外異州為僧。

translations.literal: If unworthy persons are chosen, the prefect is chief culprit and punished for violating the decree; the grand administrator, magistrate, and supervising officials are punished by degrees of joint liability; the supervisor and chief steward are transferred five hundred li outside to a different province to become monks.
translations.idiomatic: If unworthy candidates are selected, the prefect bears primary responsibility for violating the decree; the grand administrator, magistrate, and supervising officials are punished by degrees of joint liability; the supervisor and chief steward are transferred five hundred li to another province and ordained as monks.

sentences.zh: 自今奴婢悉不聽出家，諸王及親貴，亦不得輒啟請。

translations.literal: From now on male and female slaves are altogether forbidden to leave home and become monks or nuns; princes and the imperial kin likewise may not casually petition [for their ordination].
translations.idiomatic: Henceforth male and female slaves are altogether forbidden to take monastic vows; princes and the imperial kin may not casually petition for their ordination.

sentences.zh: 有犯者，以違旨論。

translations.literal: If there are violators, punish for violating the decree.
translations.idiomatic: Violators shall be punished for defying the imperial decree.

sentences.zh: 其僧尼輒度他人奴婢者，亦移五百里外為僧。

translations.literal: Monks or nuns who casually ordain others' male or female slaves are likewise transferred five hundred li outside to become monks.
translations.idiomatic: Monks or nuns who ordain others' slaves without authorization are likewise transferred five hundred li and ordained as monks.

sentences.zh: 僧尼多養親識及他人奴婢子，年大私度為弟子，自今斷之。

translations.literal: Monks and nuns frequently kept relatives and acquaintances and others' slave children; when grown they privately ordained them as disciples—from now this is cut off.
translations.idiomatic: Monks and nuns frequently harbored relatives, acquaintances, and others' slave children, privately ordaining them as disciples when they came of age—this practice is henceforth forbidden.

sentences.zh: 有犯還俗，被養者歸本等。

translations.literal: If there are violators, return to lay life; those who were kept return to their original status.
translations.idiomatic: Violators shall be returned to lay life; those who were harbored revert to their original status.

sentences.zh: 寺主聽容一人，出寺五百里，二人千里。

translations.literal: Monastery heads are permitted to keep one person within five hundred li of the monastery, two persons within a thousand li.
translations.idiomatic: Monastery heads may keep one attendant within five hundred li of the monastery, two within a thousand li.

sentences.zh: 私度之僧，皆由三長罪不及已，容多隱濫。

translations.literal: Privately ordained monks all relied on the three elders' rule that guilt does not reach oneself, and many concealed abuses.
translations.idiomatic: Those privately ordained relied on the rule that the three elders bear guilt while the individual goes unpunished, and many abuses were concealed.

sentences.zh: 自今有一人私度，皆以違旨論。

translations.literal: From now on, if even one person is privately ordained, all are punished for violating the decree.
translations.idiomatic: Henceforth, if even one person is privately ordained, all involved shall be punished for violating the decree.

sentences.zh: 隣長為首，里、黨各相降一等。

translations.literal: The neighborhood elder is chief culprit; the li and dang each have their rank reduced one degree.
translations.idiomatic: The neighborhood elder bears primary responsibility; the li and dang officials each have their rank reduced one degree.

sentences.zh: 縣滿十五人，郡滿三十人，州鎮滿三十人，免官，僚吏節級連坐。

translations.literal: If a county reaches fifteen persons, a commandery thirty, a province or garrison thirty, [officials are] dismissed from office and subordinate clerks punished by degrees of joint liability.
translations.idiomatic: If a county reaches fifteen persons, a commandery thirty, or a province or garrison thirty, officials are dismissed and subordinate clerks punished by degrees of joint liability.

sentences.zh: 私度之身，配當州下役。」

translations.literal: The privately ordained person himself is assigned to corvée labor in the lower ranks of that province.'
translations.idiomatic: The privately ordained person himself is assigned to corvée labor at the lowest level in that province."

sentences.zh: 時法禁寬褫，不能改肅也。

translations.literal: At the time legal prohibitions were lax and slack, and reform could not be enforced.
translations.idiomatic: At the time legal prohibitions had grown lax, and the reforms could not be rigorously enforced.

sentences.zh: 景明初，世宗詔大長秋卿白整準代京靈巖寺石窟，於洛南伊闕山，為高祖、文昭皇太后營石窟二所。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Jingming, Emperor Shizong ordered the Grand Director of the Palace Domestic Service Bai Zheng, following the model of the Lingyan Cave Temple of the capital of the [Northern] Wei, to build two cave shrines at Yique Mountain south of Luoyang for Emperor Gaozu and Empress Dowager Wenzhao.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Jingming, Emperor Shizong ordered Grand Director of the Palace Domestic Service Bai Zheng, following the model of the Lingyan Cave Temple at the Wei capital, to construct two cave shrines at Yique Mountain south of Luoyang for Emperor Gaozu and Empress Dowager Wenzhao.

sentences.zh: 初建之始，窟頂去地三百一十尺。

translations.literal: At the beginning of construction, the cave ceiling was three hundred and ten chi from the ground.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of construction, the cave ceiling stood three hundred and ten chi above the ground.

sentences.zh: 至正始二年中，始出斬山二十三丈。

translations.literal: By the second year of Zhengshi, excavation of the mountain had reached twenty-three zhang.
translations.idiomatic: By the second year of Zhengshi, twenty-three zhang of the mountainside had been cut away.

sentences.zh: 至大長秋卿王質，謂斬山太高，費功難就，奏求下移就平，去地一百尺，南北一百四十尺。

translations.literal: When Grand Director of the Palace Domestic Service Wang Zhi [took charge], he said the excavation was too high, the labor costly and hard to complete, and memorialized requesting it be lowered to level ground—one hundred chi from the ground, one hundred and forty chi north to south.
translations.idiomatic: When Grand Director Wang Zhi took charge, he judged the excavation too high and the labor too costly, and petitioned to lower the site to level ground—one hundred chi above ground, one hundred and forty chi north to south.

sentences.zh: 永平中，中尹劉騰奏為世宗復造石窟一，凡為三所。

translations.literal: In the Yongping period, Director of the Palace Domestic Service Liu Teng memorialized to build one more cave shrine for Emperor Shizong—three in all.
translations.idiomatic: During Yongping, Director of the Palace Domestic Service Liu Teng petitioned to build one more cave shrine for Emperor Shizong—three in all.

sentences.zh: 從景明元年至正光四年六月已前，用功八十萬二千三百六十六。

translations.literal: From the first year of Jingming to before the sixth month of the fourth year of Zhengguang, labor expended totaled eight hundred and two thousand three hundred and sixty-six [work-days].
translations.idiomatic: From the first year of Jingming through the sixth month of the fourth year of Zhengguang, labor expended totaled 802,366 work-days.

sentences.zh: 肅宗熙平中，於城內太社西，起永寧寺。

translations.literal: In the Xiping period of Emperor Suzong, the Yongning Temple was raised west of the Grand Soil Altar within the city.
translations.idiomatic: During Emperor Suzong's Xiping reign, the Yongning Temple was erected west of the Grand Soil Altar within the city.

sentences.zh: 靈太后親率百僚，表基立剎。

translations.literal: Empress Dowager Ling personally led the hundred officials to lay the foundation and establish the monastery.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Dowager Ling personally led the hundred officials to lay the foundation and establish the monastery.

sentences.zh: 佛圖九層，高四十餘丈，其諸費用，不可勝計。

translations.literal: The Buddhist pagoda had nine tiers, over forty zhang high; its various expenses were beyond reckoning.
translations.idiomatic: The Buddhist pagoda rose nine tiers, more than forty zhang high; its expenses were beyond reckoning.

sentences.zh: 景明寺佛圖，亦其亞也。

translations.literal: The Buddhist pagoda of Jingming Temple was nearly its equal.
translations.idiomatic: The pagoda of Jingming Temple was nearly its equal.

sentences.zh: 至於官私寺塔，其數甚眾。

translations.literal: As for official and private temples and pagodas, their number was very great.
translations.idiomatic: Official and private temples and pagodas numbered in the thousands.

sentences.zh: 神龜元年冬，司空公、尚書令、任城王澄奏曰：

translations.literal: In the winter of the first year of Shengui, the Duke of State, Minister of State Affairs, and Prince of Ren Cheng submitted a memorial:
translations.idiomatic: In the winter of the first year of Shengui, Duke of State, Minister of State Affairs, and Prince of Ren Cheng submitted a memorial:

sentences.zh: 仰惟高祖，定鼎嵩瀍，卜世悠遠。

translations.literal: Looking up to consider Emperor Gaozu, who established the dynasty at Song and Luo, with a mandate lasting far into the future.
translations.idiomatic: Looking up to Emperor Gaozu, who established the dynasty at Song and Luo with a mandate destined to endure for generations,

sentences.zh: 慮括終始，制洽天人，造物開符，垂之萬葉。

translations.literal: He considered beginning and end, harmonizing Heaven and man, creating things and opening the talisman, bequeathing it for myriad generations.
translations.idiomatic: he contemplated the course from beginning to end, harmonizing Heaven and man, opening the mandate of creation, and bequeathing it to ten thousand generations.

sentences.zh: 故都城制云，城內唯擬一永寧寺地，郭內唯擬尼寺一所，餘悉城郭之外。

translations.literal: Thus the capital-city regulations stated: within the city only one site for Yongning Temple was planned; within the outer walls only one nunnery; the rest all outside the walls and moat.
translations.idiomatic: Thus the capital regulations stipulated: within the city walls, only one site for Yongning Temple; within the outer walls, only one nunnery; all others outside the walls and moat.

sentences.zh: 欲令永遵此制，無敢踰矩。

translations.literal: He wished to make them forever observe this regulation, none daring to overstep the measure.
translations.idiomatic: He intended that this regulation be forever observed, with none daring to overstep its bounds.

sentences.zh: 逮景明之初，微有犯禁。

translations.literal: By the beginning of Jingming, there were slight violations of the prohibition.
translations.idiomatic: By the beginning of Jingming, the prohibition had been slightly violated.

sentences.zh: 故世宗仰修先志，爰發明旨，城內不造立浮圖、僧尼寺舍，亦欲絕其希覬。

translations.literal: Thus Emperor Shizong, looking up to carry out the former intent, thereupon issued a bright decree: within the city no pagodas, monk or nun temples and dwellings were to be built—also wishing to cut off their covetous hopes.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Shizong, upholding his predecessor's intent, issued a clear decree: no pagodas or monastic dwellings were to be built within the city—also to cut off covetous hopes.

sentences.zh: 文武二帝，豈不愛尚佛法，蓋以道俗殊歸，理無相亂故也。

translations.literal: Emperors Wen and Wu—did they not love and honor the Buddhist Law? It was because the way of clergy and laity diverge in destination, and by principle there should be no mutual confusion.
translations.idiomatic: Emperors Wen and Wu surely loved and honored the Buddhist Law—but the paths of clergy and laity diverge, and by principle they must not be confused.

sentences.zh: 但俗眩虛聲，僧貪厚潤，雖有顯禁，猶自冒營。

translations.literal: But the laity are dazzled by empty reputation, monks greedy for thick profit; though there were manifest prohibitions, they still presumptuously built.
translations.idiomatic: But the laity are dazzled by empty reputation and monks greedy for rich profit; despite clear prohibitions, they continued to build presumptuously.

sentences.zh: 至正始三年，沙門統惠深有違景明之禁，便云：「營就之寺，不忍移毀，求自今已後，更不聽立。」

translations.literal: By the third year of Zhengshi, the Supervisor of Monks Huishen violated the Jingming prohibition and said: 'Temples already built—I cannot bear to move and destroy them; I request that from now on no more be permitted.'
translations.idiomatic: By the third year of Zhengshi, Supervisor of Monks Huishen, violating the Jingming prohibition, petitioned: "Temples already built—I cannot bear to demolish them; I request that from now on no more be permitted."

sentences.zh: 先旨含寬，抑典從請。

translations.literal: The former decree contained leniency; the canonical standard was suppressed in favor of the request.
translations.idiomatic: The former decree contained leniency; canonical standards were set aside in favor of the petition.

sentences.zh: 前班之詔，仍卷不行，後來私謁，彌以奔競。

translations.literal: The earlier promulgated edict was still rolled up and not enforced; later private petitions grew ever more competitive.
