translations.idiomatic: The earlier promulgated edict was shelved and not enforced; later private petitions grew ever more competitive.

sentences.zh: 永平二年，深等復立條制，啟云：「自今已後，欲造寺者，限僧五十已上，聞徹聽造。

translations.literal: In the second year of Yongping, Huishen and others again established regulations, memorializing: 'From now on, those wishing to build temples—with fifty monks or more, upon report and approval, building is permitted.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Yongping, Huishen and others again established regulations, petitioning: "Henceforth, those wishing to build temples—with fifty monks or more, upon report and approval, building is permitted.

sentences.zh: 若有輒營置者，依俗違敕之罪，其寺僧眾，擯出外州。」

translations.literal: If anyone presumptuously builds and establishes [a temple], according to the crime of violating an edict in lay matters—the monks of that temple are expelled to outer provinces.'
translations.idiomatic: Anyone who builds without authorization shall be punished for violating an edict; the monks of that temple shall be expelled to outer provinces."

sentences.zh: 爾來十年，私營轉盛，罪擯之事，寂爾無聞。

translations.literal: In the ten years since, private building has turned ever more flourishing; matters of expulsion and punishment have been utterly unheard of.
translations.idiomatic: In the ten years since, private construction has flourished ever more; expulsions and punishments have been utterly unheard of.

sentences.zh: 豈非朝格雖明，恃福共毀，僧制徒立，顧利莫從者也。

translations.literal: Is it not that though court regulations are clear, they rely on merit and jointly destroy them; though monastic regulations are established, they look to profit and none follow?
translations.idiomatic: Is it not that though court regulations are clear, offenders rely on accumulated merit to evade them; though monastic rules exist, all look to profit and none comply?

sentences.zh: 不俗不道，務為損法，人而無厭，其可極乎！

translations.literal: Neither lay nor monastic—they strive to harm the Law; men without satiety—can it reach an end!
translations.idiomatic: Neither truly lay nor truly monastic, they strive only to harm the Law; human greed knows no bounds!

sentences.zh: 夫學迹沖妙，非浮識所辯；

translations.literal: The traces of learning are subtle and wondrous—not shallow understanding can discern them;
translations.idiomatic: The traces of learning are subtle and wondrous—not shallow understanding can discern them;

sentences.zh: 玄門曠寂，豈短辭能究。

translations.literal: The mysterious gate is vast and silent—how can brief words exhaust it?
translations.idiomatic: The mysterious gate is vast and silent—how can brief words exhaust it?

sentences.zh: 然淨居塵外，道家所先，功緣冥深，匪尚華遁。

translations.literal: Yet pure dwelling outside the dust is what the Way-family puts first; merit rooted in hidden depth is not what glorifies elegant withdrawal.
translations.idiomatic: Yet dwelling in purity beyond the dust is the Daoist ideal; merit rooted in hidden depths is not what glorifies elegant withdrawal.

sentences.zh: 苟能誠信，童子聚沙，可邁於道場；

translations.literal: If one can be sincere in faith, children piling sand can surpass a dharma-field;
translations.idiomatic: If one can be sincere in faith, children piling sand can surpass a sacred dharma-field;

sentences.zh: 純陀儉設，足薦於雙樹。

translations.literal: Chunda's frugal offering suffices to present at the Twin Trees.
translations.idiomatic: Chunda's frugal offering suffices to honor the Buddha beneath the Twin Trees.

sentences.zh: 何必縱其盜竊，資營寺觀。

translations.literal: Why must one indulge their theft and embezzlement to fund the building of temples and halls?
translations.idiomatic: Why must one indulge theft and embezzlement to fund the building of temples and halls?

sentences.zh: 此乃民之多幸，非國之福也。

translations.literal: This is the multitude's great fortune—not the state's blessing.
translations.idiomatic: This is the people's great fortune—not the state's blessing.

sentences.zh: 然比日私造，動盈百數。

translations.literal: Yet recently private construction often exceeds a hundred in number.
translations.idiomatic: Yet recently private construction often exceeds a hundred temples.

sentences.zh: 或乘請公地，[32]輒樹私福；

translations.literal: Some by petition obtain public land[32] and presumptuously plant private merit;
translations.idiomatic: Some obtain public land by petition[32] and presumptuously plant private merit;

sentences.zh: 或啟得造寺，限外廣制。

translations.literal: Some by memorial obtain permission to build a temple, then exceed the limit in broad construction.
translations.idiomatic: Some obtain permission to build a temple, then exceed the limit with expansive construction.

sentences.zh: 如此欺罔，非可稍計。

translations.literal: Deceptions such as these cannot be slightly reckoned.
translations.idiomatic: Such deceptions are beyond counting.

sentences.zh: 臣以才劣，誠忝工務，奉遵成規，裁量是總。

translations.literal: Your subject, with inferior talent, truly disgraces engineering duties; reverently following established regulations, I measure and assess the total.
translations.idiomatic: Your subject, though of inferior talent, discharges his engineering duties; reverently following established regulations, I have measured and assessed the total.

sentences.zh: 所以披尋舊旨，研究圖格，輒遣府司馬陸昶、屬崔孝芬，都城之中及郭邑之內檢括寺舍，數乘五百，[33]空地表剎，未立塔宇，不在其數。

translations.literal: Therefore I have examined old decrees and studied regulations and charts, and dispatched the prefecture's Major Lu Chang and subordinate Cui Xiaofen to inspect temples and dwellings within the capital and in the outer towns—the number multiplied by five hundred;[33] vacant land with monasteries established but no pagoda or hall yet built is not counted.
translations.idiomatic: Therefore I have examined old decrees and studied regulations, and dispatched the prefecture's Major Lu Chang and subordinate Cui Xiaofen to inspect temples within the capital and outer towns—the number exceeds five hundred;[33] vacant sites with monasteries established but no pagoda yet built are not counted.

sentences.zh: 民不畏法，乃至於斯！

translations.literal: The people do not fear the law—to this extent!
translations.idiomatic: The people do not fear the law—to this extent!

sentences.zh: 自遷都已來，年踰二紀，寺奪民居，三分且一。

translations.literal: Since the move of the capital, more than two decades have passed; temples have seized commoners' dwellings—a third and more.
translations.idiomatic: Since the capital was moved, more than two decades have passed; temples have seized commoners' dwellings—a third and more.

sentences.zh: 高祖立制，非徒欲使緇素殊途，抑亦防微深慮。

translations.literal: Emperor Gaozu established regulations—not merely to make black-robed and white-robed follow separate paths, but also to guard against the subtle with deep forethought.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Gaozu established these regulations—not merely to separate clergy from laity, but also to guard against subtle dangers with deep forethought.

sentences.zh: 世宗述之，亦不錮禁營福，當在杜塞未萌。

translations.literal: Emperor Shizong continued them—also not to lock up and forbid merit-making, but to block it before it sprouted.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Shizong continued them—not to forbid merit-making entirely, but to block abuses before they sprouted.

sentences.zh: 今之僧寺，無處不有。

translations.literal: Today's monasteries exist everywhere without exception.
translations.idiomatic: Today's monasteries exist everywhere without exception.

sentences.zh: 或比滿城邑之中，或連溢屠沽之肆，或三五少僧，共為一寺。

translations.literal: Some fill nearly an entire city; some adjoin and overflow into butcher and tavern shops; some three or five monks together make one temple.
translations.idiomatic: Some fill nearly an entire city; some adjoin butcher shops and taverns; some three or five monks together constitute one temple.

sentences.zh: 梵唱屠音，連簷接響，像塔纒於腥臊，性靈沒於嗜慾，真偽混居，往來紛雜。

translations.literal: Sanskrit chanting and butcher's sounds, eaves joined in echo; image-towers entangled in stench and filth, the spiritual nature drowned in craving and desire—true and false mixed in dwelling, coming and going in confusion.
translations.idiomatic: Sanskrit chanting mingles with butcher's cries, eaves joined in echo; image-towers stand amid stench and filth, the spiritual nature drowned in craving—true and false dwell together, coming and going in confusion.

sentences.zh: 下司因習而莫非，[34]僧曹對制而不問。

translations.literal: Lower officials, through habit, all deem it not wrong;[34] the monastic bureau, facing regulations, does not inquire.
translations.idiomatic: Lower officials, through habit, deem it not wrong;[34] the monastic bureau, facing regulations, does not inquire.

sentences.zh: 其於汙染真行，塵穢練僧，薰蕕同器，不亦甚歟！

translations.literal: As for defiling true conduct and soiling refined monks—artemisia and orchid in the same vessel—is it not excessive!
translations.idiomatic: As for defiling true conduct and soiling refined monks—artemisia and orchid in the same vessel—is it not excessive!

sentences.zh: 往在北代，有法秀之謀；

translations.literal: In the past in Northern Dai, there was the plot of Faxiu;
translations.idiomatic: In the past in Northern Dai, there was the plot of Faxiu;

sentences.zh: 近日冀州，遭大乘之變。

translations.literal: Recently in Jizhou, there was the disturbance of the Mahayana [sect].
translations.idiomatic: Recently in Jizhou, there was the disturbance of the Mahayana sect.

sentences.zh: 皆初假神教，以惑眾心，終設姦誑，用逞私悖。

translations.literal: All at first borrowed divine teaching to bewilder the multitude's hearts; in the end they set up treachery and deception to give free rein to private rebellion.
translations.idiomatic: All at first borrowed divine teaching to bewilder the multitude; in the end they set up treachery and deception to give free rein to private rebellion.

sentences.zh: 太和之制，因法秀而杜遠；

translations.literal: The Taihe regulations, because of Faxiu, blocked the distant;
translations.idiomatic: The Taihe regulations, because of Faxiu, blocked distant dangers;

sentences.zh: 景明之禁，慮大乘之將亂。

translations.literal: The Jingming prohibitions, fearing the Mahayana's impending disorder.
translations.idiomatic: the Jingming prohibitions, fearing the Mahayana's impending disorder.

sentences.zh: 始知祖宗叡聖，防遏處深。

translations.literal: Then one knows the ancestors' sage wisdom—preventing and blocking ran deep.
translations.idiomatic: Then one knows the ancestors' sage wisdom—preventing and blocking ran deep.

sentences.zh: [35]履霜堅冰，不可不慎。

translations.literal: [35]Treading on frost, solid ice—one cannot but be cautious.
translations.idiomatic: [35]Treading on frost leads to solid ice—one must be cautious.

sentences.zh: 昔如來闡教，多依山林，今此僧徒，戀著城邑。

translations.literal: In the past when the Tathagata expounded the teaching, he relied much on mountain forests; today these monks cling to the city.
translations.idiomatic: In the past when the Tathagata expounded the teaching, he relied much on mountain forests; today these monks cling to the cities.

sentences.zh: 豈湫隘是經行所宜，浮諠必栖禪之宅，當由利引其心，莫能自止。

translations.literal: How can cramped narrowness be suitable for sutra-walking, or floating clamor necessarily be the dwelling of meditation? It must be because profit draws their hearts, and they cannot stop themselves.
translations.idiomatic: How can cramped quarters suit sutra-walking, or noisy streets be fit dwellings for meditation? Profit draws their hearts, and they cannot restrain themselves.

sentences.zh: 處者既失其真，造者或損其福，乃釋氏之糟糠，法中之社鼠，內戒所不容，王典所應棄矣。

translations.literal: Those who dwell have already lost their truth; those who build sometimes damage their merit—they are the dregs of the Buddhist family, the temple rats of the Law, what inner precepts cannot tolerate and royal statutes should discard.
translations.idiomatic: Those who dwell have lost their truth; those who build sometimes damage their merit—they are the dregs of the Buddhist family, the temple rats of the Law, what inner precepts cannot tolerate and royal statutes should discard.

sentences.zh: 非但京邑如此，天下州、鎮僧寺亦然。

translations.literal: Not only the capital is thus—monasteries in provinces and garrisons throughout the empire are likewise.
translations.idiomatic: Not only the capital is thus—monasteries in provinces and garrisons throughout the empire are likewise.

sentences.zh: 侵奪細民，廣占田宅，有傷慈矜，用長嗟苦。

translations.literal: Seizing and robbing petty people, broadly occupying fields and dwellings—this harms compassionate pity and lengthens sighs of suffering.
translations.idiomatic: Seizing and robbing commoners, broadly occupying fields and dwellings—this harms compassionate pity and deepens the people's suffering.

sentences.zh: 且人心不同，善惡亦異。

translations.literal: Moreover, human hearts differ—good and evil also differ.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, human hearts differ—good and evil also differ.

sentences.zh: 或有栖心真趣，道業清遠者；

translations.literal: Some there are who lodge their hearts in true purpose, with the Way's work clear and distant;
translations.idiomatic: Some lodge their hearts in true purpose, with the Way's work clear and distant;

sentences.zh: 或外假法服，內懷悖德者。

translations.literal: Some outwardly borrow the Law's garb, inwardly harboring rebellious virtue.
translations.idiomatic: Some outwardly wear the Law's garb while inwardly harboring rebellious hearts.

sentences.zh: 如此之徒，宜辨涇渭。

translations.literal: Persons such as these should be distinguished as Jing from Wei.
translations.idiomatic: Such persons should be distinguished as Jing from Wei.

sentences.zh: 若雷同一貫，何以勸善。

translations.literal: If thunder strikes uniformly, how can one encourage good?
translations.idiomatic: If punishment strikes uniformly, how can one encourage good?

sentences.zh: 然覩法贊善，凡人所知；

translations.literal: Yet seeing the Law and praising good is what ordinary people know;
translations.idiomatic: Yet seeing the Law and praising good is what ordinary people know;

sentences.zh: 矯俗避嫌，[36]物情同趣。

translations.literal: Correcting custom and avoiding suspicion[36]—the feelings of things share the same tendency.
translations.idiomatic: Correcting custom and avoiding suspicion[36]—popular sentiment shares the same tendency.

sentences.zh: 臣獨何為，孤議獨發。

translations.literal: Your subject alone—why act thus, with a solitary opinion independently issued?
translations.idiomatic: Your subject alone—why act thus, with a solitary opinion independently issued?

sentences.zh: 誠以國典一廢，追理至難，法網暫失，條綱將亂。

translations.literal: Truly because if state canon is once abolished, pursuing reason afterward is extremely difficult; if the legal net is briefly lost, regulations and guidelines will fall into disorder.
translations.idiomatic: Truly because if state canon is once abolished, restoring order afterward is extremely difficult; if the legal net is briefly lost, regulations and guidelines will fall into disorder.

sentences.zh: 是以冒陳愚見，兩願其益。

translations.literal: Therefore I presumptuously present this foolish view, wishing benefit on both sides.
translations.idiomatic: Therefore I presumptuously present this view, wishing benefit on both sides.

sentences.zh: 臣聞設令在於必行，立罰貴能肅物。

translations.literal: Your subject has heard: establishing orders where they must be carried out; establishing punishments values the ability to awe things.
translations.idiomatic: Your subject has heard: establishing orders where they must be carried out; establishing punishments values the ability to awe offenders.

sentences.zh: 令而不行，不如無令。

translations.literal: An order that is not carried out—better no order at all.
translations.idiomatic: An order that is not carried out—better no order at all.

sentences.zh: 罰不能肅，孰與亡罰。

translations.literal: A punishment that cannot awe—what difference from no punishment?
translations.idiomatic: A punishment that cannot awe—what difference from no punishment?

sentences.zh: 頃明詔屢下，而造者更滋，嚴限驟施，而違犯不息者，豈不以假福託善，幸罪不加。

translations.literal: Recently bright edicts have been repeatedly issued, yet builders increase all the more; strict limits have been suddenly applied, yet violations do not cease—is it not because they rely on borrowed merit and entrusted goodness, hoping punishment will not be added?
translations.idiomatic: Recently bright edicts have been repeatedly issued, yet builders increase all the more; strict limits have been suddenly applied, yet violations do not cease—is it not because offenders rely on borrowed merit, hoping punishment will not be added?

sentences.zh: 人殉其私，吏難苟劾。

translations.literal: Men sacrifice themselves to private interest; officials find it hard to perfunctorily impeach.
translations.idiomatic: Men sacrifice themselves to private interest; officials find it hard to perfunctorily impeach.

sentences.zh: 前制無追往之辜，後旨開自今之恕，悠悠世情，遂忽成法。

translations.literal: Former regulations had no guilt for past acts; later decrees opened forgiveness from today onward—the vast world's feelings thus neglected what became law.
translations.idiomatic: Former regulations had no guilt for past acts; later decrees opened forgiveness from today onward—popular sentiment thus neglected what became law.

sentences.zh: 今宜加以嚴科，特設重禁，糾其來違，懲其往失。

translations.literal: Now one should add strict penalties, specially establish heavy prohibitions, correct their coming violations, and punish their past faults.
translations.idiomatic: Now one should add strict penalties, specially establish heavy prohibitions, correct ongoing violations, and punish past faults.

sentences.zh: 脫不峻檢，方垂容借，恐今旨雖明，復如往日。

translations.literal: If not strictly inspected, and leniency is extended instead, I fear that though today's decree is clear, it will be as in former days.
translations.idiomatic: If not strictly inspected, and leniency is extended instead, I fear that though today's decree is clear, it will be as in former days.

sentences.zh: 又旨令所斷，標榜禮拜之處，悉聽不禁。

translations.literal: Also, places marked by the decree's prohibition as sites of worship are altogether permitted without prohibition.
translations.idiomatic: Also, places marked by the decree's prohibition as sites of worship are altogether permitted without prohibition.

sentences.zh: 愚以為，樹榜無常，禮處難驗，欲云有造，立榜證公，須營之辭，指言嘗禮。

translations.literal: Your foolish subject thinks: posted placards are not fixed, worship sites are hard to verify; to say there was construction, establishing a placard proves it publicly—the words of building must point to saying worship once occurred.
translations.idiomatic: Your foolish subject thinks: posted placards are not fixed, worship sites are hard to verify; to claim prior construction, one need only post a placard and point to past worship.

sentences.zh: 如此則徒有禁名，實通造路。

translations.literal: Thus there would be only the name of prohibition, while in reality a path for building remains open.
translations.idiomatic: Thus there would be only the name of prohibition, while in reality a path for building remains open.

sentences.zh: 且徙御已後，斷詔四行，而私造之徒，不懼制旨。

translations.literal: Moreover, after the imperial move, four prohibition edicts were issued, yet those who built privately did not fear the regulatory decree.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, after the imperial move, four prohibition edicts were issued, yet private builders did not fear the regulatory decree.

sentences.zh: 豈是百官有司，怠於奉法？

translations.literal: Is it that the hundred officials and functionaries were slack in observing the law?
translations.idiomatic: Is it that the hundred officials and functionaries were slack in observing the law?

sentences.zh: 將由網漏禁寬，容託有他故耳。

translations.literal: Or is it because the net leaked, prohibitions were lax, and shelter and pretext had other reasons?
translations.idiomatic: Or is it because the net leaked, prohibitions were lax, and shelter and pretext had other reasons?

sentences.zh: 如臣愚意，都城之中，雖有標榜，營造粗功，事可改立者，請依先制。

translations.literal: According to your subject's foolish intent: within the capital, though there are posted placards, for construction with rough work that can be altered and rebuilt, I request following the former regulation.
translations.idiomatic: According to your subject's view: within the capital, though posted placards exist, for construction with rough work that can be altered and rebuilt, I request following the former regulation.

sentences.zh: 在於郭外，任擇所便。

translations.literal: Outside the walls, let them choose what is convenient.
translations.idiomatic: Outside the walls, let them choose what is convenient.

sentences.zh: 其地若買得，券證分明者，聽其轉之。

translations.literal: If the land was bought and obtained, with contracts and certificates clear, permit its transfer.
translations.idiomatic: If the land was bought with clear contracts and certificates, permit its transfer.

sentences.zh: 若官地盜作，即令還官。

translations.literal: If official land was stolen and built upon, immediately order its return to the state.
translations.idiomatic: If official land was stolen and built upon, immediately order its return to the state.

sentences.zh: 若靈像既成，不可移撤，請依今敕，如舊不禁，悉令坊內行止，不聽毀坊開門，以妨里內通巷。

translations.literal: If spirit-images are already completed and cannot be moved or removed, I request following today's decree—as before, not prohibited; all shall conduct affairs within the ward, not permitting destruction of the ward to open gates, so as not to obstruct lanes within the li.
translations.idiomatic: If spirit-images are already completed and cannot be moved, I request following today's decree—as before, not prohibited; all shall remain within the ward, not permitting destruction of the ward to open gates, so as not to obstruct lanes within the li.

sentences.zh: 若被旨者，不在斷限。

translations.literal: If by imperial decree, [they are] not within the prohibition's limit.
translations.idiomatic: If by imperial decree, they are not within the prohibition's limit.

sentences.zh: 郭內準此商量。

translations.literal: Within the outer walls, follow this deliberation.
translations.idiomatic: Within the outer walls, follow this deliberation.

sentences.zh: 其廟像嚴立，而逼近屠沽，請斷旁屠殺，以潔靈居。

translations.literal: Where temple-images are solemnly established yet adjoin butcher and tavern shops, I request cutting off adjacent slaughter, to purify the spirit-dwelling.
translations.idiomatic: Where temple-images are solemnly established yet adjoin butcher shops and taverns, I request cutting off adjacent slaughter, to purify the spirit-dwelling.

sentences.zh: 雖有僧數，而事在可移者，令就閑敞，以避隘陋。

translations.literal: Though there are monk-numbers, where the matter can be moved, order them to go to open spaciousness, to avoid cramped narrowness.
translations.idiomatic: Though there are sufficient monks, where relocation is feasible, order them to move to open spacious sites, to avoid cramped quarters.

sentences.zh: 如今年正月赦後造者，求依僧制，案法科治。

translations.literal: Such as those built after the amnesty of the first month this year—I request following monastic regulations, investigating and adjudicating according to law.
translations.idiomatic: Such as those built after the amnesty of the first month this year—I request following monastic regulations, investigating and adjudicating according to law.

sentences.zh: 若僧不滿五十者，共相通容，小就大寺，必令充限。

translations.literal: If monks do not reach fifty, they may mutually accommodate—small merging into large temples, necessarily making them fill the quota.
translations.idiomatic: If monks do not reach fifty, they may mutually accommodate—small merging into large temples, necessarily making them fill the quota.

sentences.zh: 其地賣還，一如上式。

translations.literal: Land sold and returned follows the above formula.
translations.idiomatic: Land sold and returned follows the above formula.

sentences.zh: 自今外州，若欲造寺，僧滿五十已上，先令本州表列，昭玄量審，奏聽乃立。

translations.literal: From now on in outer provinces, if wishing to build a temple with fifty monks or more, first order this province to memorialize and list; the Bureau of Monastic Affairs measures and examines; upon memorial and approval, then establish.
translations.idiomatic: From now on in outer provinces, if wishing to build a temple with fifty monks or more, the province must first memorialize and list; the Bureau of Monastic Affairs examines; upon approval, then establish.

sentences.zh: 若有違犯，悉依前科。

translations.literal: If there are violations, all follow the former penalties.
translations.idiomatic: If there are violations, all follow the former penalties.

sentences.zh: 州郡已下，容而不禁，罪同違旨。

translations.literal: Provinces and commanderies below, tolerating and not prohibiting—guilt equals violating the decree.
translations.idiomatic: Provinces and commanderies below, tolerating and not prohibishing—guilt equals violating the decree.

sentences.zh: 庶仰遵先皇不朽之業，俯奉今旨慈悲之令，則繩墨可全，聖道不墜矣。

translations.literal: May we look up to follow the former emperor's immortal enterprise, look down to uphold today's decree of compassion—then the measuring-cord can be preserved whole, and the sage Way not fall.
translations.idiomatic: May we look up to follow the former emperor's immortal enterprise, look down to uphold today's decree of compassion—then regulations can be preserved whole, and the sage Way not fall.

sentences.zh: 奏可。

translations.literal: The memorial was approved.
translations.idiomatic: The memorial was approved.

sentences.zh: 未幾，天下喪亂，加以河陰之酷，朝士死者，其家多捨居宅，以施僧尼，京邑第舍，略為寺矣。

translations.literal: Before long, the empire fell into disorder; added to the cruelty of Heyin, court gentlemen who died—their families mostly donated dwelling-houses to give to monks and nuns; capital mansions and residences were largely turned into temples.
translations.idiomatic: Before long, the empire fell into disorder; added to the cruelty of Heyin, court gentlemen who died—their families mostly donated dwelling-houses to monks and nuns; capital mansions were largely turned into temples.

sentences.zh: 前日禁令，不復行焉。

translations.literal: The former day's prohibition edict was no longer enforced.
translations.idiomatic: The former prohibition edict was no longer enforced.

sentences.zh: 元象元年秋，詔曰：「梵境幽玄，義歸清曠，伽藍淨土，理絕囂塵。

translations.literal: In the autumn of the first year of Yuanxiang, an edict said: 'The Buddhist realm is dark and mysterious; its meaning returns to clarity and vastness; the sangha's pure land—by principle it rejects clamor and dust.
translations.idiomatic: In the autumn of the first year of Yuanxiang, an edict said: "The Buddhist realm is dark and mysterious; its meaning returns to clarity and vastness; the sangha's pure land—by principle it rejects clamor and dust.

sentences.zh: 前朝城內，先有禁斷，自聿來遷鄴，率由舊章。

translations.literal: In the former dynasty within the city, there was already prohibition and cutting off; since coming to move the capital to Ye, all follow the old regulations.
translations.idiomatic: In the former dynasty within the city, prohibition already existed; since moving the capital to Ye, all follow the old regulations.

sentences.zh: 而百辟士民，届都之始，城外新城，並皆給宅。

translations.literal: Yet the hundred ministers and common people, at the beginning of arriving at the capital—the outer new city, all were given dwellings.
translations.idiomatic: Yet the hundred ministers and common people, upon arriving at the capital—the outer new city, all were given dwellings.

sentences.zh: 舊城中暫時普借，更擬後須，非為永久。

translations.literal: Within the old city temporarily universally borrowed—further planned for later need, not for permanence.
translations.idiomatic: Within the old city dwellings were temporarily lent—intended for later need, not for permanence.

sentences.zh: 如聞諸人，多以二處得地，或捨舊城所借之宅，擅立為寺。

translations.literal: As I have heard, many people obtained land in both places, or abandoned the old city's borrowed dwelling and presumptuously established it as a temple.
translations.idiomatic: As I have heard, many people obtained land in both places, or abandoned the old city's borrowed dwelling and presumptuously established it as a temple.

sentences.zh: 知非己有，假此一名。

translations.literal: Knowing it was not their own, they borrowed this one name.
translations.idiomatic: Knowing it was not their own, they borrowed this one name.

sentences.zh: 終恐因習滋甚，有虧恒式。

translations.literal: In the end I fear that through habit it will grow ever more severe, damaging the constant formula.
translations.idiomatic: In the end I fear that through habit it will grow ever more severe, damaging established norms.

sentences.zh: 宜付有司，精加隱括。

translations.literal: It should be entrusted to the responsible officials for meticulous hidden inspection.
translations.idiomatic: It should be entrusted to the responsible officials for meticulous inspection.

sentences.zh: 且城中舊寺及宅，並有定帳，其新立之徒，悉從毀廢。」

translations.literal: Moreover, old temples and dwellings within the city all have fixed registers; those newly established shall all be destroyed and abolished.'
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, old temples and dwellings within the city all have fixed registers; those newly established shall all be destroyed and abolished."

sentences.zh: 冬，又詔：「天下牧守令長，悉不聽造寺。

translations.literal: In winter, again an edict: 'Prefects, garrison commanders, magistrates, and chiefs throughout the empire are altogether forbidden to build temples.
translations.idiomatic: In winter, again an edict: "Prefects, garrison commanders, magistrates, and chiefs throughout the empire are altogether forbidden to build temples.

sentences.zh: 若有違者，不問財之所出，并計所營功庸，悉以枉法論。」

translations.literal: If there are violators, without asking whence the wealth came, and counting the labor expended in construction—all punished as bending the law.'
translations.idiomatic: If there are violators, without asking whence the wealth came, and counting the labor expended in construction—all punished as bending the law."

sentences.zh: 興和二年春，詔以鄴城舊宮為天平寺。

translations.literal: In the spring of the second year of Xinghe, an edict made the old palace at Ye city into Tianping Temple.
translations.idiomatic: In the spring of the second year of Xinghe, an edict made the old palace at Ye city into Tianping Temple.

sentences.zh: 世宗以來至武定末，沙門知名者，有惠猛、惠辨、惠深、僧暹、道欽、僧獻、道晞、僧深、惠光、惠顯、法榮、道長，並見重於當世。

translations.literal: From Emperor Shizong down to the end of Wuding, among monks of renown were Huimeng, Huibian, Huishen, the monk Xian, Daoqin, Sengxian, Daoxi, Sengshen, Huiguang, Huixian, Farong, and Daochang—all were honored in their age.
translations.idiomatic: From Emperor Shizong down to the end of Wuding, among monks of renown were Huimeng, Huibian, Huishen, the monk Xian, Daoqin, Sengxian, Daoxi, Sengshen, Huiguang, Huixian, Farong, and Daochang—all were honored in their age.

sentences.zh: 魏有天下，至於禪讓，佛經流通，大集中國，凡有四百一十五部，合一千九百一十九卷。

translations.literal: Wei possessed the empire down to the abdication; Buddhist sutras circulated, greatly gathered in Central States—in all four hundred and fifteen works, totaling one thousand nine hundred and nineteen scrolls.
translations.idiomatic: Wei possessed the empire down to the abdication; Buddhist sutras circulated, greatly gathered in the Central States—in all 415 works, totaling 1,919 scrolls.

sentences.zh: 正光已後，天下多虞，王役尤甚，於是所在編民，相與入道，假慕沙門，實避調役，猥濫之極，自中國之有佛法，未之有也。

translations.literal: After Zhengguang, the empire had many troubles; royal corvée was especially severe; thus registered commoners everywhere mutually entered the Way, falsely admiring monks, in reality avoiding tax and corvée—abuse to the extreme, such as never since Buddhism existed in Central States.
translations.idiomatic: After Zhengguang, the empire had many troubles; royal corvée was especially severe; thus registered commoners everywhere entered the clergy, falsely admiring monks while in reality avoiding tax and corvée—abuse to an extreme never seen since Buddhism came to the Central States.

sentences.zh: 略而計之，僧尼大眾二百萬矣，其寺三萬有餘。

translations.literal: Roughly reckoning it, the great multitude of monks and nuns numbered two million; their temples exceeded thirty thousand.
translations.idiomatic: Roughly reckoning it, the great multitude of monks and nuns numbered two million; their temples exceeded thirty thousand.

sentences.zh: 流弊不歸，一至於此，識者所以歎息也。

translations.literal: Flowing abuses not returning—reaching this point; men of insight therefore sighed.
translations.idiomatic: Flowing abuses not returning—reaching this point; men of insight therefore sighed.

sentences.zh: 道家之原，出於老子。

translations.literal: The origin of the Way-family comes from Laozi.
translations.idiomatic: The origin of the Daoist tradition comes from Laozi.

sentences.zh: 其自言也，先天地生，以資萬類。

translations.literal: In his own words, he was born before Heaven and Earth, to nourish the myriad categories.
translations.idiomatic: In his own words, he was born before Heaven and Earth, to nourish the myriad categories of beings.

sentences.zh: 上處玉京，為神王之宗；

translations.literal: Above he dwells in the Jade Capital, as patriarch of spirit-kings;
translations.idiomatic: Above he dwells in the Jade Capital, as patriarch of spirit-kings;

sentences.zh: 下在紫微，為飛仙之主。

translations.literal: Below he is at Purple Subtlety, as lord of flying immortals.
translations.idiomatic: Below he is at Purple Subtlety, as lord of flying immortals.

sentences.zh: 千變萬化，有德不德，隨感應物，厥迹無常。

translations.literal: A thousand transformations and ten thousand changes—having virtue or not having virtue; following sensation responding to things, his traces are not fixed.
translations.idiomatic: A thousand transformations and ten thousand changes—having virtue or not having virtue; following sensation and responding to things, his traces are not fixed.

sentences.zh: 授軒轅於峨嵋，教帝嚳於牧德，大禹聞長生之訣，尹喜受道德之旨。

translations.literal: He conferred [the Way] upon the Yellow Emperor at Emei, taught Emperor Ku at Mude; Great Yu heard the secret of long life; Yin Xi received the purport of the Dao and its Power.
translations.idiomatic: He conferred the Way upon the Yellow Emperor at Emei, taught Emperor Ku at Mude; Great Yu heard the secret of long life; Yin Xi received the purport of the Dao and its Power.

sentences.zh: 至於丹書紫字，昇玄飛步之經；

translations.literal: As for cinnabar writings and purple characters, sutras of ascending mystery and flying steps;
translations.idiomatic: As for cinnabar writings and purple characters, sutras of ascending mystery and flying steps;

sentences.zh: 玉石金光，妙有靈洞之說。

translations.literal: Jade-stone golden light, explanations of wondrous numinous caverns.
translations.idiomatic: jade-stone golden light, explanations of wondrous numinous caverns.

sentences.zh: 如此之文，不可勝紀。

translations.literal: Writings such as these cannot be fully recorded.
translations.idiomatic: Writings such as these cannot be fully recorded.

sentences.zh: 其為教也，咸蠲去邪累，澡雪心神，積行樹功，累德增善，乃至白日昇天，長生世上。

translations.literal: As for its teaching, all universally cut away evil accumulations, bathe and purify the spirit-mind, accumulate conduct and establish merit, accumulate virtue and increase goodness—reaching even ascending to Heaven in broad daylight, long life in the world above.
translations.idiomatic: As for its teaching, all universally cut away evil accumulations, bathe and purify the spirit-mind, accumulate conduct and establish merit, accumulate virtue and increase goodness—reaching even ascending to Heaven in broad daylight, long life in the world above.

sentences.zh: 所以秦皇、漢武，甘心不息。

translations.literal: Therefore Qin Shihuang and Emperor Wu of Han, with willing hearts, did not cease.
translations.idiomatic: Therefore Qin Shihuang and Emperor Wu of Han pursued it with willing hearts that did not cease.

sentences.zh: 靈帝置華蓋於濯龍，[37]設壇場而為禮。

translations.literal: Emperor Ling set Canopy of Flowers at Zhuolong;[37] established altar grounds and performed rites.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Ling set Canopy of Flowers at Zhuolong;[37] established altar grounds and performed rites.

sentences.zh: 及張陵受道於鵠鳴，因傳天官章本千有二百，弟子相授，其事大行。

translations.literal: When Zhang Ling received the Way at Heming, he thereupon transmitted the Heavenly Bureau's chapter-texts—one thousand two hundred in all; disciples transmitted them to one another, and the matter greatly flourished.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhang Ling received the Way at Heming, he thereupon transmitted the Heavenly Bureau's chapter-texts—1,200 in all; disciples transmitted them to one another, and the matter greatly flourished.

sentences.zh: 齋祠跪拜，各成法道，[38]有三元九府、百二十官，一切諸神，咸所統攝。

translations.literal: Fast-rituals, ancestral worship, bowing and kneeling—each became a dharma-way;[38] there are Three Primes and Nine Palaces, one hundred and twenty officials—all spirits are governed and controlled.
translations.idiomatic: Fast-rituals, ancestral worship, bowing and kneeling—each became a dharma-way;[38] there are Three Primes and Nine Palaces, 120 officials—all spirits are governed and controlled.

sentences.zh: 又稱劫數，頗類佛經。

translations.literal: They also speak of kalpa-numbers, quite resembling Buddhist sutras.
translations.idiomatic: They also speak of kalpa-numbers, quite resembling Buddhist sutras.

sentences.zh: 其延康、龍漢、赤明、開皇之屬，皆其名也。

translations.literal: Their Yankang, Longhan, Chiming, Kaihuang and the like—all are their names.
translations.idiomatic: Their Yankang, Longhan, Chiming, Kaihuang and the like—all are their names.

sentences.zh: 及其劫終，稱天地俱壞。

translations.literal: When their kalpa ends, they say Heaven and Earth are both destroyed.
translations.idiomatic: When their kalpa ends, they say Heaven and Earth are both destroyed.

sentences.zh: 其書多有禁祕，非其徒也，不得輒觀。

translations.literal: Their books mostly have prohibitions and secrets; those not their disciples may not casually view them.
translations.idiomatic: Their books mostly have prohibitions and secrets; those not their disciples may not casually view them.

sentences.zh: 至於化金銷玉，行符敕水，奇方妙術，萬等千條，上云羽化飛天，次稱消災滅禍。

translations.literal: As for transforming gold and dissolving jade, performing talismans and commanding water, strange formulas and wondrous techniques—ten thousand kinds and a thousand articles; above they say feather-transformation and flying to Heaven, below they call it eliminating disasters and extinguishing misfortune.
translations.idiomatic: As for transforming gold and dissolving jade, performing talismans and commanding water, strange formulas and wondrous techniques—ten thousand kinds and a thousand articles; above they say feather-transformation and flying to Heaven, below they call it eliminating disasters and extinguishing misfortune.

sentences.zh: 故好異者往往而尊事之。

translations.literal: Thus those who love the strange often respect and serve them.
translations.idiomatic: Thus those who love the strange often respect and serve them.

sentences.zh: 初文帝入賓於晉，從者務勿塵，姿神奇偉，登仙於伊闕之山寺。

translations.literal: At first when Emperor Wen of Wei entered Jin as a hostage, his follower Wu Wuchen—with wondrous and imposing appearance—ascended to immortality at a mountain temple at Yique.
translations.idiomatic: At first when Emperor Wen of Wei entered Jin as a hostage, his follower Wu Wuchen—with wondrous and imposing appearance—ascended to immortality at a mountain temple at Yique.

sentences.zh: 識者咸云魏祚之將大。

translations.literal: Men of insight all said Wei's mandate was about to grow great.
translations.idiomatic: Men of insight all said Wei's mandate was about to grow great.

sentences.zh: 太祖好老子之言，誦詠不倦。

translations.literal: Emperor Taizu loved Laozi's words, reciting and intoning without weariness.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Taizu loved Laozi's words, reciting and intoning without weariness.

sentences.zh: 天興中，儀曹郎董謐因獻服食仙經數十篇。

translations.literal: In the Tianxing period, Gentleman of the Ministry of Rites Dong Mi thereupon presented several tens of scrolls of immortal-consumption and transcendence sutras.
translations.idiomatic: In the Tianxing period, Gentleman of the Ministry of Rites Dong Mi thereupon presented several tens of scrolls of immortal-consumption and transcendence sutras.

sentences.zh: 於是置仙人博士，立仙坊，煮鍊百藥，封西山以供其薪蒸。

translations.literal: Thereupon he established a Transcendent Person Erudite, set up a Transcendent Quarter, boiled and refined a hundred medicines, and sealed off the Western Mountain to supply its fuel and steam.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon he established a Transcendent Person Erudite, set up a Transcendent Quarter, boiled and refined a hundred medicines, and sealed off the Western Mountain to supply its fuel and steam.

sentences.zh: 令死罪者試服之，非其本心，多死無驗。

translations.literal: He ordered those guilty of capital crimes to try consuming them—not their true intent, many died without verification.
translations.idiomatic: He ordered those guilty of capital crimes to try consuming them—not their true intent, many died without verification.

sentences.zh: 太祖猶將修焉。

translations.literal: Emperor Taizu still intended to continue the undertaking.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Taizu still intended to continue the undertaking.

sentences.zh: 太醫周澹，苦其煎採之役，欲廢其事。

translations.literal: Grand Physician Zhou Dan, bitter at the labor of boiling and gathering, wished to abolish the matter.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Physician Zhou Dan, bitter at the labor of boiling and gathering, wished to abolish the matter.

sentences.zh: 乃陰令妻貨仙人博士張曜妾，得曜隱罪。

translations.literal: He secretly ordered his wife to bribe Transcendent Person Erudite Zhang Yao's concubine, obtaining Yao's hidden crimes.
translations.idiomatic: He secretly ordered his wife to bribe Transcendent Person Erudite Zhang Yao's concubine, obtaining Yao's hidden crimes.

sentences.zh: 曜懼死，因請辟穀。

translations.literal: Yao feared death and thereupon requested grain avoidance.
translations.idiomatic: Yao feared death and thereupon requested grain avoidance.

sentences.zh: 太祖許之，給曜資用，為造靜堂於苑中，給洒掃民二家。

translations.literal: Emperor Taizu permitted it, gave Yao supplies, and for him built a Quiet Hall in the park, giving two households of sprinkling and sweeping commoners.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Taizu permitted it, gave Yao supplies, and for him built a Quiet Hall in the park, giving two households of sprinkling and sweeping commoners.

sentences.zh: 而鍊藥之官，仍為不息。

translations.literal: Yet the office of refining medicines still did not cease.
translations.idiomatic: Yet the office of refining medicines still did not cease.

sentences.zh: 久之，太祖意少懈，乃止。

translations.literal: After long time, Emperor Taizu's intent slackened somewhat, and then it stopped.
translations.idiomatic: After long time, Emperor Taizu's intent slackened somewhat, and then it stopped.

sentences.zh: 世祖時，道士寇謙之，字輔真，南雍州刺史讚之弟，自云寇恂之十三世孫。

translations.literal: In Emperor Shizu's time, the Daoist Kou Qianzhi, styled Fuzhen, younger brother of Prefect of Southern Yong Province Zan—himself said he was the thirteenth-generation descendant of Kou Xun.
translations.idiomatic: In Emperor Shizu's time, the Daoist Kou Qianzhi, styled Fuzhen, younger brother of Prefect of Southern Yong Province Zan—himself said he was the thirteenth-generation descendant of Kou Xun.

sentences.zh: 早好仙道，有絕俗之心。

translations.literal: From youth he loved the immortal Way, with a heart of transcending the vulgar.
translations.idiomatic: From youth he loved the immortal Way, with a heart set on transcending the vulgar world.

sentences.zh: 少修張魯之術，服食餌藥，歷年無效。

translations.literal: In youth he cultivated Zhang Lu's techniques, consuming and ingesting medicines and elixirs—year after year without effect.
translations.idiomatic: In youth he cultivated Zhang Lu's techniques, consuming medicines and elixirs—year after year without effect.

sentences.zh: 幽誠上達，有仙人成公興，不知何許人，至謙之從母家傭賃。

translations.literal: Hidden sincerity reached above; there was an immortal, Duke Cheng Xing—no one knew whence he came—who came to Qianzhi's maternal aunt's house as a hired laborer.
translations.idiomatic: Hidden sincerity reached above; there was an immortal, Duke Cheng Xing—no one knew whence he came—who came to Qianzhi's maternal aunt's house as a hired laborer.

sentences.zh: 謙之嘗覲其姨，見興形貌甚強，力作不倦，請回賃興代己使役。

translations.literal: Qianzhi once visited his aunt and saw Xing's form and appearance very strong, laboring without weariness; he requested to exchange and hire Xing to replace his own corvée service.
translations.idiomatic: Qianzhi once visited his aunt and saw Xing's form and appearance very strong, laboring without weariness; he requested to exchange and hire Xing to replace his own corvée service.

sentences.zh: 乃將還，令其開舍南辣田。

translations.literal: He then took him back and ordered him to open and cultivate the hot pepper field south of the house.
translations.idiomatic: He then took him back and ordered him to open and cultivate the hot pepper field south of the house.

sentences.zh: [39]謙之樹下坐算，興墾發致勤，[40]時來看算。

translations.literal: [39]Qianzhi sat beneath a tree calculating; Xing plowed and opened [the land] with utmost diligence;[40] from time to time he came to look at the calculation.
translations.idiomatic: [39]Qianzhi sat beneath a tree calculating; Xing plowed and opened the land with utmost diligence;[40] from time to time he came to look at the calculation.

sentences.zh: 謙之謂曰：「汝但力作，何為看此？」

translations.literal: Qianzhi said to him: 'You just labor hard—why look at this?'
translations.idiomatic: Qianzhi said to him: "You just labor hard—why look at this?"

sentences.zh: 二三日後，復來看之，如此不已。

translations.literal: After two or three days, he again came to look—thus without end.
translations.idiomatic: After two or three days, he again came to look—thus without end.

sentences.zh: 後謙之算七曜，有所不了，惘然自失。

translations.literal: Later when Qianzhi calculated the seven luminaries, there was something he could not resolve; he was dazed and lost.
translations.idiomatic: Later when Qianzhi calculated the seven luminaries, there was something he could not resolve; he was dazed and lost.

sentences.zh: 興謂謙之曰：「先生何為不懌？」

translations.literal: Xing said to Qianzhi: 'Sir, why are you not pleased?'
translations.idiomatic: Xing said to Qianzhi: "Sir, why are you displeased?"

sentences.zh: 謙之曰：「我學算累年，而近算周髀不合，以此自愧。

translations.literal: Qianzhi said: 'I have studied calculation for many years, yet recently my calculation of the Zhou Bi does not agree—because of this I am ashamed.
translations.idiomatic: Qianzhi said: "I have studied calculation for many years, yet recently my calculation of the Zhou Bi does not agree—because of this I am ashamed.

sentences.zh: 且非汝所知，何勞問也。」

translations.literal: Moreover it is not what you would know—why bother to ask?'
translations.idiomatic: Moreover it is not what you would know—why bother to ask?"

sentences.zh: 興曰：「先生試隨興語布之。」

translations.literal: Xing said: 'Sir, try following Xing's words and laying it out.'
translations.idiomatic: Xing said: "Sir, try following my words and laying it out."

sentences.zh: 俄然便決。

translations.literal: In a moment it was resolved.
translations.idiomatic: In a moment it was resolved.

sentences.zh: 謙之歎伏，不測興之深淺，請師事之。

translations.literal: Qianzhi sighed in submission, unable to fathom Xing's depth; he requested to take him as master.
translations.idiomatic: Qianzhi sighed in submission, unable to fathom Xing's depth; he requested to take him as master.

sentences.zh: 興固辭不肯，但求為謙之弟子。

translations.literal: Xing firmly declined and would not agree, only requesting to become Qianzhi's disciple.
translations.idiomatic: Xing firmly declined and would not agree, only requesting to become Qianzhi's disciple.

sentences.zh: 未幾，謂謙之曰：「先生有意學道，豈能與興隱遁？」

translations.literal: Before long, he said to Qianzhi: 'Sir, if you intend to study the Way, how can you hide away with Xing?'
translations.idiomatic: Before long, he said to Qianzhi: "Sir, if you intend to study the Way, how can you hide away with me?"

sentences.zh: 謙之欣然從之。

translations.literal: Qianzhi gladly followed him.
translations.idiomatic: Qianzhi gladly followed him.

sentences.zh: 興乃令謙之潔齋三日，共入華山。

translations.literal: Xing then ordered Qianzhi to purify and fast for three days, and together they entered Mount Hua.
translations.idiomatic: Xing then ordered Qianzhi to purify and fast for three days, and together they entered Mount Hua.

sentences.zh: 令謙之居一石室，自出採藥，還與謙之食藥，不復飢。

translations.literal: He ordered Qianzhi to dwell in a stone chamber; he himself went out to gather medicines, returned and shared food and medicine with Qianzhi—no longer hungry.
translations.idiomatic: He ordered Qianzhi to dwell in a stone chamber; he himself went out to gather medicines, returned and shared food and medicine with Qianzhi—they no longer hungered.

sentences.zh: 乃將謙之入嵩山。

translations.literal: He then took Qianzhi into Mount Song.
translations.idiomatic: He then took Qianzhi into Mount Song.

sentences.zh: 有三重石室，令謙之住第二重。

translations.literal: There were three tiers of stone chambers; he ordered Qianzhi to dwell in the second tier.
translations.idiomatic: There were three tiers of stone chambers; he ordered Qianzhi to dwell in the second tier.

sentences.zh: 歷年，興謂謙之曰：「興出後，當有人將藥來。

translations.literal: After years passed, Xing said to Qianzhi: 'After Xing goes out, there will be someone bringing medicine.
translations.idiomatic: After years passed, Xing said to Qianzhi: "After I go out, there will be someone bringing medicine.

sentences.zh: 得但食之，莫為疑怪。」

translations.literal: If you obtain it, just eat it—do not be suspicious or strange.'
translations.idiomatic: If you obtain it, just eat it—do not be suspicious or strange."

sentences.zh: 尋有人將藥而至，皆是毒蟲臭惡之物，謙之大懼出走。

translations.literal: Soon someone brought medicine— all were poisonous insects and foul, vile things; Qianzhi was greatly afraid and fled out.
translations.idiomatic: Soon someone brought medicine—all were poisonous insects and foul, vile things; Qianzhi was greatly afraid and fled out.

sentences.zh: 興還問狀，謙之具對，興歎息曰：「先生未便得仙，政可為帝王師耳。」

translations.literal: Xing returned and asked the circumstances; Qianzhi fully replied; Xing sighed and said: 'Sir, you are not yet able to attain immortality—you can only be a teacher to emperors.'
translations.idiomatic: Xing returned and asked the circumstances; Qianzhi fully replied; Xing sighed and said: "Sir, you are not yet able to attain immortality—you can only be a teacher to emperors."

sentences.zh: 興事謙之七年，而謂之曰：「興不得久留，明日中應去。

translations.literal: Xing served Qianzhi for seven years, then said to him: 'Xing cannot long remain; tomorrow at midday I should depart.
translations.idiomatic: Xing served Qianzhi for seven years, then said to him: "I cannot long remain; tomorrow at midday I should depart.

sentences.zh: 興亡後，先生幸為沐浴，自當有人見迎。」

translations.literal: After Xing's death, Sir, please kindly bathe [the body]—naturally there will be someone coming to welcome.'
translations.idiomatic: After my death, Sir, please kindly bathe the body—naturally there will be someone coming to welcome me."

sentences.zh: 興乃入第三重石室而卒。

translations.literal: Xing then entered the third-tier stone chamber and died.
translations.idiomatic: Xing then entered the third-tier stone chamber and died.

sentences.zh: 謙之躬自沐浴。

translations.literal: Qianzhi personally bathed [the body].
translations.idiomatic: Qianzhi personally bathed the body.

sentences.zh: 明日中，有叩石室者，謙之出視，見兩童子，一持法服，一持鉢及錫杖。

translations.literal: At midday the next day, someone knocked at the stone chamber; Qianzhi went out to look and saw two youths—one holding dharma-robes, one holding a bowl and tin staff.
translations.idiomatic: At midday the next day, someone knocked at the stone chamber; Qianzhi went out to look and saw two youths—one holding dharma-robes, one holding a bowl and tin staff.

sentences.zh: 謙之引入，至興尸所，興欻然而起，著衣持鉢、執杖而去。

translations.literal: Qianzhi led them in; arriving at Xing's corpse-place, Xing suddenly rose, put on robes, took the bowl and staff, and departed.
translations.idiomatic: Qianzhi led them in; arriving at Xing's corpse, Xing suddenly rose, put on robes, took the bowl and staff, and departed.

sentences.zh: 先是，有京兆灞城人王胡兒，其叔父亡，頗有靈異。

translations.literal: Before this, there was Wang Hu'er of Baling, Ba city in Jingzhao—his uncle had died, with considerable numinous strangeness.
translations.idiomatic: Before this, there was Wang Hu'er of Baling, Ba city in Jingzhao—his uncle had died, with considerable numinous strangeness.

sentences.zh: 曾將胡兒至嵩高別嶺，同行觀望，見金室玉堂，有一館尤珍麗，空而無人，題曰「成公興之館」。

translations.literal: He once took Hu'er to a separate ridge of Mount Song's heights; traveling together to look about, they saw a golden chamber and jade hall—with one lodge especially rare and beautiful, empty without people; inscribed: 'Lodge of Duke Cheng Xing.'
translations.idiomatic: He once took Hu'er to a separate ridge of Mount Song's heights; traveling together to look about, they saw a golden chamber and jade hall—with one lodge especially rare and beautiful, empty without people; inscribed: "Lodge of Duke Cheng Xing."

sentences.zh: 胡兒怪而問之，其叔父曰：「此是仙人成公興館，坐失火燒七間屋，被謫為寇謙之作弟子七年。」

translations.literal: Hu'er wondered and asked; his uncle said: 'This is the immortal Duke Cheng Xing's lodge—he sat and lost control of fire, burning seven rooms; he was demoted to be Kou Qianzhi's disciple for seven years.'
translations.idiomatic: Hu'er wondered and asked; his uncle said: "This is the immortal Duke Cheng Xing's lodge—he sat and lost control of fire, burning seven rooms; he was demoted to be Kou Qianzhi's disciple for seven years."

sentences.zh: 始知謙之精誠遠通，興乃仙者謫滿而去。

translations.literal: Then one knew Qianzhi's sincerity reached far; Xing was an immortal whose demotion-term was fulfilled and who departed.
translations.idiomatic: Then one knew Qianzhi's sincerity reached far; Xing was an immortal whose demotion-term was fulfilled and who departed.

sentences.zh: 謙之守志嵩岳，精專不懈，以神瑞二年十月乙卯，忽遇大神，乘雲駕龍，導從百靈，仙人玉女，左右侍衞，集止山頂，稱太上老君。

translations.literal: Qianzhi kept his resolve at Mount Song, concentrating exclusively without slackening; on the yimao day of the tenth month of the second year of Shenrui, he suddenly encountered a great spirit, riding clouds and driving dragons, with a hundred numinous beings as guides, immortal maidens left and right attending and guarding; gathering and stopping at the mountain peak, calling himself the Most High Lord Lao.
translations.idiomatic: Qianzhi kept his resolve at Mount Song, concentrating exclusively without slackening; on the yimao day of the tenth month of the second year of Shenrui, he suddenly encountered a great spirit, riding clouds and driving dragons, with a hundred numinous beings as guides, immortal maidens left and right attending and guarding; gathering and stopping at the mountain peak, calling himself the Most High Lord Lao.

sentences.zh: 謂謙之曰：「往辛亥年，嵩岳鎮靈集仙宮主，表天曹，稱自天師張陵去世已來，地上曠誠，[41]修善之人，無所師授。

translations.literal: He said to Qianzhi: 'In the past xinhai year, the Lord of the Numinous Assembly Palace at Mount Song memorialized the Heavenly Bureau, saying: Since Celestial Master Zhang Ling passed away, sincerity on earth has been vast and empty;[41] persons cultivating goodness have had no one to receive them as master.
translations.idiomatic: He said to Qianzhi: "In the past xinhai year, the Lord of the Numinous Assembly Palace at Mount Song memorialized the Heavenly Bureau, saying: Since Celestial Master Zhang Ling passed away, sincerity on earth has been vast and empty;[41] persons cultivating goodness have had no one to receive them as master.

sentences.zh: 嵩岳道士上谷寇謙之，立身直理，行合自然，才任軌範，首處師位，[42]吾故來觀汝，授汝天師之位，賜汝雲中音誦新科之誡二十卷。

translations.literal: The Mount Song Daoist Kou Qianzhi of Shanggu—upright in person and straight in principle, conduct matching nature, talent fitting the standard, first occupying the master's seat[42]—I therefore come to observe you, confer upon you the Celestial Master's seat, and bestow upon you twenty scrolls of new precepts in cloud-middle incantation.
translations.idiomatic: The Mount Song Daoist Kou Qianzhi of Shanggu—upright in person and straight in principle, conduct matching nature, talent fitting the standard, first occupying the master's seat[42]—I therefore come to observe you, confer upon you the Celestial Master's seat, and bestow upon you twenty scrolls of new precepts in cloud-middle incantation.

sentences.zh: 號曰『並進』。」

translations.literal: Called 'Concurrent Advancement.'
translations.idiomatic: Called "Concurrent Advancement."

sentences.zh: [43]言：「吾此經誡，自天地開闢已來，不傳於世，今運數應出。

translations.literal: [43]He said: 'These sutra-precepts of mine, since Heaven and Earth opened and unfolded, have not been transmitted in the world; now the cycle of fate responds and they should emerge.
translations.idiomatic: [43]He said: "These sutra-precepts of mine, since Heaven and Earth opened and unfolded, have not been transmitted in the world; now the cycle of fate responds and they should emerge.

sentences.zh: 汝宣吾新科，清整道教，除去三張偽法，租米錢稅，及男女合氣之術。

translations.literal: You shall proclaim my new precepts, purify and rectify the Daoist teaching, remove the false methods of the Three Zhangs, grain-rent and money-taxes, and the technique of male-female union of breaths.
translations.idiomatic: You shall proclaim my new precepts, purify and rectify the Daoist teaching, remove the false methods of the Three Zhangs, grain-rent and money-taxes, and the technique of male-female union of breaths.

sentences.zh: 大道清虛，豈有斯事。

translations.literal: The Great Way is pure and empty—how could there be such matters?
translations.idiomatic: The Great Way is pure and empty—how could there be such matters?

sentences.zh: 專以禮度為首，而加之以服食閉練。」

translations.literal: Take ritual norms as foremost, and add to them grain-avoidance and breath-sealing refinement.'
translations.idiomatic: Take ritual norms as foremost, and add to them grain-avoidance and breath-sealing refinement."

sentences.zh: 使王九疑人長客之等十二人，[44]授謙之服氣導引口訣之法。

translations.literal: He sent twelve persons including Chang Kezhi of Wangjiuyi to confer upon Qianzhi the oral formulas of qi-ingestion and daoyin.
translations.idiomatic: He sent twelve persons including Chang Kezhi of Wangjiuyi to confer upon Qianzhi the oral formulas of qi-ingestion and daoyin.

sentences.zh: 遂得辟穀，氣盛體輕，顏色殊麗。

translations.literal: Thereupon he attained grain-avoidance; his qi flourished and body lightened, his complexion exceptionally beautiful.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon he attained grain-avoidance; his qi flourished and body lightened, his complexion exceptionally beautiful.

sentences.zh: 弟子十餘人，皆得其術。

translations.literal: More than ten disciples all obtained his techniques.
translations.idiomatic: More than ten disciples all obtained his techniques.

sentences.zh: 泰常八年十月戊戌，有牧土上師李譜文來臨嵩岳，云：老君之玄孫，昔居代郡桑乾，以漢武之世得道，為牧土宮主，領治三十六土人鬼之政。

translations.literal: On the wuxu day of the tenth month of the eighth year of Taichang, the Pastoral Earth Superior Master Li Puwen came to Mount Song, saying: He was the Mysterious Grandson of Lord Lao; in the past he dwelt at Sanggan in Dai Commandery; in Emperor Wu of Han's age he attained the Way, becoming Lord of the Pastoral Earth Palace, governing the policies of thirty-six earths of men and ghosts.
translations.idiomatic: On the wuxu day of the tenth month of the eighth year of Taichang, the Pastoral Earth Superior Master Li Puwen came to Mount Song, saying he was the Mysterious Grandson of Lord Lao; in the past he dwelt at Sanggan in Dai Commandery; in Emperor Wu of Han's age he attained the Way, becoming Lord of the Pastoral Earth Palace, governing the policies of thirty-six earths of men and ghosts.

sentences.zh: 地方十八萬里有奇，蓋歷術一章之數也。

translations.literal: The territory was one hundred and eighty thousand li and more—covering the number of one chapter of calendrical calculation.
translations.idiomatic: The territory was 180,000 li and more—covering the number of one chapter of calendrical calculation.

sentences.zh: 其中為方萬里者有三百六十方。

translations.literal: Among them, those forming squares of ten thousand li each numbered three hundred and sixty squares.
translations.idiomatic: Among them, those forming squares of ten thousand li each numbered 360 squares.

sentences.zh: [45]遣弟子宣教，云嵩岳所統廣漢平土方萬里，以授謙之。

translations.literal: [45]He dispatched disciples to proclaim the teaching, saying the Guanghan Pingtu square of ten thousand li governed by Mount Song was conferred upon Qianzhi.
translations.idiomatic: [45]He dispatched disciples to proclaim the teaching, saying the Guanghan Pingtu square of ten thousand li governed by Mount Song was conferred upon Qianzhi.

sentences.zh: 作誥曰：「吾處天宮，敷演真法，處汝道年二十二歲，除十年為竟蒙，其餘十二年，教化雖無大功，且有百授之勞。

translations.literal: An edict was made: 'I dwell in the Heavenly Palace, spreading and expounding the true Law; you have been in the Way for twenty-two years; ten years are removed as childish obscurity—the remaining twelve years, though teaching without great merit, yet have the labor of a hundred transmissions.
translations.idiomatic: An edict was made: "I dwell in the Heavenly Palace, spreading and expounding the true Law; you have been in the Way for twenty-two years; ten years are removed as childish obscurity—the remaining twelve years, though teaching without great merit, yet have the labor of a hundred transmissions.

sentences.zh: [46]今賜汝遷入內宮，太真太寶九州真師、治鬼師、治民師、繼天師四錄。

translations.literal: [46]Now I bestow upon you transfer into the Inner Palace—the four registers of True Master of the Great Perfection and Great Treasure of the Nine Provinces, Master of Governing Ghosts, Master of Governing People, and Successor Celestial Master.
translations.idiomatic: [46]Now I bestow upon you transfer into the Inner Palace—the four registers of True Master of the Great Perfection and Great Treasure of the Nine Provinces, Master of Governing Ghosts, Master of Governing People, and Successor Celestial Master.

sentences.zh: 修勤不懈，依勞復遷。

translations.literal: Cultivate diligence without slackening; according to labor, further transfer.
translations.idiomatic: Cultivate diligence without slackening; according to labor, further transfer.

sentences.zh: 賜汝天中三真太文錄，劾召百神，以授弟子。

translations.literal: I bestow upon you the Great Perfection Great Text Register of the Three Perfections of the Heavenly Center, commanding and summoning the hundred spirits, to confer upon disciples.
translations.idiomatic: I bestow upon you the Great Perfection Great Text Register of the Three Perfections of the Heavenly Center, commanding and summoning the hundred spirits, to confer upon disciples.

sentences.zh: 文錄有五等，一曰陰陽太官，二曰正府真官，三曰正房真官，四曰宿宮散官，五曰並進錄主。

translations.literal: Text-registers have five grades: first, Yin-Yang Great Official; second, Correct Prefecture True Official; third, Correct Chamber True Official; fourth, Lodging Palace Dispersed Official; fifth, Concurrent Advancement Register Lord.
translations.idiomatic: Text-registers have five grades: first, Yin-Yang Great Official; second, Correct Prefecture True Official; third, Correct Chamber True Official; fourth, Lodging Palace Dispersed Official; fifth, Concurrent Advancement Register Lord.

sentences.zh: 壇位、禮拜、衣冠儀式各有差品。

translations.literal: Altar positions, worship, robes and caps, ritual forms—each has graded distinctions.
translations.idiomatic: Altar positions, worship, robes and caps, ritual forms—each has graded distinctions.

sentences.zh: 凡六十餘卷，號曰錄圖真經。

translations.literal: In all more than sixty scrolls, called the Register-Chart True Sutra.
translations.idiomatic: In all more than sixty scrolls, called the Register-Chart True Sutra.

sentences.zh: 付汝奉持，輔佐北方泰平真君，[47]出天宮靜輪之法。

translations.literal: Entrusted to you to uphold and assist the Northern True Lord of Great Peace[47]—issuing the Heavenly Palace Quiet Wheel Law.
translations.idiomatic: Entrusted to you to uphold and assist the Northern True Lord of Great Peace[47]—issuing the Heavenly Palace Quiet Wheel Law.

sentences.zh: [48]能興造克就，則起真仙矣。

translations.literal: [48]If you can raise and complete construction, then true immortals will arise.
translations.idiomatic: [48]If you can raise and complete construction, then true immortals will arise.

sentences.zh: [49]又地上生民，末劫垂及，其中行教甚難。

translations.literal: [49]Also, the living people on earth—the final kalpa hangs near; among them, carrying out teaching is very difficult.
translations.idiomatic: [49]Also, the living people on earth—the final kalpa hangs near; among them, carrying out teaching is very difficult.

sentences.zh: 但令男女立壇宇，朝夕禮拜，若家有嚴君，功及上世。

translations.literal: But order men and women to establish altar halls, worship morning and evening—if the household has a strict elder, merit reaches to upper generations.
translations.idiomatic: But order men and women to establish altar halls, worship morning and evening—if the household has a strict elder, merit reaches to upper generations.

sentences.zh: 其中能修身練藥，學長生之術，即為真君種民。」

translations.literal: Among them, those who can cultivate body and refine medicine, study the technique of long life—they are seed-people of the True Lord.'
translations.idiomatic: Among them, those who can cultivate body and refine medicine, study the technique of long life—they are seed-people of the True Lord."

sentences.zh: 藥別授方，銷練金丹、雲英、八石、玉漿之法，皆有決要。

translations.literal: Medicines were separately conferred in formulas—methods of dissolving and refining golden elixir, cloud-essence, eight stones, and jade-broth—all have decisive essentials.
translations.idiomatic: Medicines were separately conferred in formulas—methods of dissolving and refining golden elixir, cloud-essence, eight stones, and jade-broth—all have decisive essentials.

sentences.zh: 上師李君手筆有數篇，其餘，皆正真書曹趙道覆所書。

translations.literal: Superior Master Lord Li's own hand had several scrolls; the rest were all written by the True Writing Clerk of the Correct Perfection, Cao Daofu.
translations.idiomatic: Superior Master Lord Li's own hand had several scrolls; the rest were all written by the True Writing Clerk of the Correct Perfection, Cao Daofu.

sentences.zh: 古文鳥迹，篆隸雜體，辭義約辯，婉而成章。

translations.literal: Ancient script in bird-tracks, seal and clerical mixed forms—word-meaning concise and eloquent, graceful and forming chapters.
translations.idiomatic: Ancient script in bird-tracks, seal and clerical mixed forms—word-meaning concise and eloquent, graceful and forming chapters.

sentences.zh: 大自與世禮相準，擇賢推德，信者為先，勤者次之。

translations.literal: Greatly from the beginning matching worldly rites—choosing the worthy and promoting virtue, the faithful come first, the diligent second.
translations.idiomatic: Greatly from the beginning matching worldly rites—choosing the worthy and promoting virtue, the faithful come first, the diligent second.

sentences.zh: 又言二儀之間有三十六天，中有三十六宮，[50]宮有一主。

translations.literal: Also it says: Between the Two Principles there are thirty-six Heavens; within them are thirty-six palaces;[50] each palace has one lord.
translations.idiomatic: Also it says: Between the Two Principles there are thirty-six Heavens; within them are thirty-six palaces;[50] each palace has one lord.

sentences.zh: 最高者無極至尊，次曰大至真尊，次天覆地載陰陽真尊。

translations.literal: The highest is the Limitless Supreme; next is the Great Perfect True; next the Heaven-Covering Earth-Bearing Yin-Yang True.
translations.idiomatic: The highest is the Limitless Supreme; next is the Great Perfect True; next the Heaven-Covering Earth-Bearing Yin-Yang True.

sentences.zh: 次洪正真尊，姓趙名道隱，以殷時得道，牧土之師也。

translations.literal: Next the Vast Correct True, surname Zhao named Daoyin—he attained the Way in the Yin age, master of the Pastoral Earth.
translations.idiomatic: Next the Vast Correct True, surname Zhao named Daoyin—he attained the Way in the Yin age, master of the Pastoral Earth.

sentences.zh: 牧土之來，赤松、王喬之倫，及韓終、張安世、劉根、張陵，近世仙者，並為翼從。

translations.literal: When the Pastoral Earth came, Chisongzi, Wang Qiao and their kind, and Han Zhong, Zhang Anshi, Liu Gen, Zhang Ling—recent-age immortals—all were wing-followers.
translations.idiomatic: When the Pastoral Earth came, Chisongzi, Wang Qiao and their kind, and Han Zhong, Zhang Anshi, Liu Gen, Zhang Ling—recent-age immortals—all were wing-followers.

sentences.zh: 牧土命謙之為子，與群仙結為徒友。

translations.literal: The Pastoral Earth ordered Qianzhi as son, and with the host of immortals formed master-disciple friendship.
translations.idiomatic: The Pastoral Earth ordered Qianzhi as son, and with the host of immortals formed master-disciple friendship.

sentences.zh: 幽冥之事，世所不了，謙之具問，一一告焉。

translations.literal: Matters of the dark and hidden—what the world cannot understand—Qianzhi fully asked; one by one he was told.
translations.idiomatic: Matters of the dark and hidden—what the world cannot understand—Qianzhi fully asked; one by one he was told.

sentences.zh: 經云：佛者，昔於西胡得道，在三十二天，[51]為延真宮主。

translations.literal: The sutra says: The Buddha—in the past attained the Way in Western Hu, in the thirty-second Heaven,[51] as Lord of the Extended Perfection Palace.
translations.idiomatic: The sutra says: The Buddha—in the past attained the Way in Western Hu, in the thirty-second Heaven,[51] as Lord of the Extended Perfection Palace.

sentences.zh: 勇猛苦教，故其弟子皆髠形染衣，斷絕人道，諸天衣服悉然。

translations.literal: Bold and brave in bitter teaching, therefore his disciples all shave their heads and dye their robes, cutting off human relations—the clothes of all heavens are likewise.
translations.idiomatic: Bold and brave in bitter teaching, therefore his disciples all shave their heads and dye their robes, cutting off human relations—the clothes of all heavens are likewise.

sentences.zh: 始光初，奉其書而獻之，世祖乃令謙之止於張曜之所，供其食物。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Shiguang, [Qianzhi] presented his books and offered them; Emperor Shizu thereupon ordered Qianzhi to stay at Zhang Yao's place, supplying his food.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Shiguang, [Qianzhi] presented his books and offered them; Emperor Shizu thereupon ordered Qianzhi to stay at Zhang Yao's place, supplying his food.

sentences.zh: 時朝野聞之，若存若亡，未全信也。

translations.literal: At the time court and countryside heard of it—as if present, as if absent—not fully believing.
translations.idiomatic: At the time court and countryside heard of it—as if present, as if absent—not fully believing.

sentences.zh: 崔浩獨異其言，因師事之，受其法術。

translations.literal: Cui Hao alone found his words strange; he thereupon took him as master, receiving his dharma-techniques.
translations.idiomatic: Cui Hao alone found his words strange; he thereupon took him as master, receiving his dharma-techniques.

sentences.zh: 於是上疏，讚明其事曰：「臣聞聖王受命，則有大應。

translations.literal: Thereupon he submitted a memorial, praising and clarifying the matter: 'Your subject has heard: when a sage king receives the mandate, then there are great responses.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon he submitted a memorial, praising and clarifying the matter: "Your subject has heard: when a sage king receives the mandate, then there are great responses.

sentences.zh: 而河圖、洛書，皆寄言於蟲獸之文。

translations.literal: Yet the Yellow River Chart and Luo River Writ are both entrusted in words of insects and beasts.
translations.idiomatic: Yet the Yellow River Chart and Luo River Writ are both entrusted in words of insects and beasts.

sentences.zh: 未若今日人神接對，手筆粲然，辭旨深妙，自古無比。

translations.literal: They are not like today—human and spirit face to face, hand-writing brilliant, word-intent deep and wondrous, without parallel since antiquity.
translations.idiomatic: They are not like today—human and spirit face to face, hand-writing brilliant, word-intent deep and wondrous, without parallel since antiquity.

sentences.zh: 昔漢高雖復英聖，四皓猶或耻之，不為屈節。

translations.literal: In the past Emperor Gaozu of Han, though again heroic and sage, the Four Whiteheads were still ashamed and would not bend their integrity.
translations.idiomatic: In the past Emperor Gaozu of Han, though again heroic and sage, the Four Whiteheads were still ashamed and would not bend their integrity.

sentences.zh: 今清德隱仙，不召自至。

translations.literal: Now the pure virtue hidden immortal comes without being summoned.
translations.idiomatic: Now the pure virtue hidden immortal comes without being summoned.

sentences.zh: 斯誠陛下侔蹤軒黃，應天之符也，豈可以世俗常談，而忽上靈之命。

translations.literal: This is truly Your Majesty matching the traces of Xuanyuan and the Yellow Emperor, the talisman responding to Heaven—how can one neglect the command of upper spirits with worldly common talk?
translations.idiomatic: This is truly Your Majesty matching the traces of Xuanyuan and the Yellow Emperor, the talisman responding to Heaven—how can one neglect the command of upper spirits with worldly common talk?

sentences.zh: 臣竊懼之。」

translations.literal: Your subject secretly fears it.'
translations.idiomatic: Your subject secretly fears it."

sentences.zh: 世祖欣然，乃使謁者奉玉帛牲牢，祭嵩岳，迎致其餘弟子在山中者。

translations.literal: Emperor Shizu was pleased; he then sent the Herald bearing jade silks and sacrificial animals to sacrifice at Mount Song, welcoming and bringing the remaining disciples in the mountains.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Shizu was pleased; he then sent the Herald bearing jade silks and sacrificial animals to sacrifice at Mount Song, welcoming and bringing the remaining disciples in the mountains.

sentences.zh: 於是崇奉天師，顯揚新法，宣布天下，道業大行。

translations.literal: Thereupon he honored and upheld the Celestial Master, displayed and spread the new Law, proclaimed it throughout the empire—the Way's work greatly flourished.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon he honored and upheld the Celestial Master, displayed and spread the new Law, proclaimed it throughout the empire—the Way's work greatly flourished.

sentences.zh: 浩事天師，拜禮甚謹。

translations.literal: Hao served the Celestial Master, bowing and performing rites with utmost reverence.
translations.idiomatic: Hao served the Celestial Master, bowing and performing rites with utmost reverence.

sentences.zh: 人或譏之，浩聞之曰：「昔張釋之為王生結襪。

translations.literal: Some ridiculed him; Hao, hearing it, said: 'In the past Zhang Shizhi tied socks for Lord Wang.
translations.idiomatic: Some ridiculed him; Hao, hearing it, said: "In the past Zhang Shizhi tied socks for Lord Wang.

sentences.zh: 吾雖才非賢哲，今奉天師，足以不愧於古人矣。」

translations.literal: Though my talent is not that of worthies and sages, now serving the Celestial Master, it suffices not to be ashamed before the ancients.'
translations.idiomatic: Though my talent is not that of worthies and sages, now serving the Celestial Master, it suffices not to be ashamed before the ancients."

sentences.zh: 及嵩高道士四十餘人至，遂起天師道場於京城之東南，重壇五層，遵其新經之制。

translations.literal: When more than forty Mount Song daoists arrived, they thereupon raised the Celestial Master's dharma-ground southeast of the capital city—a heavy altar of five tiers, following the new sutra's regulations.
translations.idiomatic: When more than forty Mount Song daoists arrived, they thereupon raised the Celestial Master's dharma-ground southeast of the capital city—a heavy altar of five tiers, following the new sutra's regulations.

sentences.zh: 給道士百二十人衣食，齊肅祈請，六時禮拜，月設厨會數千人。

translations.literal: They gave one hundred and twenty daoists food and clothing; solemnly they prayed and requested; six times daily they bowed and worshipped; each month they set up kitchen assemblies of several thousand persons.
translations.idiomatic: They gave 120 daoists food and clothing; solemnly they prayed and requested; six times daily they bowed and worshipped; each month they set up kitchen assemblies of several thousand persons.

sentences.zh: 世祖將討赫連昌，太尉長孫嵩難之，世祖乃問幽徵於謙之。

translations.literal: Emperor Shizu was about to campaign against Helian Chang; Grand Commandant Changsun Song found it difficult; the emperor then asked Qianzhi about hidden omens.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Shizu was about to campaign against Helian Chang; Grand Commandant Changsun Song found it difficult; the emperor then asked Qianzhi about hidden omens.

sentences.zh: 謙之對曰：「必克。

translations.literal: Qianzhi replied: 'Certainly victorious.
translations.idiomatic: Qianzhi replied: "Certainly victorious.

sentences.zh: 陛下神武應期，天經下治，當以兵定九州，後文先武，以成太平真君。」

translations.literal: Your Majesty's divine martial responds to the age; Heaven's norm descends to govern—you should with arms settle the Nine Provinces; afterward culture, before martial—thereby completing the True Lord of Great Peace.'
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty's divine martial responds to the age; Heaven's norm descends to govern—you should with arms settle the Nine Provinces; afterward culture, before martial—thereby completing the True Lord of Great Peace."

sentences.zh: 真君三年，謙之奏曰：「今陛下以真君御世，建靜輪天宮之法，開古以來，未之有也。

translations.literal: In the third year of Zhenjun, Qianzhi memorialized: 'Now Your Majesty with the True Lord governs the age, establishing the Quiet Wheel Heavenly Palace Law—opening since antiquity, never before existing.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Zhenjun, Qianzhi memorialized: "Now Your Majesty with the True Lord governs the age, establishing the Quiet Wheel Heavenly Palace Law—opening since antiquity, never before existing.

sentences.zh: 應登受符書，以彰聖德。」

translations.literal: You should ascend and receive talisman-texts, to display sage virtue.'
translations.idiomatic: You should ascend and receive talisman-texts, to display sage virtue."

sentences.zh: 世祖從之。

translations.literal: Emperor Shizu followed it.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Shizu followed it.

sentences.zh: 於是親至道壇，受符錄。

translations.literal: Thereupon he personally arrived at the dharma-altar and received talisman-registers.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon he personally arrived at the dharma-altar and received talisman-registers.

sentences.zh: 備法駕，旗幟盡青，以從道家之色也。

translations.literal: Fully equipped with the imperial carriage, banners and flags all green—to follow the Daoist family's color.
translations.idiomatic: Fully equipped with the imperial carriage, banners and flags all green—to follow the Daoist family's color.

sentences.zh: 自後諸帝，每即位皆如之。

translations.literal: From afterward, every emperor upon accession did likewise.
translations.idiomatic: Thereafter, every emperor upon taking the throne did the same.

sentences.zh: 恭宗見謙之奏造靜輪宮，必令其高不聞雞鳴狗吠之聲，欲上與天神交接，功役萬計，經年不成。

translations.literal: Prince Gong saw Qianzhi's memorial to build the Quiet Wheel Palace, insisting it be made so high that cockcrow and dog bark could not be heard, intending that the emperor ascend to join with celestial spirits—labor in the tens of thousands; a full year passed and it was still unfinished.
translations.idiomatic: When Prince Gong saw Kou Qianzhi's memorial proposing the Quiet Wheel Palace—built so high that neither cockcrow nor dog bark could be heard, so the emperor might ascend and commune with celestial spirits—he noted that the project consumed tens of thousands of laborers and remained unfinished after a full year.

sentences.zh: 乃言於世祖曰：「人天道殊，卑高定分。

translations.literal: He then spoke to Emperor Shizu, saying: 'The paths of men and Heaven differ; high and low have fixed stations.
translations.idiomatic: He then said to Emperor Shizu, "The paths of men and Heaven differ; high and low have fixed stations.

sentences.zh: 今謙之欲要以無成之期，說以不然之事，財力費損，百姓疲勞，無乃不可乎？

translations.literal: Now Qianzhi would hold you to a deadline that cannot be fulfilled, persuading you with things that cannot be so—wealth and resources wasted, the people worn out—is this not impermissible?
translations.idiomatic: Now Qianzhi would bind you to a deadline that cannot be met, persuading you with what cannot be so—wealth squandered, the people exhausted. Surely this will not do?

sentences.zh: 必如其言，未若因東山萬仞之上，為功差易。」

translations.literal: Even if one must follow his words, would it not be easier to build upon the ten-thousand-ren heights of East Mountain?'
translations.idiomatic: Even if his plan were followed, would it not be easier to build on the ten-thousand-ren heights of East Mountain?"

sentences.zh: 世祖深然恭宗之言，但以崔浩贊成，難違其意，沉吟者久之，乃曰：「吾亦知其無成，事既爾，何惜五三百功。」
