translations.literal: Emperor Shizu deeply approved Prince Gong's words, but because Cui Hao had endorsed it, it was hard to go against his intent; he pondered a long while, then said: 'I too know it will not succeed. Since matters have come to this, what is the loss of five or six hundred units of labor?'
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Shizu deeply agreed with Prince Gong, but since Cui Hao had endorsed the project, he could hardly refuse. He pondered a long while, then said, "I too know it will never succeed. Since matters have come to this, what harm in spending five or six hundred units of labor?"

sentences.zh: 九年，謙之卒，葬以道士之禮。

translations.literal: In the ninth year, Qianzhi died and was buried with daoist rites.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year, Qianzhi died and was buried with daoist rites.

sentences.zh: 先於未亡，謂諸弟子曰：「及謙之在，汝曹可求遷錄。

translations.literal: Before his death, he told his disciples: 'While Qianzhi remains, you may seek transfer registers.
translations.idiomatic: Before he died, he told his disciples, "While I am still here, you may seek transfer registers.

sentences.zh: 吾去之後，天宮真難就。」

translations.literal: After I am gone, the Heavenly Palace will truly be hard to attain.'
translations.idiomatic: After I am gone, the Heavenly Palace will truly be hard to attain."

sentences.zh: 復遇設會之日，更布二席於上師坐前。

translations.literal: On a day when a feast was held, he again spread two mats before the seat of the supreme master.
translations.idiomatic: On a day when a feast was held, he again laid out two mats before the seat of the supreme master.

sentences.zh: 弟子問其故，謙之曰：「仙官來。」

translations.literal: Disciples asked the reason; Qianzhi said: 'Immortal officials are coming.'
translations.idiomatic: When disciples asked why, Qianzhi said, "Immortal officials are coming."

sentences.zh: 是夜卒。

translations.literal: That night he died.
translations.idiomatic: That night he died.

sentences.zh: 前一日，忽言「吾氣息不接，腹中大痛」，而行止如常，至明旦便終。

translations.literal: The day before, he had suddenly said, 'My breath fails to connect; great pain in my belly,' yet his movements remained as usual; by dawn the next day he was dead.
translations.idiomatic: The day before, he had suddenly said, "My breath fails to connect; great pain in my belly," yet carried on as usual; by dawn the next day he was dead.

sentences.zh: 須臾，口中氣狀若烟雲，上出窗中，至天半乃消。

translations.literal: In a moment, breath from his mouth shaped like smoke and cloud rose through the window and, reaching mid-heaven, dispersed.
translations.idiomatic: In a moment, breath from his mouth like smoke and cloud rose through the window and, reaching mid-heaven, dispersed.

sentences.zh: 屍體引長，弟子量之，八尺三寸。

translations.literal: The corpse stretched longer; disciples measured it—eight feet three inches.
translations.idiomatic: The corpse stretched; disciples measured it at eight feet three inches.

sentences.zh: 三日已後，稍縮，至斂量之，長六寸。

translations.literal: After three days it gradually shrank; when measured for burial, it was six inches long.
translations.idiomatic: After three days it gradually shrank; measured for burial, it was six inches long.

sentences.zh: [52]於是諸弟子以為尸解變化而去，不死也。

translations.literal: [52] Thereupon the disciples took it that he had shed the corpse, transformed, and departed—not dead.
translations.idiomatic: [52] Thereupon the disciples believed he had shed his corpse, transformed, and departed—not that he had died.

sentences.zh: 時有京兆人韋文秀，隱於嵩高，徵詣京師。

translations.literal: At the time there was Wei Wenxiu of Jingzhao, who lived in seclusion on Mount Song; he was summoned to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: At the time there was Wei Wenxiu of Jingzhao, living in seclusion on Mount Song, who was summoned to the capital.

sentences.zh: 世祖曾問方士金丹事，多曰可成。

translations.literal: Emperor Shizu had once questioned adepts about the golden elixir; most said it could be achieved.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Shizu had once questioned adepts about the golden elixir; most said it could be achieved.

sentences.zh: 文秀對曰：「神道幽昧，變化難測，可以闇遇，難以豫期。

translations.literal: Wenxiu replied: 'The divine Way is obscure; transformation is hard to fathom. One may meet it in darkness, but cannot foretell it.
translations.idiomatic: Wenxiu replied, "The divine Way is obscure; transformation is hard to fathom. One may encounter it unawares, but cannot foretell it.

sentences.zh: 臣昔者受教於先師，曾聞其事，未之為也。」

translations.literal: Your servant once received instruction from his former master and heard tell of the matter, but has never practiced it.'
translations.idiomatic: Your servant once received instruction from his former master and heard of the matter, but has never practiced it."

sentences.zh: 世祖以文秀關右豪族，風操溫雅，言對有方，遣與尚書崔賾詣王屋山合丹，竟不能就。

translations.literal: Emperor Shizu, because Wenxiu came from a great clan west of the Pass, had refined conduct and gentle speech, and answered with propriety, sent him with the Minister Cui Yan to Mount Wangwu to compound the elixir—but in the end they could not succeed.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Shizu, finding Wenxiu a man of a great clan west of the Pass, with refined conduct, gentle speech, and apt replies, sent him with Minister Cui Yan to Mount Wangwu to compound the elixir—but in the end they could not succeed.

sentences.zh: 時方士至者前後數人。

translations.literal: Adepts who arrived at the time numbered several, one after another.
translations.idiomatic: Several adepts arrived during this period, one after another.

sentences.zh: 河東祁纖，好相人。

translations.literal: Qi Xian of Hedong was skilled at physiognomy.
translations.idiomatic: Qi Xian of Hedong was skilled at physiognomy.

sentences.zh: 世祖賢之，拜纖上大夫。

translations.literal: Emperor Shizu respected him and appointed Xian Senior Grand Master.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Shizu respected him and appointed Xian Senior Grand Master.

sentences.zh: 潁陽絳略、聞喜吳劭，道引養氣，積年百餘歲，神氣不衰。

translations.literal: Jiang Lüe of Yingyang and Wu Shao of Wenxi practiced daoyin and nourishing qi; for over a hundred years their spirit and vigor did not decline.
translations.idiomatic: Jiang Lüe of Yingyang and Wu Shao of Wenxi had practiced daoyin and nourishing qi for over a hundred years; their spirit and vigor did not decline.

sentences.zh: 恒農閻平仙，博覽百家之言，然不能達其意，辭占應對，義旨可聽。

translations.literal: Yan Pingxian of Hengnong had read widely among the hundred schools, yet could not penetrate their meaning; in divination by words and in reply, the purport was worth hearing.
translations.idiomatic: Yan Pingxian of Hengnong had read widely among the hundred schools but could not grasp their meaning; in divination and reply, his points were worth hearing.

sentences.zh: 世祖欲授之官，終辭不受。

translations.literal: Emperor Shizu wished to grant him office, but he consistently declined and would not accept.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Shizu wished to grant him office, but he consistently declined.

sentences.zh: 扶風魯祈，遭赫連屈孑暴虐，避地寒山，教授弟子數百人，好方術，少嗜慾。

translations.literal: Lu Qi of Fufeng, suffering Helian Quxie's brutal tyranny, fled to Cold Mountain, taught several hundred disciples, loved alchemical arts, and had few desires.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Qi of Fufeng, fleeing Helian Quxie's brutal tyranny, took refuge on Cold Mountain, taught several hundred disciples, loved alchemical arts, and had few desires.

sentences.zh: 河東羅崇之，常餌松脂，不食五穀，自稱受道於中條山。

translations.literal: Luo Chongzhi of Hedong regularly consumed pine resin, ate no grain, and claimed to have received the Way on Mount Zhongtiao.
translations.idiomatic: Luo Chongzhi of Hedong regularly consumed pine resin, ate no grain, and claimed to have received the Way on Mount Zhongtiao.

sentences.zh: 世祖令崇還鄉里，立壇祈請。

translations.literal: Emperor Shizu ordered Chongzhi to return to his native place and set up an altar to pray and petition.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Shizu ordered Chongzhi to return to his native place and set up an altar to pray and petition.

sentences.zh: 崇云：「條山有穴，與崐崘、蓬萊相屬。

translations.literal: Chongzhi said: 'On Mount Tiao there is a cave connected to Kunlun and Penglai.
translations.idiomatic: Chongzhi said, "On Mount Tiao there is a cave connected to Kunlun and Penglai.

sentences.zh: 入穴中得見仙人，與之往來。」

translations.literal: Entering the cave, one may see immortals and go back and forth with them.'
translations.idiomatic: Entering the cave, one may see immortals and go back and forth with them."

sentences.zh: 詔令河東郡給所須。

translations.literal: An edict ordered Hedong commandery to supply what was required.
translations.idiomatic: An edict ordered Hedong Commandery to supply what was required.

sentences.zh: 崇入穴，行百餘步，遂窮。

translations.literal: Chongzhi entered the cave and walked more than a hundred steps, then the way ended.
translations.idiomatic: Chongzhi entered the cave and walked more than a hundred steps before the passage ended.

sentences.zh: 後召至，有司以崇誣罔不道，奏治之。

translations.literal: Later he was summoned again; the authorities, charging Chongzhi with deceit and heterodox conduct, memorialized for punishment.
translations.idiomatic: Later he was summoned again; the authorities charged Chongzhi with deceit and heterodox conduct and memorialized for punishment.

sentences.zh: 世祖曰：「崇修道之人，豈至欺妄以詐於世，或傳聞不審，而至於此。

translations.literal: Emperor Shizu said: 'Chongzhi is a man who cultivates the Way—how could he stoop to falsehood to cheat the world? Perhaps hearsay was inexact and led to this.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Shizu said, "Chongzhi is a man who cultivates the Way—how could he stoop to deceit the world? Perhaps hearsay was inaccurate and led to this.

sentences.zh: 古之君子，進人以禮，退人以禮。

translations.literal: The gentlemen of old advanced men with rites and dismissed men with rites.
translations.idiomatic: The gentlemen of old advanced men with rites and dismissed men with rites.

sentences.zh: 今治之，是傷朕待賢之意。」

translations.literal: Now to punish him would wound Our intent in treating the worthy.'
translations.idiomatic: To punish him now would wound Our intent in treating the worthy."

sentences.zh: 遂赦之。

translations.literal: He was therefore pardoned.
translations.idiomatic: He was therefore pardoned.

sentences.zh: 又有東萊人王道翼，少有絕俗之志，隱韓信山，四十餘年，斷粟食荽，[53]通達經章，書符錄。

translations.literal: There was also Wang Daoyi of Donglai, who from youth had an ambition to transcend the vulgar; he hid on Mount Hanxin for more than forty years, cutting off grain and eating coriander,[53] mastering scriptural chapters, and writing talismans and registers.
translations.idiomatic: There was also Wang Daoyi of Donglai, who from youth aspired to transcend the vulgar; he lived in seclusion on Mount Hanxin for more than forty years, cutting off grain and eating coriander,[53] mastering scriptural chapters, and writing talismans and registers.

sentences.zh: 常隱居深山，不交世務，年六十餘。

translations.literal: He always lived deep in the mountains and had no commerce with worldly affairs; he was over sixty.
translations.idiomatic: He always lived deep in the mountains, had no commerce with worldly affairs, and was over sixty.

sentences.zh: 顯祖聞而召焉。

translations.literal: Emperor Xianzu heard of him and summoned him.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xianzu heard of him and summoned him.

sentences.zh: 青州刺史韓頹遣使就山徵之，翼乃赴都。

translations.literal: Han Yan, governor of Qing Province, sent envoys to the mountain to summon him; Daoyi then came to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Han Yan, governor of Qing Province, sent envoys to the mountain to summon him; Daoyi then came to the capital.

sentences.zh: 顯祖以其仍守本操，遂令僧曹給衣食，以終其身。

translations.literal: Emperor Xianzu, because he still kept to his original resolve, ordered the Monks' Office to provide food and clothing for the rest of his life.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xianzu, seeing that he still held to his original resolve, ordered the Monks' Office to provide food and clothing for the rest of his life.

sentences.zh: 太和十五年秋，詔曰：「夫至道無形，虛寂為主。

translations.literal: In the autumn of the fifteenth year of Taihe, an edict said: 'The utmost Way is formless; emptiness and stillness are its lord.
translations.idiomatic: In the autumn of the fifteenth year of Taihe, an edict said, "The utmost Way is formless; emptiness and stillness are its lord.

sentences.zh: 自有漢以後，置立壇祠，先朝以其至順可歸，用立寺宇。

translations.literal: Since Han times altars have been established, and former dynasties, finding their utmost compliance fit to be honored, erected temple halls.
translations.idiomatic: Since Han times altars have been established; former dynasties, finding their utmost compliance fit to be honored, erected temple halls.

sentences.zh: 昔京城之內，居舍尚希。

translations.literal: In former days within the capital, dwellings were still sparse.
translations.idiomatic: In former days within the capital, dwellings were still sparse.

sentences.zh: 今者里宅櫛比，人神猥湊，非所以祗崇至法，清敬神道。

translations.literal: Now houses stand row upon row; men and spirits crowd together—this is not the way to reverence the supreme Law and keep pure respect for the divine Way.
translations.idiomatic: Now houses stand row upon row; men and spirits crowd together—this is not the way to reverence the supreme Law and keep pure respect for the divine Way.

sentences.zh: 可移於都南桑乾之陰，岳山之陽，永置其所。

translations.literal: It may be moved to the south of the capital, on the shady side of the Sanggan, on the sunny side of Mount Yue, and permanently established there.
translations.idiomatic: It shall be moved south of the capital, on the shady side of the Sanggan and the sunny side of Mount Yue, and permanently established there.

sentences.zh: 給戶五十，以供齋祀之用，仍名為崇虛寺。

translations.literal: Grant fifty households to supply offerings for pure sacrifice, and still name it the Temple of Revering Emptiness.
translations.idiomatic: Grant fifty households to supply offerings for pure sacrifice, and still name it the Temple of Revering Emptiness.

sentences.zh: 可召諸州隱士，員滿九十人。」

translations.literal: Recluses from the provinces may be summoned, the quota filled to ninety persons.'
translations.idiomatic: Recluses from the provinces may be summoned until the quota of ninety is filled."

sentences.zh: 遷洛移鄴，踵如故事。

translations.literal: When the capital moved to Luoyang, Ye was treated according to precedent.
translations.idiomatic: When the capital moved to Luoyang, Ye was treated according to precedent.

sentences.zh: 其道壇在南郊，方二百步，以正月七日、七月七日、十月十五日，壇主、道士、哥人一百六人，[54]以行拜祠之禮。

translations.literal: Its Way-altar lay in the southern suburb, two hundred paces square; on the seventh day of the first, seventh, and tenth months, the altar master, daoists, and ge singers—one hundred six persons [54]—performed bowing and sacrificial rites.
translations.idiomatic: Its Way-altar lay in the southern suburb, two hundred paces square; on the seventh day of the first, seventh, and tenth months, the altar master, daoists, and ge singers—one hundred six persons [54]—performed bowing and sacrificial rites.

sentences.zh: 諸道士罕能精至，又無才術可高。

translations.literal: Daoists could rarely achieve refined attainment, and none had talent or learning of high standing.
translations.idiomatic: Daoists could rarely achieve refined attainment, and none had talent or learning of high standing.

sentences.zh: 武定六年，有司執奏罷之。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Wuding, the authorities memorialized requesting abolition.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year of Wuding, the authorities memorialized requesting abolition.

sentences.zh: 其有道術，如河東張遠遊、河間趙靜通等，齊文襄王別置館京師而禮接焉。

translations.literal: Those who possessed the Way's arts, such as Zhang Yuanyou of Hedong and Zhao Jingtong of Hejian, were separately given lodges in the capital by Prince Wenxiang of Qi and received with courtesy.
translations.idiomatic: Those who possessed the Way's arts, such as Zhang Yuanyou of Hedong and Zhao Jingtong of Hejian, were separately given lodges in the capital by Prince Wenxiang of Qi and received with courtesy.

sentences.zh: 校勘記

translations.literal: Collation notes
translations.idiomatic: Collation notes

sentences.zh: 項有日光 諸本作「頂有白光」，冊府卷五一

translations.literal: Light on the nape like sunlight: various editions read 'white light on the crown'; Cefu yuangui juan 51
translations.idiomatic: Light on the nape like sunlight: various editions read "white light on the crown"; Cefu yuangui, juan 51

sentences.zh: 〈五六六頁〉
作「頂有日光」，廣弘明集卷二錄釋老志如上摘句。

translations.literal: reads 'sunlight on the crown'; Guang hongming ji juan 2 quotes the Treatise on Buddhism and Daoism as above.
translations.idiomatic: reads "sunlight on the crown"; Guang hongming ji, juan 2, quotes the Treatise on Buddhism and Daoism as above.

sentences.zh: 按水經注卷一六穀水篇作「項佩日光」，洛陽伽藍記卷四白馬寺條作「項背日月光明」，牟子理惑論作「身有日光」。

translations.literal: According to Shui jing zhu juan 16, Gushui pian, it reads 'sunlight hung on the nape'; Luoyang qielan ji juan 4, White Horse Temple entry, reads 'sun and moon light on the nape and back'; Mouzi lihuo lun reads 'the body had sunlight.'
translations.idiomatic: According to Shui jing zhu, juan 16, Gushui pian, it reads "sunlight hung on the nape"; Luoyang qielan ji, juan 4, White Horse Temple entry, reads "sun and moon light on the nape and back"; Mouzi lihuo lun reads "the body had sunlight."

sentences.zh: 可證廣弘明集引志是，今據改。

translations.literal: This confirms that Guang hongming ji's citation of the Treatise is correct; the text is amended accordingly.
translations.idiomatic: This confirms that Guang hongming ji's citation of the Treatise is correct; the text is amended accordingly.

sentences.zh: 漢因立白馬寺於洛城雍門西 諸本「門」作「關」。

translations.literal: Han therefore established the White Horse Temple west of Yong Gate in Luoyang: various editions read 'pass' for 'gate.'
translations.idiomatic: Han therefore established the White Horse Temple west of Yong Gate in Luoyang: various editions read "pass" for "gate."

sentences.zh: 按水經注穀水篇、伽藍記並稱北魏洛陽之西陽門即漢之「雍門」，牟子理惑論云：「時於洛陽城西雍門外起佛寺。」

translations.literal: According to Shui jing zhu, Gushui pian, and Qielan ji, both state that the Xiyang Gate of Northern Wei Luoyang was Han's 'Yong Gate'; Mouzi lihuo lun says: 'At the time a Buddhist temple was raised outside Yong Gate west of Luoyang city.'
translations.idiomatic: According to Shui jing zhu, Gushui pian, and Qielan ji, the Xiyang Gate of Northern Wei Luoyang was Han's "Yong Gate"; Mouzi lihuo lun says, "At the time a Buddhist temple was raised outside Yong Gate west of Luoyang city."

sentences.zh: 這裏「關」乃「門」之訛，今改正。

translations.literal: Here 'pass' is a corruption of 'gate'; it is corrected.
translations.idiomatic: Here "pass" is a corruption of "gate"; it is corrected.

sentences.zh: 澡練神明 諸本「澡」作「藻」，御覽卷六五三

translations.literal: Bathing and refining the spirit: various editions read 'the cited text' for 'the cited text'; Imperial Readings juan 653
translations.idiomatic: Bathing and refining the spirit: various editions read "the cited text" for "the cited text"; Imperial Readings, juan 653

sentences.zh: 〈二九一七頁〉、
廣弘明集卷二引志作「澡」。

translations.literal: and Guang hongming ji juan 2's citation of the Treatise read 'the cited text.'
translations.idiomatic: and Guang hongming ji, juan 2, citation of the Treatise read "the cited text."

sentences.zh: 按下文敍道教也說「澡雪精神」，這裏「藻」字訛，今據改。

translations.literal: According to the passage below, Daoism also speaks of 'bathing and purifying the spirit'; here 'the cited text' is corrupt; it is amended accordingly.
translations.idiomatic: According to the passage below, Daoism also speaks of "bathing and purifying the spirit"; here "the cited text" is corrupt; it is amended accordingly.

sentences.zh: 婦入道者曰比丘尼 百衲、南、汲、局四本「入」作「人」，北本、殿本作「入」。

translations.literal: Women who enter the Way are called bhikṣuṇīs: the Bai na, Nan, Ji, and Ju editions read 'the cited text' for 'the cited text'; the Bei and Dian editions read 'the cited text.'
translations.idiomatic: Women who enter the Way are called bhikṣuṇīs: the Bai na, Nan, Ji, and Ju editions read "the cited text" for "the cited text"; the Bei and Dian editions read "the cited text."

sentences.zh: 疑當作「婦人入道者」，舊本脫「入」字，北本改「人」為「入」。

translations.literal: It is suspected it should read 'women who enter the Way'; the old edition dropped 'the cited text,' and the Bei edition changed 'the cited text' to 'the cited text.'
translations.idiomatic: It is suspected it should read "women who enter the Way"; the old edition dropped "the cited text," and the Bei edition changed "the cited text" to "the cited text."

sentences.zh: 今姑從北、殿本。

translations.literal: For now the Bei and Dian editions are followed.
translations.idiomatic: For now the Bei and Dian editions are followed.

sentences.zh: 皆以□為本 百衲本空格作墨釘，北、汲、殿三本注「闕」，南本、局本作「五戒」。

translations.literal: All take □ as the root: the Bai na edition's blank space is a black dot; the Bei, Ji, and Dian editions note 'missing'; the Nan and Ju editions read 'five precepts.'
translations.idiomatic: All take □ as the root: the Bai na edition's blank space is a black dot; the Bei, Ji, and Dian editions note "missing"; the Nan and Ju editions read "five precepts."

sentences.zh: 按南本當是以意補，今作空格。

translations.literal: The Nan edition appears to supply by conjecture; a blank space is used here.
translations.idiomatic: The Nan edition appears to supply by conjecture; a blank space is used here.

sentences.zh: 凡人修行粗為極 按語不可解，疑有訛脫，今於「極」字句斷。

translations.literal: When ordinary people cultivate, roughly as the utmost: the phrase is unintelligible; corruption or omission is suspected; a break is made after 'utmost.'
translations.idiomatic: When ordinary people cultivate, roughly as the utmost: the phrase is unintelligible; corruption or omission is suspected; a break is made after "utmost."

sentences.zh: 其根業各差 諸本「各」作「太」，廣弘明集卷二作「各」。

translations.literal: Their root-karma each differs: various editions read 'the cited text' for 'the cited text'; Guang hongming ji juan 2 reads 'the cited text.'
translations.idiomatic: Their root-karma each differs: various editions read "the cited text" for "the cited text"; Guang hongming ji, juan 2, reads "the cited text."

sentences.zh: 按上云「有三種人」，作「各」是，今據改。

translations.literal: According to the passage above, 'there are three kinds of people,' reading 'the cited text' is correct; it is amended accordingly.
translations.idiomatic: According to the passage above, "there are three kinds of people," reading "the cited text" is correct; it is amended accordingly.

sentences.zh: 彌歷長遠 諸本無「歷」字，廣弘明集卷二有。

translations.literal: Extending through long ages: various editions lack 'the cited text'; Guang hongming ji juan 2 has it.
translations.idiomatic: Extending through long ages: various editions lack "the cited text"; Guang hongming ji, juan 2, has it.

sentences.zh: 按文義當有此字，今據補。

translations.literal: According to the sense, this character should be present; it is supplied accordingly.
translations.idiomatic: According to the sense, this character should be present; it is supplied accordingly.

sentences.zh: 文言將來有彌勒佛 按「文」疑當作「又」。

translations.literal: The text says that in the future there will be the Buddha Maitreya: 'the cited text' is suspected to be 'the cited text.'
translations.idiomatic: The text says that in the future there will be the Buddha Maitreya: "the cited text" is suspected to be "the cited text."

sentences.zh: 役諸鬼神 諸本「役」作「於」，廣弘明集卷二作「役」。

translations.literal: Employing spirits and demons: various editions read 'the cited text' for 'the cited text'; Guang hongming ji juan 2 reads 'the cited text.'
translations.idiomatic: Employing spirits and demons: various editions read "the cited text" for "the cited text"; Guang hongming ji, juan 2, reads "the cited text."

sentences.zh: 按阿育王役鬼神，一日一夜造八萬四千塔的神話屢見佛教紀載。

translations.literal: According to the myth, repeated in Buddhist records, that King Aśoka employed spirits and demons to build eighty-four thousand stūpas in one day and one night.
translations.idiomatic: According to the myth, repeated in Buddhist records, that King Aśoka employed spirits and demons to build eighty-four thousand stūpas in one day and one night.

sentences.zh: 「於」乃「役」之訛，今據改。

translations.literal: 'the cited text' is a corruption of 'the cited text'; it is amended accordingly.
translations.idiomatic: "the cited text" is a corruption of "the cited text"; it is amended accordingly.

sentences.zh: 今洛陽彭城姑臧臨淄皆有阿育王寺 諸本「淄」作「渭」，廣弘明集卷二作「淄」。

translations.literal: Now Luoyang, Pengcheng, Guzang, and Linzi all have Aśoka temples: various editions read 'the cited text' for 'the cited text'; Guang hongming ji juan 2 reads 'the cited text.'
translations.idiomatic: Now Luoyang, Pengcheng, Guzang, and Linzi all have Aśoka temples: various editions read "the cited text" for "the cited text"; Guang hongming ji, juan 2, reads "the cited text."

sentences.zh: 按廣弘明集卷一五列塔像神瑞迹列舉所謂阿育王塔無「臨渭」而有「臨淄」，云「青州臨淄城中有阿育王寺，其形象露盤在深林巨樹下。」

translations.literal: According to Guang hongming ji juan 15's list of stūpa-image miracles, the so-called Aśoka stūpas have no 'Linwei' but do have 'Linzi,' saying: 'In Linzi city of Qing Province there is an Aśoka temple; its image and dew-dish stand beneath deep forest and great trees.'
translations.idiomatic: According to Guang hongming ji, juan 15, list of stūpa-image miracles, the so-called Aśoka stūpas have no "Linwei" but do have "Linzi," saying, "In Linzi city of Qing Province there is an Aśoka temple; its image and dew-dish stand beneath deep forest and great trees."

sentences.zh: 語出高僧傳卷一０竺佛圖澄傳。

translations.literal: The words come from Gaoseng zhuan juan 10, biography of the monk Fotudeng.
translations.idiomatic: The words come from Gaoseng zhuan, juan 10, biography of the monk Fotudeng.

sentences.zh: 這裏「渭」字乃「淄」形近而訛，今據改。

translations.literal: Here 'the cited text' is a corruption through graphic similarity to 'the cited text'; it is amended accordingly.
translations.idiomatic: Here "the cited text" is a corruption through graphic similarity to "the cited text"; it is amended accordingly.

sentences.zh: 遂徙於道東 百衲本「東」字空格，諸本注「闕」字。

translations.literal: Thereupon moved east of the road: the Bai na edition has a blank space for 'the cited text'; various editions note 'missing.'
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon moved east of the road: the Bai na edition has a blank space for "the cited text"; various editions note "missing."

sentences.zh: 按法苑珠林卷五三舍利篇敍此云：「乃於道東造周閭百間」，知此志所脫是「東」字，今據補。

translations.literal: According to Fayuan zhulin juan 53, Relics section, which narrates this: 'Thereupon east of the road they built a hundred rooms of Zhou pavilions'-knowing that this Treatise dropped 'the cited text,' it is supplied accordingly.
translations.idiomatic: According to Fayuan zhulin, juan 53, Relics section, which narrates this: "Thereupon east of the road they built a hundred rooms of Zhou pavilions"-knowing that this Treatise dropped "the cited text," it is supplied accordingly.

sentences.zh: 「閣」「閭」皆可通。

translations.literal: 'the cited text' and 'the cited text' are both acceptable.
translations.idiomatic: "the cited text" and "the cited text" are both acceptable.

sentences.zh: 文帝久在洛陽 諸本「久」作「又」，冊府卷五一

translations.literal: Emperor Wen long in Luoyang: various editions read 'the cited text' for 'the cited text'; Cefu juan 51
